topics.scope: The reported phase comparison motivates model correction. Specify and validate the thermal dynamics and load boundary conditions required for closed-loop operation; optimizing a single phase on a response map is not the full project.

control.state: Hot and cold thermal states, acoustic response and observed cooling load.
control.action: Schedule both source amplitudes and their relative phase through a cooling transient.
control.dynamics: Retained thermal inertia couples successive drive choices; a steady phase-response map supplies only part of the model.
control.objective: Track cooling demand with minimum acoustic energy within temperature and drive limits over the transient.

topics.title: Elastocaloric regenerator cycle
topics.problem: Elastocaloric regenerator: time the loading, unloading and fluid flow to maximize cooling per unit of work under a fatigue-limiting strain bound
topics.hook: The Ljubljana NiTi regenerator reached a 31.3 K span and over 60 W (4,400 W/kg at a 10 K span). The 1D model, validated against experiments and written in MATLAB, uses step flow and instantaneous loading, so shaping the cycle is left open.
topics.start: [Ahčin et al. 2022, numerical modeling of a shell-and-tube-like elastocaloric regenerator, Energies](https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/15/23/9253); [Ahčin et al. 2022, fatigue-resistant elastocaloric cooling and heat pumping in compression, Joule (lab page)](https://lahde.fs.uni-lj.si/en/high-performance-cooling-and-heat-pumping-based-on-fatigue-resistant-elastocaloric-effect-in-compression/); [Qian et al. 2023, multimode elastocaloric cooling system, Science (summary)](https://ceee.umd.edu/news/story/elastocaloric-cooling-system-codeveloped-by-ceee-faculty-featured-innbspscience); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: fixed Brayton-like cycle with step on/off flow at a swept frequency
topics.angle: periodic trajectory optimization of the strain and flow waveforms on the 1D model, amortized into a policy over span and load; optionally learn when to switch between regeneration and maximum-utilization modes as in the Maryland device

control.state: Regenerator temperature profile, material loading phase and fluid thermal state.
control.action: Choose strain-loading and unloading timing and fluid-flow waveforms during each cycle.
control.dynamics: Loading changes material temperature; fluid flow moves heat and sets the initial profile for subsequent cycles.
control.objective: Maximize useful cooling relative to work while respecting strain, flow and fatigue-related operating limits.

topics.title: Magnetocaloric heat pump seasonal operation
topics.problem: Magnetocaloric heat pump for a house: choose cycle frequency, fluid flow rate and the number of active regenerators each hour to meet heating demand at the highest seasonal COP
topics.hook: The open Python model takes flow and field profiles over the cycle as inputs. The paper reaches a seasonal COP of 5.6 by adjusting flow and frequency and switching regenerator groups, and estimates about 69 regenerators for peak demand, which leaves room to test a predictive policy against it.
topics.start: [Pineda Quijano et al. 2024, seasonal COP of a residential magnetocaloric heat pump based on MnFePSi, Int. J. Refrig.](https://iifiir.org/en/fridoc/seasonal-cop-of-a-residential-magnetocaloric-heat-pump-based-on-mnfepsi-148745); [Pineda Quijano et al. 2023, layering strategies for AMRs, Appl. Therm. Eng. (open access)](https://research.tudelft.nl/en/publications/layering-strategies-for-active-magnetocaloric-regenerators-using-); [code: FAME_AMR_model, Python 1D AMR](https://github.com/diego-pineda/FAME_AMR_model); [data and code, 4TU](https://data.4tu.nl/datasets/cd51b1e3-ab4a-4e6c-a668-f53da25475d4)
topics.baseline: the paper's strategy: set flow and frequency from steady-state maps and switch regenerator groups on and off to match demand
topics.angle: train a fast surrogate of the 1D AMR model, couple it to a declared building thermal model, then use MPC or DP over hourly demand. Carry building temperature and relevant regenerator states forward; compare seasonal electricity at equal comfort against the steady-map strategy
topics.scope: Reproduce the regenerator model first. Document the building model and retained cycle-state assumptions; independently selecting the best COP each hour omits the intertemporal control problem.

control.state: Building and regenerator thermal states, operating mode and forecast heat demand.
control.action: Set cycle frequency, fluid flow and active regenerator groups at each interval.
control.dynamics: Thermal storage and building heat losses couple operating choices across time; static COP maps omit that memory.
control.objective: Serve seasonal heating demand with minimum electricity within comfort, flow and equipment limits.

topics.title: Adsorption chiller cycle timing
topics.problem: Two-bed adsorption chiller on solar or waste heat: choose the adsorption, desorption and mass-recovery phase durations as source and ambient temperatures drift, to trade cooling power against COP
topics.hook: On a validated Modelica model of a test bed, cutting the cycle from 1860 s to about 393 s raised volumetric cooling power from 29 to 42 kW/m3 for silica gel but lowered COP substantially, so the best timing depends on what the heat source can supply.
topics.start: [RWTH (Bardow group) 2015, optimal design of adsorption chillers based on a validated dynamic object-oriented model, Sci. Technol. Built Environ. (open manuscript)](https://publications.rwth-aachen.de/record/466219/files/466219.pdf); [Gräber et al. 2011, optimal cyclic operation of two-bed adsorption chillers with mass recovery](https://iifiir.org/en/fridoc/optimal-cyclic-operation-of-two-bed-adsorption-chillers-with-mass-27649); [Daborer-Prado and Resch 2021, lumped two-bed silica gel/water chiller model](https://pure.fh-ooe.at/en/publications/preliminary-results-on-experimental-modelling-of-an-adsorption-ch/); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: fixed cycle time tuned offline at nominal temperatures
topics.angle: periodic optimal control by multiple shooting, amortized into a feedback policy of heat-source and ambient temperature; compare with MPC over a varying heat source

control.state: Adsorbent loading, bed and heat-exchanger temperatures and current cycle phase.
control.action: Choose when to switch adsorption and regeneration phases and their durations.
control.dynamics: Each phase changes bed temperature and remaining adsorption capacity, affecting output in later phases.
control.objective: Meet cooling demand with low heat and pumping input while respecting temperature and phase-switching constraints.

topics.title: Absorption heat pump part-load control
topics.problem: LiBr/H2O absorption heat pump or chiller: modulate the driving heat and the internal and external flows to track output temperature over a wide part-load range
topics.hook: Absorption devices run on heat instead of electricity, but Staudt et al. note that poor control limits their modulation and part-load range. They provide a validated control-oriented model and a linearized state-space version intended for MPC.
topics.start: [Staudt et al. 2023, control-oriented modeling of a LiBr/H2O absorption heat pumping device with experimental validation, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.15097); [code: Absolut Modelica library for absorption cycles](https://github.com/carlesRT/Absolut)
topics.baseline: conventional PI control of output temperature
topics.angle: linear or nonlinear MPC on the validated DAE model, with a learned residual fitted on Modelica runs

control.state: Solution and heat-exchanger thermal states, flow measurements and source and sink conditions.
control.action: Adjust driving heat and controllable flow rates as the heating load changes.
control.dynamics: Fluid inventories and heat-exchanger inertia delay output changes and influence later operating efficiency.
control.objective: Track useful heat demand with minimum driving energy within temperature, flow and equipment limits.

topics.title: Variable-geometry ejector chiller
topics.problem: Control spindle position during changing cooling load and condenser conditions, retaining generator thermal inertia and actuator limits to meet cooling demand efficiently without leaving critical operation.
topics.hook: Changing spindle position trades entrainment against the critical-pressure margin. The control project asks how to manage that trade-off through a load transient when generator temperature and spindle position cannot change instantly.
topics.start: [Besagni and Inzoli 2022, influence of variable geometry control on an R290 ejector refrigeration system, J. Phys. Conf. Ser.](https://re.public.polimi.it/retrieve/e0c31c12-dbfe-4599-e053-1705fe0aef77/Besagni_2022_J._Phys.__Conf._Ser._2177_012010.pdf); [code: simpy_ejector, 1D ejector simulator (CoolProp)](https://github.com/AdamBuruzs/simpy_ejector); cycle model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: fixed-geometry ejector, or the spindle look-up table the authors propose
topics.angle: combine the steady ejector response with a justified lumped generator thermal model and spindle-rate limits. Use MPC or amortize its policy, and compare energy, cooling shortfall and critical-mode violations over complete load transients
topics.scope: simpy_ejector supplies a steady ejector model. The dynamic cycle and actuator extension must be specified and checked; a temperature-to-optimal-spindle lookup alone is the myopic baseline.

control.state: Generator thermal state, condenser conditions, cooling demand and previous spindle position.
control.action: Move the spindle at successive control intervals with feasible motion rates.
control.dynamics: Generator thermal inertia and spindle motion limits couple successive settings; the steady ejector map supplies instantaneous performance.
control.objective: Meet cooling demand efficiently over a load transient while respecting critical-mode and actuator constraints.

topics.title: 150 °C steam heat pump start-up and turndown
topics.problem: Cascade heat pump making 150 °C steam from an ambient source: coordinate compressor speeds and expansion-valve superheat setpoints through cold start and load changes, avoiding liquid at compressor inlets and staying inside compressor maps
topics.hook: Steam heat pumps like this cascade prototype (R1233zd(E) over R513a) are meant to replace fossil steam boilers. The thesis shows that the plain PID scheme needs an ad hoc superheat change during turndown to keep liquid out of the compressors.
topics.start: [Ryan 2024, transient modeling of an ambient-source centrifugal-compressor steam-generating heat pump, Colorado State MS thesis](https://mountainscholar.org/items/81dbe058-fd5b-499b-b3ee-e9454baa2c59/full); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: PID loops with a fixed LP/HP compressor speed ratio and a temporary 15 K superheat setpoint during turndown
topics.angle: constrained MPC on a reduced cascade model that coordinates the three compressors and both valves, with a learned surrogate for the heat exchangers

control.state: Temperatures, pressures, refrigerant phase conditions and compressor operating states.
control.action: Choose compressor speeds and valve settings during start-up and load changes.
control.dynamics: Thermal inventories and refrigerant transport govern pressure and superheat trajectories through later stages.
control.objective: Reach and track steam demand while limiting electricity, pressure, temperature and compressor-map violations.

topics.title: Electrified milk evaporator (MVR)
topics.problem: Falling-film milk evaporator with mechanical vapor recompression: set the compression ratio and feed temperature over time to reach the target dry-mass content at the least electricity cost
topics.hook: MVR is a heat pump that replaces process steam with electricity. In this model, dynamic optimization cut the annual electricity cost by about 30% for a 35% dry-mass product, and the authors find the case for MVR is sensitive to the electricity price.
topics.start: [Tsochatzidi, Arvanitidis, Georgiadis 2024, model-based optimization of energy consumption in milk evaporators, Processes](https://mdpi-res.com/d_attachment/processes/processes-12-00209/article_deploy/processes-12-00209.pdf); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: steady operation at a fixed compression ratio and feed temperature (the paper's non-optimized case)
topics.angle: economic MPC on the evaporator model with time-varying electricity prices and dry-mass constraints, then amortize the dynamic optimization into a policy

control.state: Evaporator temperature, liquid hold-up, dry-matter concentration and compressor state.
control.action: Adjust vapor-compression ratio and feed conditions during evaporation.
control.dynamics: Water removal concentrates the retained liquid; heat and mass inventories determine subsequent evaporation requirements.
control.objective: Meet final dry-matter and throughput targets with minimum electricity within pressure and temperature limits.

topics.title: Vapor-compression superheat benchmark
topics.problem: Single-stage vapor-compression chiller: move compressor speed and expansion-valve opening to track the brine outlet temperature and evaporator superheat under inlet-temperature disturbances
topics.hook: The Simulink benchmark comes with fixed 20-minute test scenarios, input constraints and a combined score, so a student can compare a learned or predictive controller with tuned PID in a week. Its refrigerant is R404a, which makes moving the model to a low-GWP refrigerant a natural extension.
topics.start: [Bejarano et al. 2018, benchmark for PID control of refrigeration systems based on vapour compression, IFAC PID'18](https://skoge.folk.ntnu.no/prost/proceedings/PID-2018/0043.PDF); [code: MATLAB/Simulink benchmark files](https://www.dia.uned.es/~fmorilla/benchmarkPID2018/)
topics.baseline: the benchmark's default decentralised PID controller
topics.angle: linear or nonlinear MPC, or an RL policy trained in the simulator, scored with the benchmark's combined index J; extension: rebuild the moving-boundary model for propane or CO2

control.state: Evaporator and condenser pressure and temperature states, superheat and measured brine conditions.
control.action: Set compressor speed and expansion-valve opening at each benchmark control step.
control.dynamics: Refrigerant and thermal dynamics couple superheat regulation to later brine-temperature and pressure responses.
control.objective: Track prescribed temperature and superheat references with low control effort while respecting operating bounds.

topics.title: Field heat pumps: weather-curve tuning
topics.problem: Installed air-source heat pumps: choose each home's weather-compensation curve (slope and offset) from its own monitoring data to maximize seasonal performance without losing comfort or causing short cycling
topics.hook: OpenEnergyMonitor's analysis of the EoH trial finds a mean SPF H4 of 2.81 across 428 air-source units, against 3.86 for 170 HeatpumpMonitor systems, and links much of the gap to weather-compensation curves set too high.
topics.start: [Electrification of Heat heat pump performance cleansed data 2020-2023, UK Data Service SN 9050 (open, OGL)](https://b2find.eudat.eu/dataset/21e967cf-72a2-5344-b412-3e8e14cc1afb); [OpenEnergyMonitor analysis of the EoH trial data](https://docs.openenergymonitor.org/heatpumpmonitor/eoh.html); [worked examples of curves set too high](https://docs.openenergymonitor.org/heatpumpmonitor/commissioning.html); model learned from the data
topics.baseline: the installer's or factory-default weather-compensation curve
topics.angle: identify a per-home thermal and cycling model, then optimize weather-curve parameters as a feedback policy evaluated over simulated seasons. Compare prediction-trained and decision-trained models through electricity, comfort and cycling outcomes on unseen weather
topics.venture: Heat-pump installers, utilities and efficiency programs, which pay to make installed heat pumps run more efficiently without a site visit.
topics.scope: A fixed curve parameterizes repeated control actions, so evaluate its closed-loop thermal trajectory. Monitoring data must support the modeled interventions; replaying recorded consumption under an unobserved curve does not estimate its savings.

control.state: Estimated building and tank temperatures, cycling history and outdoor weather, inferred from monitoring data.
control.action: Choose a weather-compensation curve whose repeated setpoints drive the heat pump through the season.
control.dynamics: Building thermal inertia and cycling carry across intervals, so a curve must be evaluated through full closed-loop trajectories.
control.objective: Minimize seasonal electricity while maintaining indoor comfort and feasible cycling and supply-temperature limits.

topics.title: Heat pump inspections: adaptive visit allocation
topics.problem: Allocate a limited sequence of heat-pump inspection and follow-up visits, learning from revealed faults to choose later households and maximize modeled electricity savings over the campaign.
topics.hook: HEAPO combines smart-meter data from 1,408 households with 410 inspection reports. It can inform a visit-allocation model in which each inspection reveals faults, spends capacity and changes where the next visit is most useful.
topics.start: [Brudermueller et al. 2025, HEAPO open dataset for heat pump optimization, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16993); [data, Zenodo (CC BY 4.0)](https://zenodo.org/records/15056919); [code: Python data loader](https://github.com/tbrumue/heapo)
topics.baseline: Uniform visit allocation and greedy expected-savings ranking under the same visit budget and information
topics.angle: learn fault beliefs from meter and inspection data, then plan adaptive visits with a finite-budget belief-state model. Compare with greedy allocation in a declared intervention simulator; test sensitivity to uncertain savings and selection bias
topics.scope: Inspection reports and before-and-after consumption do not automatically identify causal savings or support off-policy evaluation. State an intervention-response model and its assumptions, or justify identification and action support before estimating counterfactual visit-policy value.

control.state: Household features, inspection history, remaining visit budget and beliefs about faults and intervention effects.
control.action: Choose the next households to inspect and when to follow up during a campaign.
control.dynamics: Visits consume capacity and reveal faults; outcomes update beliefs used to select later visits.
control.objective: Maximize cumulative modeled electricity savings under visit and coverage constraints, accounting for effect-estimation uncertainty.

topics.title: Boreal forest management
topics.problem: Boreal forest management: carbon storage vs permafrost thaw over 50 years
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Boreal forests hold huge carbon stocks above permafrost. Thinning and species choices trade carbon today against thaw tomorrow.
topics.start: [BoreaRL, Dsouza et al., ICLR 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19846); [code](https://github.com/kevinbdsouza/BoreaRL)
topics.baseline: No management or a fixed thinning rule
topics.angle: DP or model-based RL with a learned surrogate of the physics simulator

control.state: Stand age, biomass and soil-carbon state, with uncertain growth and disturbance conditions.
control.action: Choose thinning, harvest or continued growth at each management period.
control.dynamics: Harvest changes stand structure and carbon stocks; regrowth and soil processes affect returns decades later.
control.objective: Balance timber returns and long-term carbon storage within regeneration and ecological constraints.

topics.title: Peatland water tables
topics.problem: Peatland water-table control for greenhouse-gas mitigation
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Drained peat releases its carbon as it dries out; keeping it wet stops much of that. A Nature paper gives the emission curve to control against.
topics.start: [Evans et al. 2021, water table control on peatland emissions, Nature](https://nora.nerc.ac.uk/id/eprint/530414/); [Mahmoodi et al. 2026, HESS](https://hess.copernicus.org/articles/30/6019/2026/hess-30-6019-2026.html) with field data
topics.baseline: Fixed weir setting
topics.angle: learned hydrology + MPC with rainfall forecasts; the emission relation is an annual mean, treat it with care

control.state: Water-table depth and soil-water storage, observed with weather and drainage conditions.
control.action: Adjust weirs or pumping at successive water-management intervals.
control.dynamics: Rain, drainage and evapotranspiration alter stored water; present levels affect later drying and inundation.
control.objective: Maintain water-table targets associated with lower emissions while meeting land-use and feasible water-level constraints.

topics.title: Rice paddy wetting and drying
topics.problem: Rice paddy alternate wetting and drying for methane
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Flooded rice fields emit methane. Letting them dry at the right moments cuts it without hurting yield.
topics.start: [Oo et al. 2020, DNDC-Rice validation under irrigation practices, Agriculture](https://ideas.repec.org/a/gam/jagris/v10y2020i8p355-d398813.html); [DNDC model](https://www.dndc.sr.unh.edu/)
topics.baseline: Continuous flooding or threshold AWD
topics.angle: DP or RL on a reduced water-balance and methane model, MPC with rainfall forecast

control.state: Soil-water state, crop stage and modeled methane-related conditions, with weather forecasts.
control.action: Choose irrigation and drainage amounts and timing through the growing season.
control.dynamics: Drying and reflooding change water availability, crop development and subsequent methane production.
control.objective: Reduce water use and modeled emissions while preserving yield and avoiding crop water stress.

topics.title: Landfill gas collection
topics.problem: Landfill gas wellfield vacuum control
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Landfills leak methane, a potent greenhouse gas. Tuning the vacuum on each well captures more of it without pulling air into the waste.
topics.start: [Townsend et al. 2005, gas flow model for landfill collection systems, J. Environmental Engineering](https://ascelibrary.com/doi/10.1061/%28ASCE%290733-9372%282005%29131%3A12%281716%29); Darcy-flow model rebuilt
topics.baseline: Monthly manual wellhead tuning
topics.angle: learned well-response model + MPC per well; no public wellhead data
topics.venture: Landfill operators, who pay for more captured methane, which is sold as energy, and fewer emissions violations.

control.state: Well pressures, gas composition and estimated methane generation across connected landfill regions.
control.action: Set well vacuum or extraction rates as measurements arrive.
control.dynamics: Pressure and gas transport couple wells; extraction changes later recoverable gas and air-intrusion risk.
control.objective: Maximize methane capture net of extraction effort while maintaining acceptable oxygen and pressure conditions.

topics.title: Wastewater nitrous oxide
topics.problem: Wastewater N2O mitigation by aeration and recirculation control
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Treatment plants emit nitrous oxide, a strong greenhouse gas, as a by-product of removing nitrogen. Aeration control can cut it.
topics.start: [Santín et al. 2023, N2O reduction by recirculation control, J. Water Process Engineering](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2023/7cb675cdc712/1_s2.0_S2214714423003215_main.pdf); [bsm2-python](https://bsm2-python.readthedocs.io)
topics.baseline: Ammonia cascade PI
topics.angle: MPC or RL on BSM2 with a learned N2O surrogate

control.state: Biological reactor states, oxygen, nitrogen species and estimated N2O production, with influent measurements.
control.action: Adjust aeration and available recirculation settings during treatment.
control.dynamics: Microbial activity and nitrogen transformations respond with delays and affect later effluent and gas emissions.
control.objective: Meet effluent limits while reducing aeration energy and modeled N2O emissions over repeated load cycles.

topics.title: Flow battery control
topics.problem: Vanadium redox flow battery: electrolyte flow-rate control
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Flow batteries store energy in tanks of liquid electrolyte for long durations. Pump too fast and you waste energy; too slow and the cells starve.
topics.start: [Wang et al. 2023, dynamic optimisation of VRFB flow rate, J. Energy Storage](https://research-repository.uwa.edu.au/en/publications/model-based-nonlinear-dynamic-optimisation-for-the-optimal-flow-r/); [Xiong et al. 2023, GRU flow-rate-aware model](https://research.chalmers.se/publication/538370/file/538370_Fulltext.pdf); model rebuilt
topics.baseline: Fixed flow or lookup table
topics.angle: learned dynamics + MPC, open-loop optimal schedule amortized

control.state: State of charge, electrolyte temperatures and concentration imbalance, with current demand measurements.
control.action: Set electrolyte pump flow as the battery charges and discharges.
control.dynamics: Electrolyte transport and stored charge determine future voltage, concentration and pumping requirements.
control.objective: Maximize net delivered energy after pumping losses while respecting concentration, temperature and flow limits.

topics.title: Dynamic line rating
topics.problem: Control multi-period grid redispatch using weather-dependent line limits, retaining conductor thermal inertia so current loading affects later feasible power flows.
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Power lines can carry more current when it is cold and windy. Using that headroom lets more renewable power through without building new lines.
topics.start: [Rabecq et al. 2025, dynamic line ratings in AC OPF](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.10832); [NREL hourly DLR data](https://data.openei.org/submissions/6231); [pandapower](https://github.com/e2nIEE/pandapower)
topics.baseline: Rolling dispatch using static line ratings and the same available forecasts
topics.angle: learn weather or thermal-model predictions for closed-loop dispatch cost, and use MPC with transient conductor temperature. The action is redispatch or curtailment, not the rating forecast; compare renewable energy served, cost and temperature violations
topics.scope: Couple the network solver to a transient conductor heat balance. Hourly rating data and independent OPF solves alone do not supply action-dependent temperature dynamics.

control.state: Conductor temperature, network loading and available flexibility, with uncertain wind and ambient conditions.
control.action: Choose generation redispatch, curtailment or storage dispatch at each grid interval.
control.dynamics: Current heats the conductor; thermal inertia and flexibility commitments determine future permissible loading.
control.objective: Serve demand at minimum operating cost while keeping conductor temperature and network flows within limits.

topics.title: Energy-optimal train driving
topics.problem: Energy-optimal train driving under timetable disturbances
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Pontryagin's principle says how to drive a train: power, cruise, coast, brake. Real timetables and delays turn it into a feedback problem.
topics.start: [Albrecht et al. 2016, key principles of optimal train control, Transportation Research Part B](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/transb/v94y2016icp482-508.html); [Xie et al. 2023, metro energy under disturbances with RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.13443)
topics.baseline: The Pontryagin structure (power, hold, coast, brake)
topics.angle: amortize PMP solutions into a policy, RL under delays; trivial unless disturbances are included

control.state: Train position, speed and timetable deviation, with route grade and speed-limit information.
control.action: Choose traction, coasting or braking along the route.
control.dynamics: Acceleration changes future speed and arrival time; braking and grade alter remaining energy requirements.
control.objective: Minimize journey energy while meeting arrival time, speed limits and feasible traction and braking bounds.

topics.title: Electric bus depot charging
topics.problem: Electric bus depot charging scheduling
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: A bus fleet goes electric only if the depot can charge everyone overnight without a huge grid connection. STM's open timetables give a Montreal instance.
topics.start: [Heide et al. 2025, electric bus fleet deployment, World Electric Vehicle Journal](https://www.mdpi.com/2032-6653/16/7/378); [Qi et al. 2025, hierarchical deep RL for bus charging](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10296); [eflips-depot](https://pypi.org/project/eflips-depot); STM GTFS for a Montreal instance
topics.baseline: Plug-and-charge and the ILP
topics.angle: amortize the ILP, MPC with a rolling schedule, RL under uncertainty
topics.venture: Transit agencies and fleet operators electrifying their buses, who pay for lower charging bills and grid-connection costs.

control.state: Bus state of charge, charger occupancy and scheduled departures and returns.
control.action: Assign chargers and set charging power as vehicles arrive and forecasts change.
control.dynamics: Charging accumulates energy; departures remove vehicles and create deadlines that compete for later depot capacity.
control.objective: Minimize electricity and peak costs while meeting departure charge requirements and charger and feeder limits.

topics.title: Truck platooning
topics.problem: Heavy-duty truck platooning: look-ahead energy control
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Trucks driving close together cut drag. Looking ahead at the hills lets the platoon coordinate speed and save fuel.
topics.start: [Ard et al. 2022, cooperative MPC for truck platooning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.02119); [Besselink et al. 2015, cyber-physical control of road freight](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.03466)
topics.baseline: Cruise control and CACC
topics.angle: look-ahead MPC over road grade, learned fuel map, policy distilled from MPC

control.state: Truck speeds, intervehicle gaps and route position, with grade and lead-vehicle information.
control.action: Set longitudinal acceleration or speed commands for each truck.
control.dynamics: Acceleration propagates through vehicle motion and platoon gaps, changing later drag savings and safety margins.
control.objective: Reduce total fuel while meeting travel-time requirements and headway, acceleration and speed constraints.

topics.title: Storm-surge barrier closure
topics.problem: Storm-surge barrier closure as optimal stopping (Maeslant, MOSE)
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Closing a surge barrier stops a flood but halts shipping. The call has to be made on forecasts that are wrong in known ways.
topics.start: [Trace-Kleeberg et al. 2025, Coastal Engineering](https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/502090) (16 years of forecasts vs gauge); [Umgiesser et al. 2021, floods in Venice, NHESS](https://nhess.copernicus.org/articles/21/2679/2021/)
topics.baseline: Threshold rule on the forecast
topics.angle: POMDP or optimal stopping with a learned forecast-error model; false closures vs misses

control.state: Sea and river levels, barrier mode and an evolving forecast distribution for surge.
control.action: Wait, initiate closure or reopen when conditions permit.
control.dynamics: Closure takes time and changes subsequent flood exposure and navigation access; waiting preserves information but reduces response time.
control.objective: Balance flood losses and closure costs while satisfying barrier timing and operating constraints.

topics.title: Forecast-informed dam releases
topics.problem: Forecast-informed emergency dam pre-releases
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Release water before a big storm to make room for the flood, but release too much and the reservoir runs short. Ensemble forecasts make it a decision under uncertainty.
topics.start: [Brodeur et al. 2024, synthetic forecast ensembles for forecast-informed reservoir operations, Water Resources Research](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10530480)
topics.baseline: Ensemble forecast operations rule with a risk curve
topics.angle: policy over ensemble statistics, decision-focused forecast calibration

control.state: Reservoir storage, downstream conditions and updated inflow-forecast ensembles.
control.action: Choose releases at successive forecast updates before and during storms.
control.dynamics: Releases create storage space but reduce water available after the storm; routing delays affect downstream peaks.
control.objective: Limit flood damage while preserving water supply within reservoir and downstream release constraints.

topics.title: Drought restrictions
topics.problem: Drought restriction policies for urban water supply
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: When should a city ask people to cut water use, and by how much? A stochastic DP question that droughts make urgent.
topics.start: [Eum et al. 2011, sampling stochastic DP with a hedging rule, J. Water Resources Planning and Management](https://ascelibrary.com/doi/10.1061/%28ASCE%29WR.1943-5452.0000095); [Macian-Sorribes et al. 2015, HESS](https://hess.copernicus.org/articles/19/3925/2015/hess-19-3925-2015-metrics.html)
topics.baseline: Fixed trigger rule curves
topics.angle: sampling SDP, policy search over thresholds, learned inflow model

control.state: Reservoir storage, demand trends and estimated response to existing restrictions.
control.action: Choose the restriction stage at each drought-management review.
control.dynamics: Consumption depletes storage; restrictions change future demand, with persistence and delayed public response.
control.objective: Reduce shortage risk and restriction costs over the drought within storage and essential-supply requirements.

topics.title: Nonlinear 20-story seismic benchmark
topics.problem: Choose active actuator forces or semi-active damper commands at each control step from noisy floor accelerations to reduce inter-story drift and floor accelerations of a 20-story steel frame that yields under strong earthquakes, within the benchmark's device and sensor constraints.
topics.hook: This is the structural control community's standard yardstick, with a fixed nonlinear evaluation model and fixed criteria, so a learned controller is compared with decades of published designs. On a smaller five-story benchmark a model-free RL controller reported about 25% more drift reduction than LQG; testing whether that holds on the yielding 20-story frame is a clean project.
topics.start: [Ohtori, Christenson, Spencer and Dyke, third-generation benchmark control problems for seismically excited nonlinear buildings (3-, 9- and 20-story SAC frames), benchmark definition page](https://sstl.cee.illinois.edu/benchmarks/bench3def/); [NEES database of structural control benchmark problems, MATLAB data and simulation files](https://datacenterhub.org/resources/257); [Spencer 2004, editorial on the benchmark special issue, J. Eng. Mech.](https://ascelibrary.com/doi/10.1061/%28ASCE%290733-9399%282004%29130%3A4%28363%29); [Eshkevari et al. 2021, RL-Controller for active structural control, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.07616)
topics.baseline: the benchmark's sample LQG active controller, plus the uncontrolled frame
topics.angle: RL or learned-model MPC that uses the nonlinear (yielding) evaluation model; amortize the MPC into an output-feedback network and test across records and intensities

control.state: Estimated floor displacement and velocity, yielding state and actuator state from noisy measurements.
control.action: Apply actuator or controllable-damper commands at each simulation step.
control.dynamics: Building motion and nonlinear yielding propagate earthquake forces and past control inputs into later response.
control.objective: Reduce drift and acceleration during earthquakes within actuator-force, stroke and model operating limits.

topics.title: Wind-excited 76-story tower with ATMD
topics.problem: Choose the active tuned mass damper force on top of a 76-story, 306 m tower from a few floor accelerations to cut wind-induced floor accelerations under wind-tunnel loads, with force within ±118 kN, stroke within 95 cm, and building stiffness uncertain by ±15%.
topics.hook: The building, the wind-tunnel loads and both an LQG and a hard-constrained MPC (±118 kN, 95 cm stroke) are published, so the project is about beating a known controller rather than building a model. The open question is whether a cheap explicit policy keeps the MPC's constraint handling when stiffness is off by 15%.
topics.start: [Mei, Kareem and Kantor 2004, model predictive control of wind-excited building: benchmark study, J. Eng. Mech.](https://nathaz.nd.edu/journals/%282004%29ModelPredictiveControlofWind-ExcitedBuilding.pdf); [Yang, Lin and Jabbari 2004, multiobjective controllers on the same benchmark vs LQG, J. Eng. Mech.](https://ascelibrary.com/doi/10.1061/%28ASCE%290733-9399%282004%29130%3A4%28471%29); [benchmark index, wind-excited 76-story building with MATLAB models](https://sstl.cee.illinois.edu/benchmarks/); [NEES structural control benchmark files](https://datacenterhub.org/resources/257); [wind tunnel data, NEES-2014-1241](https://datacenterhub.org/landingpages/519/519_LandingPage.html)
topics.baseline: the benchmark LQG sample controller and the constrained MPC of Mei et al. (2004)
topics.angle: amortize the constrained MPC into an explicit policy, or train a policy robust to the stiffness range by domain randomization

control.state: Estimated tower motion and tuned-mass-damper position and velocity under wind excitation.
control.action: Command active damper force at each feedback step.
control.dynamics: Tower and damper inertia couple current force to future sway and available damper stroke.
control.objective: Reduce occupant acceleration while keeping damper force and travel within benchmark limits.

topics.title: Bridge deck maintenance from NBI ratings
topics.problem: Each year, choose do-nothing, maintain, repair or replace for every deck in a bridge network from noisy condition ratings, to minimize life-cycle cost under an annual budget and a limit on the share of decks in poor condition.
topics.hook: The NBI files give a deck rating for every listed US bridge in each year from 1992 to 2025, so the deterioration model comes from real data. On a Pennsylvania network, a constrained multi-agent DRL policy cost about 32% less than the state DOT's policy and about 6% less than a tuned condition-based policy.
topics.start: [Bhattacharya, Saifullah and Papakonstantinou 2024, DRL-driven life-cycle management of bridge and pavement systems (PennDOT and Hampton Roads networks), IABMAS](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10552119); [Andriotis and Papakonstantinou 2020, DRL inspection and maintenance planning under incomplete information and constraints, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.01380); [FHWA National Bridge Inventory annual ASCII files 1992-2025 (deck item 58, superstructure 59, substructure 60)](https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/nbi/ascii.cfm); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: a condition-based threshold policy tuned on the same model, and the agency's rule-based policy
topics.angle: estimate Markov transitions from NBI deck rating histories; exact constrained DP or POMDP for one deck, multi-agent actor-critic with Lagrangian budget constraints for the network

control.state: Beliefs about deck condition from inspection ratings, maintenance history and remaining annual funds.
control.action: Choose inspection, repair, rehabilitation or replacement for bridges each year.
control.dynamics: Decks deteriorate between inspections; interventions reset condition and consume budgets needed for later work.
control.objective: Minimize lifecycle maintenance and poor-condition costs while respecting budgets and service requirements.

topics.title: Montreal water main renewal
topics.problem: Choose which street segments' water mains to renew each year under a fixed budget, given break histories and segment condition data with uncertain future break rates, to minimize breaks and repair costs over a multi-year horizon.
topics.hook: Montreal publishes the date and location of water-main repairs back to 1972, plus its own A-D intervention class for each street segment, so a local project can test a model against the city's actual plan. In Syracuse, ranking by past breaks already reached a precision of 0.48 on the riskiest 1% of mains, against 0.62 for a boosted-tree model.
topics.start: [Kumar et al. 2018, using machine learning to assess the risk of and prevent water main breaks (Syracuse), arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.03597); [Ville de Montreal, water-main break repairs from 1972 with coordinates, CC-BY 4.0](https://www.donneesquebec.ca/recherche/fr/dataset/vmtl-reparation-reseau-eau-potable); [Ville de Montreal, intervention plan results by street segment, classes A-D, lengths and costs](https://www.donneesquebec.ca/recherche/fr/dataset/0d5fab8e-f673-48fd-96dd-745f50ca1ec0); repair records carry no pipe ID, so join them spatially to segments; model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: rank segments by past break count (the strongest heuristic in Kumar et al.) or follow the city's A-D intervention classes
topics.angle: train a break-risk model for multi-year renewal cost through DP or rolling-horizon planning. Include deterioration and an explicit post-renewal risk reset; compare cumulative breaks and cost against historical-risk ranking using identical annual budgets
topics.venture: Water utilities, which pay to spend a fixed renewal budget on the pipes most likely to break.
topics.scope: Historical break prediction does not identify the effect of renewal. Document the deterioration and renewal-response assumptions and test sensitivity; a single-year knapsack is a static baseline, not the final control task.

control.state: Segment-condition and break-rate beliefs, renewal history and annual budget availability.
control.action: Choose street segments to renew each year using information available at that date.
control.dynamics: Unrenewed pipes deteriorate; renewal resets modeled risk and changes which segments merit later budgets.
control.objective: Minimize cumulative break and renewal costs across years within annual budget and intervention constraints.

topics.title: Fatigue inspection planning, offshore wind
topics.problem: Decide when to inspect and when to repair each fatigue-prone component of an offshore wind support structure or k-out-of-n system, with crack size seen only through imperfect inspections, to minimize inspection, repair and system-failure costs.
topics.hook: An inspection is only worth what it changes in the repair decision, and a POMDP belief policy prices exactly that. Morato et al. found POMDP policies substantially cheaper than the heuristic rules used in risk-based inspection, and the environments run on NumPy alone.
topics.start: [Morato et al. 2022, optimal inspection and maintenance planning for deteriorating structural components through dynamic Bayesian networks and MDPs, Structural Safety (arXiv)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.04547); [Leroy et al. 2023, IMP-MARL, environments for infrastructure management planning, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.11551); [IMP-MARL code: k-out-of-n and offshore wind fatigue environments plus heuristics, Apache-2.0, NumPy only](https://github.com/moratodpg/imp_marl)
topics.baseline: the expert-based heuristic inspection and repair policies shipped with IMP-MARL
topics.angle: exact point-based POMDP on one component, then multi-agent actor-critic on the system; measure the value of information of each inspection

control.state: Beliefs about fatigue-crack size, load history and inspection or repair status.
control.action: Choose when to inspect and whether to repair each component.
control.dynamics: Cracks grow between decisions; imperfect inspections update beliefs and repairs change future failure risk.
control.objective: Minimize inspection, repair and failure costs over asset life within risk and maintenance-budget limits.

topics.title: Post-storm repair crew dispatch
topics.problem: After a storm, assign repair crews to damaged feeder components as outage calls and field reports arrive, to minimize customer interruption time subject to radial precedence, travel times and the number of crews.
topics.hook: On a radial feeder, fixing a downstream line restores nobody until the upstream fault is cleared, which makes this scheduling with precedence. Tan et al. give a 2-approximation rule, a sharp baseline for a policy that must also cope with damage revealed over time.
topics.start: [Tan et al. 2017, scheduling post-disaster repairs in electricity distribution networks, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.08382); [Amani, Ardali and Kargarian 2026, event-driven deep RL dispatcher for post-storm restoration on IEEE 13- and 123-bus feeders, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.10044); [Shuai and Li 2021, AlphaZero-based post-storm repair crew dispatch, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.06764); [IEEE PES distribution test feeders](https://cmte.ieee.org/pes-testfeeders/resources/); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: Tan et al.'s ρ-factor dispatch rule, or their time-indexed ILP re-solved as information arrives
topics.angle: MCTS or actor-critic over the belief state of damage; amortize the re-solved ILP into a fast dispatch policy

control.state: Observed damage, crew locations, ongoing-job completion times and current service restoration.
control.action: Assign each available crew to its next repair job as new damage is reported.
control.dynamics: Travel and repairs occupy crews; completed jobs alter network connectivity and the value of later repairs.
control.objective: Minimize cumulative service interruption while respecting crew skills, travel times and repair dependencies.

topics.title: Post-earthquake water network repairs
topics.problem: After an earthquake, choose the order in which a few crews repair broken pipes, with damage drawn from fragility curves and only partly observed, to maximize the water demand served over the recovery period.
topics.hook: WNTR already models earthquake damage through fragility curves and pressure-dependent demand, so the repair-sequencing environment is a thin wrapper. Klise et al. stress that how bad an earthquake is for water service depends on available resources and repair strategy, not only on the shaking.
topics.start: [Klise et al. 2017, a software framework for assessing the resilience of drinking water systems to disasters with an example earthquake case study, Environ. Model. Softw.](https://www.sandia.gov/research/publications/details/a-software-framework-for-assessing-the-resilience-of-drinking-water-systems-2017-01-01/); [Fan, Zhang and Yu 2022, GCN-DRL model for resilient water distribution network repair decisions, CACAIE](https://researchconnect.buffalo.edu/en/publications/a-graph-convolution-network-deep-reinforcement-learning-model-for/); [WNTR simulator (EPA), pip install wntr](https://github.com/USEPA/WNTR); [WNTR disaster models: earthquake PGA, fragility curves, pipe leaks](https://usepa.github.io/WNTR/disaster_models.html)
topics.baseline: a fixed ranking of damaged pipes by component importance, the conventional rule
topics.angle: rollout or MCTS on WNTR with a learned value function, or a graph-network policy trained by RL; a learned hydraulic surrogate to make planning fast

control.state: Damaged-pipe estimates, network hydraulic state, crew availability and unfinished repairs.
control.action: Choose the next pipe repairs and crew assignments after each completion or assessment.
control.dynamics: Repair restores network paths and pressure; changing connectivity alters unmet demand and subsequent repair priorities.
control.objective: Restore water service quickly under crew, repair-time and hydraulic feasibility constraints.

topics.title: Critical load restoration with DERs
topics.problem: During a post-event outage with the feeder islanded, choose which critical loads to restore and how to dispatch local distributed energy resources over the coming hours under uncertain wind and solar forecasts, to maximize restored load within power-flow and energy limits.
topics.hook: NREL released the environment and the MPC baseline, so the project starts at the control question. Zhang et al. report that RL controllers were less sensitive to renewable forecast errors than the MPCs, a claim worth testing against a properly stochastic MPC.
topics.start: [Zhang et al. 2022, curriculum-based RL for distribution system critical load restoration, IEEE TPWRS (arXiv)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.04166); [Zhang et al. 2021, curriculum-learned controller on the IEEE 13-bus system, IEEE PES GM](https://research-hub.nrel.gov/en/publications/restoring-critical-loads-in-resilient-distribution-systems-using--3/); [NREL hybrid-rl-mpc4clr: gym environment, MPC and RL code, BSD-3, archived 2026](https://github.com/NREL/hybrid-rl-mpc4clr)
topics.baseline: the repo's MPC driven by imperfect renewable forecasts
topics.angle: hybrid RL-MPC where RL sets the reserve the MPC must hold to hedge forecast error; compare with a scenario-based stochastic MPC

control.state: Feeder topology, restored loads, generator availability and storage state of charge.
control.action: Choose load pickup, feasible switching and DER dispatch during restoration.
control.dynamics: Picked-up loads consume future energy; switching and depleted storage change later restoration options.
control.objective: Maximize critical load served over the outage while meeting electrical, fuel and storage constraints.

topics.title: Volt-VAR control
topics.problem: Volt-VAR control of an IEEE distribution feeder: capacitor switching, regulator taps and battery dispatch to hold voltages in band at minimum losses
topics.hook: Rooftop solar pushes voltages out of range on distribution feeders. Capacitors, tap changers and batteries keep them in band.
topics.start: [PowerGym, Fan et al. 2022, L4DC](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v168/fan22a.html); [Gao and Yu 2022, Volt-VAR logs for offline RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.09500); [PowerGym on OpenDSS](https://github.com/siemens/powergym)
topics.baseline: Local droop curves or OPF with the full model
topics.angle: offline RL from the logs, learned voltage-sensitivity model + mixed-integer MPC, or a policy amortized from OPF solutions

control.state: Network voltage estimates, tap and capacitor positions, switching timers and storage charge where modeled.
control.action: Choose tap, capacitor and inverter reactive-power settings at successive intervals.
control.dynamics: Device switching limits and storage or controller states couple responses to later load and solar changes.
control.objective: Reduce losses and voltage deviations while meeting voltage, inverter-capacity and switching-frequency limits.

topics.title: Grid topology control
topics.problem: Grid topology control to relieve line congestion (L2RPN): substation reconfiguration and redispatch
topics.hook: Rewiring substations can relieve congested lines without building new ones. The action space is huge, and that is the challenge.
topics.start: [Marot et al. 2021, L2RPN retrospective](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03104); [Grid2Op](https://grid2op.readthedocs.io/en/latest/)
topics.baseline: Do-nothing and greedy one-step lookahead
topics.angle: tree search or MPC-style lookahead with the simulator as the model, offline RL from expert logs; keep to the 14-bus sandbox

control.state: Grid topology, line flows, previous switching actions and available redispatch.
control.action: Select topology changes and permitted redispatch as load and contingencies evolve.
control.dynamics: Switches persist and impose cooldowns; actions reshape flows and the options available after later disturbances.
control.objective: Maintain secure supply with low congestion and switching cost within network and action-frequency constraints.

topics.title: EV charging and vehicle-to-grid
topics.problem: EV fleet smart charging and vehicle-to-grid at a parking lot under transformer limits
topics.hook: Parked EVs can charge when power is cheap and even give some back. The simulator ships with a perfect-information MPC oracle to measure your gap.
topics.start: [EV2Gym, Orfanoudakis et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01849); [Diaz-Londono et al. 2024, MPC for V2G demand response](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.11963); [ev2gym](https://pypi.org/project/ev2gym/)
topics.baseline: Charge-as-fast-as-possible and the perfect-information MPC oracle
topics.angle: policy amortized from MPC solutions, stochastic MPC with learned arrival and price models, offline RL
topics.venture: Charging operators and fleet owners, who pay to charge more vehicles under a fixed transformer limit and earn grid revenue.

control.state: Vehicle charge levels, charger availability and beliefs about departure times and energy needs.
control.action: Set charging or discharging rates and allocate chargers each interval.
control.dynamics: Energy accumulates or is sold back; departures make present charging decisions irreversible for service delivery.
control.objective: Minimize net energy and degradation cost while meeting departure, battery and grid-power constraints.

topics.title: Battery fast charging
topics.problem: Health-aware fast charging of a lithium-ion cell on an electrochemical model
topics.hook: Charging faster plates lithium and ages the cell. An electrochemical model lets you push right up to that limit.
topics.start: [Park et al. 2020, RL fast charging](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.02060); [Yuan and Zou 2025, lifelong RL for health-aware fast charging](https://web3.arxiv.org/abs/2505.11061); [PyBaMM](https://pybamm.org/)
topics.baseline: CC-CV protocol
topics.angle: NMPC on a reduced single-particle model with a learned residual, or a policy trained on SPMe and tested on DFN; plating potential as a hard constraint
topics.venture: Battery and device makers, who license charging algorithms that charge faster without shortening battery life.

control.state: Estimated state of charge, cell temperature and internal concentration and degradation states.
control.action: Choose charging current repeatedly during a charging session.
control.dynamics: Diffusion and heat accumulation create delayed voltage and plating risks; early current limits later safe charging.
control.objective: Reach target charge quickly while satisfying voltage, temperature, plating-related and degradation constraints.

topics.title: Wind-farm wake steering
topics.problem: Wind-farm wake steering: yaw offsets per turbine for farm-level power
topics.hook: Turning upstream turbines slightly off the wind steers their wakes away from the turbines behind. More energy from the same farm.
topics.start: [WFCRL, Bizon Monroc et al. 2024, NeurIPS D&B](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13592); [WindGym, JOSS 2026](https://www.theoj.org/joss-papers/joss.09946/10.21105.joss.09946.pdf); [wfcrl-env](https://github.com/ifpen/wfcrl-env), [FLORIS](https://github.com/NREL/floris)
topics.baseline: Greedy zero-yaw and the FLORIS static lookup table
topics.angle: learn a transient wake surrogate from FAST.Farm for yaw MPC, or learn a yaw policy and evaluate it with wake propagation and actuator-rate limits. Compare energy and yaw travel over changing wind sequences; static FLORIS lookup is the baseline
topics.venture: Wind-farm owners, who pay for more energy from turbines they already have, delivered as a software upgrade.
topics.scope: Use a dynamic wake environment for final policy comparison. Independent steady-state FLORIS maximizations do not capture wake travel or actuator memory.

control.state: Turbine yaw positions, evolving wake state and estimated wind direction and speed.
control.action: Command turbine yaw changes at successive wind-farm control intervals.
control.dynamics: Yaw actuators move gradually and wake changes travel downstream; static FLORIS evaluations omit these delays.
control.objective: Increase farm energy over time while limiting yaw travel, loads and actuator rates.

topics.title: Grid frequency control
topics.problem: Primary frequency control with inverter-based resources, stability-constrained
topics.hook: Grids with fewer spinning generators need inverters that react within a fraction of a second. Stability guarantees meet learned controllers.
topics.start: [Cui et al. 2021, RL for primary frequency control, a Lyapunov approach](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.05654) with [code](https://github.com/Wenqi-Cui/RNN-RL-Frequency-Lyapunov); [ANDES](https://docs.andes.app/en/stable/)
topics.baseline: Optimized linear droop and LQR on the linearized swing model
topics.angle: structured monotone policy trained by backprop through the dynamics; compare with MPC

control.state: Frequency deviations, phase or swing states and controller internal states from grid measurements.
control.action: Set inverter or other controllable power injections at each feedback step.
control.dynamics: Power imbalance changes rotating or virtual inertia states and propagates through network dynamics.
control.objective: Restore frequency with low control effort while maintaining stability and actuator-power limits.

topics.title: Electrolyzer scheduling
topics.problem: PEM electrolyzer scheduling under variable renewable power with usage-based degradation: when to run, at what load, how much hydrogen to store
topics.hook: Green hydrogen is cheap only if electrolyzers run on cheap renewable power without wearing out. Degradation makes every start count.
topics.start: [Schofield et al. 2024, dynamic optimization of PEM electrolyzers with usage-based degradation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.06766)
topics.baseline: Open-loop MILP with perfect foresight
topics.angle: receding-horizon MPC with learned price and renewable forecasts and a learned degradation model, or a policy amortized from MILP solutions
topics.venture: Green-hydrogen producers, whose margins depend on running on cheap power without wearing out the stack.

control.state: Hydrogen stock, electrolyzer operating mode, thermal or health states and price forecasts.
control.action: Choose start-stop decisions, electrical load and hydrogen-storage flows each scheduling interval.
control.dynamics: Hydrogen inventory, start-up commitments and accumulated wear carry into later demand and price periods.
control.objective: Meet hydrogen demand at minimum electricity and wear cost within storage, ramp and operating limits.

topics.title: Water pump scheduling from logs
topics.problem: Pump scheduling in a real water distribution system from three years of facility logs
topics.hook: Pumping drinking water is a large electricity bill for a city. Three years of real logs from a German facility let you learn from what operators did.
topics.start: [Donâncio et al. 2022, the pump scheduling problem](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.11111) with [code and data](https://gitlab.com/hdonancio/pumpscheduling); [WNTR](https://usepa.github.io/WNTR/)
topics.baseline: Level-hysteresis rules and MILP with a demand forecast
topics.angle: offline RL from operator logs, learned demand model + MPC, exact DP over the tank level as a ceiling
topics.venture: Water utilities, for which pumping is often the largest electricity bill.

control.state: Tank levels, pump modes and time since switching, with estimated network demand.
control.action: Set pump on-off states or speeds on a rolling schedule.
control.dynamics: Pumping fills tanks; demand drains them, and minimum run times restrict later switching.
control.objective: Minimize electricity and switching costs while maintaining tank levels and network-pressure requirements.

topics.title: Lake Como reservoir
topics.problem: Multi-objective reservoir release on Lake Como daily records (1946 to 2010)
topics.hook: Lake Como's water serves farms and hydropower, and floods the town when it rises too far. Decades of daily records come ready to use.
topics.start: [Gym4ReaL, Salaorni et al. 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.00257), [DamEnv](https://daveonwave.github.io/gym4ReaL/dam.html)
topics.baseline: Historical operator releases and stochastic DP
topics.angle: fitted value iteration vs MPC with ensemble inflow forecasts; Pareto front across objectives

control.state: Lake storage or level, season and inflow forecasts updated from observations.
control.action: Choose release each reservoir-management interval.
control.dynamics: Releases reduce stored water and affect future irrigation supply, hydropower and flood-storage capacity.
control.objective: Balance irrigation, hydropower and flood objectives within lake-level and feasible release limits.

topics.title: Wastewater aeration
topics.problem: Aeration (dissolved oxygen) control in an activated-sludge plant (BSM1/BSM2)
topics.hook: Aeration is the largest energy use in a wastewater plant. BSM1 is the benchmark the field itself uses.
topics.start: [Hernández-del-Olmo et al. 2016, Energies](https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/9/9/755); [bsm2-python](https://pypi.org/project/bsm2-python/)
topics.baseline: Default PI loops
topics.angle: learned reduced model + economic MPC, or RL on setpoints with PI underneath, scored with the standard cost and effluent-quality indices
topics.venture: Wastewater treatment plants, where aeration is the largest energy use and effluent limits are strict.

control.state: Estimated activated-sludge states, dissolved oxygen and influent load history.
control.action: Set aeration or dissolved-oxygen references and available recirculation inputs over time.
control.dynamics: Biological populations and substrate inventories evolve slowly, delaying effects on effluent and later oxygen demand.
control.objective: Meet treatment-quality requirements while reducing energy and operating costs within benchmark constraints.

topics.title: Irrigation canal regulation
topics.problem: Water-level regulation of an 11 km canal reach (Saint-Venant PDE)
topics.hook: Irrigation canals lose water when gates are badly operated. The dynamics are a hyperbolic PDE, so building a reduced model is the main event.
topics.start: [Wang and Qi 2026, backstepping-guided RL for canal regulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20089)
topics.baseline: PI on the downstream level and the backstepping law
topics.angle: reduced-order (POD or Koopman) model + MPC; robustness to large deviations; the solver is yours to write

control.state: Water levels and flow profiles along canal reaches, with offtake demand observations.
control.action: Adjust gates or commanded inflows at successive regulation steps.
control.dynamics: Water transport creates delays and interacting pools; upstream changes affect downstream levels later.
control.objective: Track delivery and level targets with modest gate movement while avoiding overtopping and low-water limits.

topics.title: Chlorine dosing in water networks
topics.problem: Chlorine booster dosing in a water network
topics.hook: Too little chlorine and the water is unsafe; too much and it forms by-products. Transport delays through the pipes make it a lagged control problem.
topics.start: [Monsia et al. 2026, surrogate-assisted chlorination](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07299); [WNTR](https://usepa.github.io/WNTR/)
topics.baseline: Constant or scheduled dosing
topics.angle: learned transport surrogate from EPANET runs, MPC with constraint tightening; transport delays make credit assignment interesting

control.state: Estimated chlorine concentrations and water residence states in pipes and tanks.
control.action: Set booster chlorine injection rates as demand and residual measurements change.
control.dynamics: Advection, mixing and decay make a dose affect different consumers after different delays.
control.objective: Use minimum disinfectant while keeping future delivered residuals within prescribed lower and upper bounds.

topics.title: Fair allocation of food bank donations
topics.problem: As a food bank's mobile pantry visits sites one after another over a season, decide how much of each donated commodity to give each site. Demand at the sites still to come is unknown and the truck's supply is fixed. The goal is to maximize Nash social welfare while keeping envy between sites and leftover food low.
topics.section: Food security and the future of food
topics.hook: The problem comes from a real Feeding America partner: in 2019 its Mobile Food Pantry served 70 regular sites over 722 visits. The paper proves that fairness and efficiency cannot both be had online, so the student has to choose a point on that tradeoff explicitly.
topics.start: [Sinclair et al. 2021, Sequential Fair Allocation: Achieving the Optimal Envy-Efficiency Tradeoff Curve, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.05308); [Sinclair et al. 2020, Sequential Fair Allocation of Limited Resources under Stochastic Demands, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.14382); [ORSuite resource-allocation env built on the Food Bank of the Southern Tier case](https://orsuite.readthedocs.io/en/latest/resource_allocation_readme.html); [code, MIT, needs an older Gymnasium](https://github.com/cornell-orie/ORSuite)
topics.baseline: ORSuite's equal-allocation agent and the paper's HopeGuardrail threshold policy
topics.angle: rolling-horizon re-solve or ADP with learned demand histograms; policy gradient on the ORSuite env, scored against the paper's envy-efficiency frontier

control.state: Remaining food inventory, previous allocations and beliefs about needs at unvisited sites.
control.action: Allocate quantities when each recipient site is reached.
control.dynamics: Allocations are irrevocable and reduce supply for later sites whose demand is not yet known.
control.objective: Improve welfare and fairness across the full route while respecting stock, perishability and allocation constraints.

topics.title: WFP food aid sourcing under uncertainty
topics.problem: Each month over a multi-month operation, choose the ration basket, the procurement source (international, regional or local) and the delivery routing for a World Food Programme operation. Funding, prices and lead times are uncertain. The goal is to minimize cost while meeting nutrient targets for every beneficiary, within capacity limits.
topics.section: Food security and the future of food
topics.hook: WFP's model cut Iraq operating costs by about 12% with almost no change in kilocalories. The authors say it is not robust to uncertain costs, lead times and capacities, which is exactly the gap a sequential, uncertainty-aware controller fills.
topics.start: [Peters et al. 2021, The Nutritious Supply Chain: Optimizing Humanitarian Food Assistance, INFORMS J. Optimization](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/abs/10.1287/ijoo.2019.0047); [preprint with the full MILP](https://optimization-online.org/2019/05/7198/); [WFP market price data, 76 countries](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/wfp-food-prices); [IPC acute food insecurity data](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/ipc-country-data); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: the paper's deterministic MILP, re-solved with point estimates
topics.angle: stochastic or robust rolling-horizon MPC over funding and price scenarios; decision-focused training of the price or IPC-phase forecaster on the cost of the resulting plan

control.state: Food stocks, shipments in transit, funds and uncertain future demand and donations.
control.action: Choose procurement, shipment and ration quantities at each planning update.
control.dynamics: Purchases arrive after lead times; distributions reduce future stock and spending reduces later flexibility.
control.objective: Meet nutritional needs with low procurement, transport and unmet-demand costs within cash and logistics limits.

topics.title: Grain reserve and trade policy as SDP
topics.problem: Each year after the harvest, a government sets public storage (and, optionally, trade taxes) for a staple food based on available supply and the world price. Harvests and world prices are random. The goal is to maximize welfare and stabilize prices, with stocks that can never go negative.
topics.section: Food security and the future of food
topics.hook: Gouel and Jean find that storage alone can hurt consumers in a small open economy because the stabilizing effect leaks to world markets, while pairing storage with trade policy stabilizes prices far more. The occasionally binding constraint that stocks stay non-negative is why tools like Dynare cannot solve these models.
topics.start: [Gouel and Jean 2015, Optimal Food Price Stabilization in a Small Open Developing Country, World Bank Economic Review](https://openknowledge.worldbank.org/handle/10986/24604); [working paper PDF](https://www.usitc.gov/research_and_analysis/documents/Gouel_and_Jean-Optimal_Food_0.pdf); [RECS rational-expectations storage solver, MATLAB](https://github.com/christophe-gouel/recs); [FAO Food Price Index, monthly since 1990](https://www.fao.org/worldfoodsituation/foodpricesindex/en/); [WFP domestic market prices](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/wfp-food-prices)
topics.baseline: private competitive storage only, or a fixed price-band buffer-stock rule; the paper's collocation solution as the reference
topics.angle: fitted value iteration, or a neural policy that amortizes the complementarity solver, scaled to larger states (several commodities, harvest forecasts) where the paper's 41x23 collocation grid stops scaling

control.state: Public grain stocks, prices, harvest information and beliefs about next-period supply.
control.action: Choose reserve purchases, releases and modeled trade interventions each period.
control.dynamics: Storage carries grain forward with losses; intervention changes future availability and modeled market prices.
control.objective: Reduce food-supply volatility and welfare losses within storage, fiscal and trade-policy constraints.

topics.title: Stored-grain aeration fan control
topics.problem: Hour by hour over a storage season, decide when to run a grain bin's aeration fan. The weather is uncertain, and grain temperature, moisture and the insect population are only partly observed. The goal is to minimize insect growth, spoilage and fan energy without re-wetting the grain.
topics.section: Food security and the future of food
topics.hook: In Yang et al.'s US simulations, raising the aeration target temperature roughly doubled adult insect numbers in southern states, so the fan rule decides whether insecticide is needed. In a 2025 barley trial, a drying-capacity trigger ran the fan 61 to 79% less than a simulated fixed schedule.
topics.start: [Yang et al. 2017, Regional analysis of bin aeration as an alternative to insecticidal control, Ecological Modelling](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/ecomod/v359y2017icp165-181.html); [Zekri et al., Energy-saving aeration control for semi-arid barley stores using a psychrometric drying-capacity criterion](https://www.ecoeet.com/Energy-saving-aeration-control-for-reducing-post-harvest-losses-in-semi-arid-barley,226004,0,2.html); [Roskopf 2015, MSc thesis simulating wheat aeration and cooling in Argentina](https://repositorio.inta.gob.ar/handle/20.500.12123/25183); [hourly ERA5 weather](https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/historical-weather-api); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: target-temperature thermostat rule (Yang et al.) or a fixed night-time schedule
topics.angle: MPC with weather forecasts and time-of-use electricity prices on a reduced bin heat-and-moisture model coupled to an age-structured insect model; offline RL from logged fan and sensor data
topics.venture: Farms and grain elevators, which pay to prevent spoilage and insect damage while running fans less.

control.state: Grain temperature and moisture profiles and estimated insect-development state, with ambient conditions.
control.action: Switch aeration fans on or off as weather and grain measurements change.
control.dynamics: Airflow moves cooling fronts; moisture and pest development retain the effects of earlier fan operation.
control.objective: Prevent spoilage and pest growth with low fan energy while avoiding rewetting and unsafe grain conditions.

topics.title: Fish feeding control with growth models
topics.problem: Each day of a grow-out cycle, choose the feed ration (and, where they can be controlled, temperature and dissolved oxygen) for a tank or pen. Appetite, water quality (unionized ammonia) and growth are uncertain. The goal is to track a target harvest weight at minimum feed cost and mortality.
topics.section: Food security and the future of food
topics.hook: Aljehani et al. report that Q-learning avoided mortality but tended to underfeed, while MPC cut both mortality and feed use at every ammonia level they tested, a clean model-based versus model-free comparison to extend. FishMet adds an appetite model validated on rainbow trout and Atlantic salmon.
topics.start: [Chahid et al. 2021, Model Predictive Control Paradigms for Fish Growth Reference Tracking in Precision Aquaculture, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.00004); [Aljehani et al. 2023, Model-based versus model-free feeding control and water quality monitoring for fish growth tracking, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.09915); [FishMet salmonid appetite and growth digital twin, AGPL code](https://git.app.uib.no/Sergey.Budaev/fishmet); [FishMet overview, Budaev et al. 2025](https://ahamodel.uib.no/fishmet-a-digital-twin-framework-for-appetite-feeding-decisions-and-growth-in-salmonid-fish.html)
topics.baseline: fixed feeding table (percent of body weight per day), or the papers' MPC
topics.angle: MPC on the Nile tilapia bioenergetic model compared with RL, then transfer to salmon or trout with FishMet as a stochastic, higher-fidelity simulator; objective aware of the feed conversion ratio
topics.venture: Fish farms, where feed is the largest operating cost.

control.state: Estimated fish biomass, appetite and relevant water-quality states from feeding and growth observations.
control.action: Choose feed ration at successive feeding intervals.
control.dynamics: Feed affects growth and waste loads; biomass and water conditions change later appetite and oxygen demand.
control.objective: Maximize harvest value net of feed cost while respecting ration and water-quality limits.

topics.title: Single-cell protein bioreactor control
topics.problem: Over a 48-hour moving horizon, set the six inlet flows (water, ammonium, nitrate, sodium, methane, oxygen) of a continuous Methylococcus capsulatus reactor. Kinetics and gas transfer are uncertain. The goal is to maximize biomass revenue minus feed cost while keeping pH on target.
topics.section: Food security and the future of food
topics.hook: Protein grown on methane by bacteria is one of the few alternative proteins with a published, control-ready reactor model: pH chemistry is coupled to growth, and six inputs must be coordinated. The lab model has seven differential states, and the industrial U-loop version reaches 87 states after discretization, a natural step up.
topics.start: [Nielsen et al. 2022, Modelling and Economic Optimal Control for a Laboratory-scale Continuous Stirred Tank Reactor for Single-cell Protein Production, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.02210); [Ritschel et al. 2020, Economic Nonlinear Model Predictive Control of a U-loop Bioreactor, ECC](https://orbit.dtu.dk/en/publications/economic-nonlinear-model-predictive-control-of-a-u-loop-bioreacto/); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: fixed steady-state feed rates, or the paper's open-loop economic optimal control
topics.angle: economic NMPC with an extended Kalman filter, then amortize the NMPC into a policy network or learn residual kinetics from data

control.state: Biomass, substrate, dissolved gases and pH, estimated from reactor measurements.
control.action: Choose the six modeled inlet flow rates at each control step.
control.dynamics: Microbial growth, reaction and gas transfer change the concentrations and future productive capacity.
control.objective: Maximize product value net of feed and energy costs while keeping pH and process inputs feasible.

topics.title: Fungicide spray timing for wheat septoria
topics.problem: Through the season, decide on which days to spray winter wheat against septoria, and at what dose. Weather forecasts are uncertain and the infection stays partly hidden until symptoms show. The goal is to maximize yield revenue minus fungicide cost and the number of sprays.
topics.section: Food security and the future of food
topics.hook: The spray decision is made on a hidden epidemic state, so this is a real POMDP and not just a threshold rule. Siddique et al. apply robust RL to weekly codling moth sprays in apple orchards, and FraNchEstYN models fungicide timing, dose and decay directly, so the same idea can be tested on wheat.
topics.start: [Milne et al. 2007, A model of the effect of fungicides on disease-induced yield loss for use in wheat disease management decision support systems, Annals of Applied Biology](https://repository.rothamsted.ac.uk/item/89x14/a-model-of-the-effect-of-fungicides-on-disease-induced-yield-loss-for-use-in-wheat-disease-management-decision-support-systems); [Siddique et al. 2019, Robust Pest Management Using Reinforcement Learning](https://www.cs.unh.edu/~mpetrik/pub/Siddique2019.pdf); [simpest crop, disease and fungicide simulator, Python, MIT](https://github.com/KaziJahidurRahaman/simpest); [FraNchEstYN crop, disease and fungicide model, R/C#](https://github.com/GeoModelLab/FraNchEstYN)
topics.baseline: fixed two-spray calendar at set growth stages, or a disease-threshold rule
topics.angle: POMDP with a belief over latent infection, solved by rollout or MPC on the simulator or by policy gradient; robust RL across calibrated parameter sets

control.state: Crop stage, estimated latent and visible infection and remaining spray budget, with weather forecasts.
control.action: Choose when to spray and the permitted dose during the season.
control.dynamics: Infection progresses before symptoms appear; treatment changes disease growth and protection available later.
control.objective: Protect final yield with minimum treatment cost within spray, timing and application limits.

topics.title: Seasonal stocking and pasture renewal SDP
topics.problem: Each season, set the stocking rate and decide whether to re-sow the pasture, given pasture biomass and the share of desirable species. Seasonal climate is random. The goal is to maximize the present value of grazing returns without degrading the pasture.
topics.section: Food security and the future of food
