topics.hook: Behrendt et al. treat pasture as a renewable resource, solve a four-season SDP by value iteration, and find the pasture states where tactical rests or re-sowing pay off. Adding paddocks makes it a rotational grazing problem that grid-based DP struggles with.
topics.start: [Behrendt et al. 2016, Using Seasonal Stochastic Dynamic Programming to identify optimal management decisions that achieve maximum economic sustainable yields from grasslands under climate risk, Agricultural Systems](https://hau.repository.guildhe.ac.uk/17250/1/Karl%20Behrendt%20using%20seasonal%20upload.pdf); [SILO daily climate data for Australia since 1889](https://www.longpaddock.qld.gov.au/silo/); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: a fixed stocking rate; the paper's discretized SDP as the reference
topics.angle: fitted value iteration or MPC over a continuous state with climate-conditioned transitions; extend to several paddocks to make it a rotational grazing problem

control.state: Pasture biomass, species composition and renewal status at each seasonal review.
control.action: Choose stocking rate and whether to renew pasture.
control.dynamics: Grazing depletes biomass and changes composition; regrowth and reseeding determine future carrying capacity.
control.objective: Maximize long-run livestock returns net of renewal cost while preserving viable pasture condition.

topics.title: Solar-pump drip irrigation scheduling
topics.problem: Each day, and hour by hour within it, decide when and how long to run a solar-powered drip-irrigation pump and how much to draw from a small battery. Solar power and crop water demand are only forecast. The goal is to meet the crop's water needs reliably with the least water and the smallest battery.
topics.section: Food security and the future of food
topics.hook: Over three growing seasons, the POWEIr controller cut water use by up to 44% and energy use by up to 43% compared with typical farmer practice, with no loss of yield. Unlike yield-based irrigation scheduling (the existing AquaCrop topic), the binding constraint here is when the sun shines.
topics.start: [Sheline et al. 2025, Designing a predictive optimal water and energy irrigation (POWEIr) controller for solar-powered drip irrigation systems in resource-constrained contexts, Applied Energy](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/appene/v377y2025ipas0306261924014909.html); [Sheline et al. 2026, Technical validation of the POWEIr controller, Smart Agricultural Technology](https://repo.mel.cgiar.org/items/1998f0b9-821f-45df-91ad-d3671bec18df); [Sheline 2024, MIT PhD thesis](https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/154164); [NASA POWER solar and weather data](https://power.larc.nasa.gov/); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: typical farmer practice (fixed daily schedule), or the POWEIr optimizer
topics.angle: stochastic MPC on solar and evapotranspiration forecasts; decision-focused training of the solar forecaster on irrigation shortfall

control.state: Root-zone water, battery charge and water-delivery state, with solar and irrigation-demand forecasts.
control.action: Schedule pump operation and battery charging or discharge through the day.
control.dynamics: Pumping spends stored electricity and replenishes soil water; solar and evapotranspiration alter future reserves.
control.objective: Meet crop-water needs reliably with low energy cost within pump, battery and soil-moisture bounds.

topics.title: Lettuce greenhouse climate
topics.problem: Lettuce greenhouse climate: RL-tuned MPC vs MPC vs RL on the van Henten model
topics.hook: Greenhouses burn gas for heat and CO2. Tuning an MPC with RL on the standard lettuce model is a well-scoped first project.
topics.start: [Mallick et al. 2024, RL-based MPC for greenhouse climate](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12789) with [code](https://github.com/SamuelMallick/mpcrl-greenhouse); [Morcego et al. 2023, RL vs MPC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.06110)
topics.baseline: Nominal MPC with the true model and grower setpoint schedules
topics.angle: RL tuning of the MPC cost, backoff or model under mismatch, or a learned terminal cost for short-horizon MPC

control.state: Indoor climate and crop biomass, observed with outdoor weather and production stage.
control.action: Set the heating, ventilation and CO2 inputs available in the published model.
control.dynamics: Heat and gas balances affect later climate; photosynthesis accumulates harvestable biomass throughout the crop cycle.
control.objective: Maximize harvest revenue net of heating and CO2 costs within climate and actuator constraints.

topics.title: Tomato greenhouse (GreenLight)
topics.problem: Tomato production control on the GreenLight model
topics.hook: GreenLight is the reference model for high-tech greenhouses. Short-horizon MPC with a learned terminal value is this course's spine in one project.
topics.start: [GreenLight-Gym, van Laatum et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05336); [van Laatum et al. 2026, RL inside short-horizon MPC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07365); [GreenLightGym](https://github.com/BartvLaatum/GreenLightGym)
topics.baseline: Rule-based grower controller
topics.angle: short-horizon NMPC with an RL-learned terminal value vs PPO under parametric uncertainty
topics.venture: Commercial greenhouse growers, who pay for more yield per unit of heating and lighting energy.

control.state: Greenhouse temperature, humidity, CO2 and crop-growth states, with weather and price forecasts.
control.action: Choose heating, ventilation, lighting and CO2 dosing at successive intervals.
control.dynamics: Climate responds with thermal and moisture delays; light and temperature alter future crop development.
control.objective: Maximize crop value net of energy and input costs while maintaining climate and equipment limits.

topics.title: Nitrogen fertilization
topics.problem: Nitrogen fertilization timing and dose for wheat
topics.hook: Making and spreading nitrogen fertilizer emits a lot, and what the crop does not take up pollutes water. The right dose at the right time cuts both.
topics.start: [CropGym, Overweg et al. 2021](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.04326); [WOFOSTGym, Solow et al. 2025, RLC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.19308); [WOFOSTGym](https://github.com/Intelligent-Reliable-Autonomous-Systems/WOFOSTGym)
topics.baseline: Agronomic split-application rule and an open-loop optimized schedule
topics.angle: offline RL and off-policy evaluation from logged seasons, forecast-aware policy vs DP over discretized soil nitrogen

control.state: Soil nitrogen and crop-development states, with weather, soil and growth observations.
control.action: Choose fertilizer amounts and application dates through the season.
control.dynamics: Nitrogen persists, is taken up or leaches; current dose changes later growth and fertilizer requirements.
control.objective: Maximize yield value net of fertilizer and environmental costs within application and crop-management limits.

topics.title: Irrigation scheduling
topics.problem: Irrigation scheduling for maize or wheat with soil-water dynamics
topics.hook: Agriculture uses most of the world's freshwater. Measuring the value of a weather forecast in litres saved makes a good poster.
topics.start: [Saikai et al. 2023, deep RL for irrigation scheduling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.00899); [gym-DSSAT, Gautron et al. 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.03270); [AquaCrop-OSPy](https://aquacropos.github.io/aquacrop/)
topics.baseline: Soil-moisture threshold rule
topics.angle: MPC with weather-ensemble forecasts on the AquaCrop model vs the rule vs an RL policy; quantify the value of forecast information
topics.venture: Farms and irrigation-equipment makers, who pay for the same yield with less water and pumping energy.

control.state: Root-zone moisture and crop-growth state, with rainfall and evapotranspiration forecasts.
control.action: Choose irrigation amount at each permitted watering decision.
control.dynamics: Water persists in soil, drains or is consumed; earlier stress influences future growth and yield.
control.objective: Maintain yield with low water and pumping use within irrigation-capacity and soil-water constraints.

topics.title: Indoor-farm lighting
topics.problem: Indoor-farm LED lighting with time-of-use prices and a thermal model
topics.hook: Vertical farms trade sunlight for electricity. Lighting when power is cheap while hitting the plants' daily light dose is the whole business.
topics.start: [LightFARM, Yu et al. 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27649)
topics.baseline: Fixed photoperiod
topics.angle: learned light-response model + MPC, or DP over the daily light budget with prices; the model is rebuilt from the paper

control.state: Crop-growth state, accumulated light exposure and room temperature, with electricity-price forecasts.
control.action: Choose light intensity and timing across successive photoperiods.
control.dynamics: Photosynthesis and thermal accumulation carry over; light used now changes remaining daily and seasonal requirements.
control.objective: Minimize electricity for a harvest target while respecting photoperiod, light-dose, temperature and fixture limits.

topics.title: Process units with an NMPC oracle
topics.problem: PC-Gym process units (crystallizer, four-tank, biofilm reactor) against an NMPC oracle
topics.hook: A tidy set of process units with an NMPC oracle, so you always know how far your learned controller is from optimal.
topics.start: [PC-Gym, Bloor et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.22093); [pc-gym](https://github.com/MaximilianB2/pc-gym)
topics.baseline: PID and the built-in NMPC oracle
topics.angle: learned Koopman or NN model + MPC, policy distilled from NMPC, RL under mismatch; report the optimality gap to the oracle

control.state: The concentrations, levels or temperatures of one selected process, with measured disturbances.
control.action: Choose the flow, feed or heating inputs defined for that process at each control step.
control.dynamics: Use the selected process's differential equations to propagate material and energy inventories between decisions.
control.objective: Match its published tracking or economic objective while satisfying the same state and input constraints as NMPC.

topics.title: Decision-focused models for a chemical plant
topics.problem: Economic NMPC for demand response of a chemical process under electricity prices
topics.hook: Train the model for the decision, not for prediction accuracy. A chemical plant that follows electricity prices makes the question concrete.
topics.start: [Mayfrank et al. 2024, end-to-end RL of Koopman models for eNMPC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.01674); [air-separation follow-up, 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.04522)
topics.baseline: eNMPC with the mechanistic model and a system-identified Koopman model
topics.angle: decision-focused training of the Koopman model through the MPC

control.state: Selected plant concentrations, temperatures and inventories, together with current demand or price forecasts.
control.action: Set the modeled production and energy inputs through receding-horizon optimization.
control.dynamics: Reaction, storage and transport dynamics make prediction errors change later feasible production and cost.
control.objective: Minimize closed-loop economic cost within plant constraints, comparing models through the same NMPC controller.

topics.title: Penicillin fermentation
topics.problem: Fed-batch penicillin fermentation: feed and environment control
topics.hook: Fed-batch fermentation makes antibiotics and many other products. Batch datasets let you try offline RL against an MPC baseline.
topics.start: [SMPL, Zhang et al. 2022, NeurIPS D&B](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.08851); [Petsagkourakis et al. 2019, RL for batch bioprocess optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.07292); [smpl](https://github.com/smpl-env/smpl)
topics.baseline: Fixed recipe and the included MPC
topics.angle: offline RL from the batch datasets, batch-to-batch policy gradient, GP or NN dynamics + MPC with a terminal reward

control.state: Biomass, substrate, penicillin concentration and broth volume, with noisy batch measurements.
control.action: Adjust feed and other modeled pH or temperature inputs throughout fermentation.
control.dynamics: Growth and product formation accumulate; feed changes future substrate, volume and productivity.
control.objective: Maximize terminal penicillin yield net of input costs while maintaining feasible volume and fermentation conditions.

topics.title: Tennessee Eastman plant
topics.problem: Tennessee Eastman plant-wide control with a residual policy
topics.hook: The classic plant-wide control problem of process engineering: 41 measurements, 12 valves and 20 standard disturbances.
topics.start: [Abbas et al. 2023, residual safe RL on the TE process](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.14788); [simplified TEP environment](https://github.com/AIRI-Institute/iprl_benchmark) (MATLAB-free)
topics.baseline: Decentralized PID structure
topics.angle: residual policy on top of PID, or learned Koopman model + MPC on a subset of loops under the standard disturbances

control.state: Estimated reactor and separator states, recycle conditions and measured product composition.
control.action: Change selected supervisory PID setpoints at each control interval.
control.dynamics: Material recycle and thermal dynamics delay responses and couple production, pressure and product quality.
control.objective: Meet production and quality targets with low operating cost while respecting benchmark safety and actuator limits.

topics.title: Anaerobic digester
topics.problem: Anaerobic digester (ADM1) biogas production under feedstock uncertainty
topics.hook: Digesters turn food waste and sludge into biogas. Overfeed them and the microbes acidify and stop; the constraint is real.
topics.start: [Gao et al. 2024, Communications Engineering](https://link.springer.com/10.1038/s44172-024-00183-7); [PyADM1](https://github.com/CaptainFerMag/PyADM1)
topics.baseline: PID on gas flow and constant loading rate
topics.angle: learned two-time-scale dynamics + MPC, robust policy with randomized influent, acidification as a hard constraint
topics.venture: Biogas and renewable-natural-gas plants, which pay for more gas from variable feedstocks without upsetting the digester.

control.state: Estimated microbial populations, substrate, volatile acids and alkalinity, with gas and pH measurements.
control.action: Choose feed rate and feed mixture as digestion conditions evolve.
control.dynamics: Slow microbial growth and faster acid accumulation create delayed instability after aggressive feeding.
control.objective: Increase useful methane production net of feed cost while avoiding acidification and process operating violations.

topics.title: Microalgae photobioreactor
topics.problem: Microalgae raceway photobioreactor: pH, dissolved oxygen, harvest and economics
topics.hook: Microalgae grow on CO2 and sunlight. The cited group deployed behaviour cloning on an industrial reactor, so the path to the real thing is short.
topics.start: [Otálora et al. 2025, economic MPC for industrial microalgae](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.15668); [Gil et al. 2025, behaviour cloning deployed on an industrial photobioreactor](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06853)
topics.baseline: Fixed harvest and on/off CO2 with PI on pH
topics.angle: behaviour cloning from PID then online fine-tuning, or EMPC with a learned growth model; the model is rebuilt from the paper

control.state: Biomass concentration, pH, dissolved oxygen and thermal state under observed light conditions.
control.action: Set CO2 dosing and harvesting or dilution inputs through the growth cycle.
control.dynamics: Photosynthesis, gas transfer and dilution change biomass and the conditions for later growth.
control.objective: Maximize harvested biomass value with low CO2 and energy use within pH, oxygen and equipment limits.

topics.title: Traffic signals with speed advice
topics.problem: Traffic-signal control with speed advice on calibrated city corridors (RESCO scenarios in SUMO)
topics.hook: Idling at red lights burns fuel and time. Calibrated scenarios from Cologne and Ingolstadt keep it real.
topics.start: [RESCO, Ault and Sharon 2021, NeurIPS D&B](https://datasets-benchmarks-proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2021/hash/f0935e4cd5920aa6c7c996a5ee53a70f-Abstract-round1.html); [Busch et al. 2023, joint signal and speed advice](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.09881); [sumo-rl](https://github.com/lucasalegre/sumo-rl), [CityFlow](https://github.com/cityflow-project/CityFlow)
topics.baseline: Fixed-time (Webster) and max-pressure
topics.angle: learn a store-and-forward queue model from rollouts, MPC over phases, amortize into a policy; compare with the published DQN numbers
topics.venture: Cities and transport departments, which pay for less delay and fuel at intersections they already control.

control.state: Intersection queues, approaching vehicle positions and current signal phases.
control.action: Choose signal phases and green durations and provide feasible vehicle-speed advice.
control.dynamics: Served vehicles leave one queue and enter downstream traffic; phase commitments determine later service opportunities.
control.objective: Reduce network travel time and stops while satisfying signal-clearance, minimum-green and vehicle-speed constraints.

topics.title: Highway ramp metering
topics.problem: Highway ramp metering with MPC as the policy class (METANET model)
topics.hook: MPC as the policy class, tuned by RL. The paper's code is public, so your contribution is a new network, a learned model or real demand data.
topics.start: [Airaldi et al. 2023, RL with MPC for ramp metering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.08820) with [code](https://github.com/FilippoAiraldi/mpcrl-for-ramp-metering); [sym-metanet](https://github.com/FilippoAiraldi/sym-metanet)
topics.baseline: PI-ALINEA
topics.angle: MPC with a deliberately wrong model whose parameters are tuned by Q-learning, or learned residual dynamics, vs black-box DDPG; change the network or use logged demand so it is not a rerun

control.state: Mainline traffic densities, ramp queues and current arrival estimates.
control.action: Set ramp admission rates at each traffic-control interval.
control.dynamics: Admitted vehicles affect downstream congestion; withheld vehicles accumulate in queues and constrain later metering.
control.objective: Minimize total travel and waiting time while respecting ramp storage and metering-rate limits.

topics.title: Workplace EV charging
topics.problem: Workplace EV charging on the Caltech ACN data
topics.hook: Real charging sessions from Caltech and JPL garages, with real three-phase limits. Forecast when drivers leave and you can charge more cars on the same wires.
topics.start: [Lee et al. 2019, ACN-Data, e-Energy](https://authors.library.caltech.edu/records/yvh76-f6d35); [ACN-Sim, Lee et al. 2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.02809); [acnportal](https://github.com/zach401/acnportal)
topics.baseline: Round-robin and least-laxity-first
topics.angle: MPC with learned arrival and departure forecasts fitted on the data, or offline RL from historical sessions, with the three-phase constraints checked

control.state: Vehicle charge levels, charger occupancy and beliefs about departures and requested energy.
control.action: Allocate charging power among connected vehicles as arrivals and needs are observed.
control.dynamics: Charging accumulates energy before individual deadlines and competes for future shared electrical capacity.
control.objective: Minimize charging cost and unmet requests within charger, phase and site-power constraints.

topics.title: Eco-driving at intersections
topics.problem: Eco-driving of a connected EV through signalized intersections
topics.hook: Knowing when the light turns green lets a car glide instead of braking. Longitudinal MPC with a learned model of the car ahead.
topics.start: [Jiang et al. 2022, eco-driving at signalized intersections](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.12065); SUMO electric-vehicle model
topics.baseline: Car-following plus a green-wave heuristic
topics.angle: MPC on longitudinal dynamics with a learned leader predictor, then distill into a policy

control.state: Vehicle position, speed and battery state, with traffic-signal and lead-vehicle forecasts.
control.action: Choose acceleration and regenerative-braking commands along the approach and crossing.
control.dynamics: Motion determines future signal encounters; acceleration and braking change energy use and remaining travel time.
control.objective: Minimize energy and delay while satisfying collision-avoidance, signal, speed and acceleration limits.

topics.title: Airport departure metering
topics.problem: Airport departure metering (pushback rate control) with a learned runway-queue model
topics.hook: Planes queueing for takeoff with engines running burn fuel for nothing. Holding them at the gate a little longer cuts that without losing throughput.
topics.start: [Simaiakis and Balakrishnan 2016, Transportation Science](https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/105359); [Sandberg et al. 2014, pushback rate control](https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/96873); [BTS on-time performance data](https://www.transtats.bts.gov/DL_SelectFields.aspx?gnoyr_VQ=FGJ&QO_fu146_anzr=b0-gvzr)
topics.baseline: Fixed pushback rate
topics.angle: fit the transient queue model to one airport's taxi-out data, MPC on the pushback rate, offline RL on logged days; the surface simulator is yours to build

control.state: Aircraft waiting at gates, taxiway and runway queues and predicted departure demand.
control.action: Release selected aircraft for pushback at successive departure-management decisions.
control.dynamics: Pushbacks enter taxi queues; holding aircraft preserves surface capacity but accumulates gate delay.
control.objective: Reduce taxi fuel and total delay while maintaining runway throughput and airport operating constraints.

topics.title: Spacecraft docking
topics.problem: Spacecraft docking and inspection with run-time assurance (Clohessy-Wiltshire dynamics)
topics.hook: Approaching a station comes with hard safety cones. Run-time assurance lets a learned controller fly inside them.
topics.start: [Dunlap et al. 2021, run-time assurance for docking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.00447); [Dunlap et al. 2024, six-degree-of-freedom inspection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11795); [safe-autonomy-sims](https://github.com/act3-ace/safe-autonomy-sims)
topics.baseline: LQR or MPC on the CW model
topics.angle: RL with a control-barrier filter vs MPC with learned residual dynamics (drag, J2)

control.state: Estimated relative position and velocity, attitude where modeled and remaining maneuver resources.
control.action: Choose thrust commands throughout the rendezvous and docking approach.
control.dynamics: Orbital and relative-motion dynamics propagate each burn into later position, velocity and reachable docking conditions.
control.objective: Dock with low fuel use while respecting keep-out zones, approach-speed and thrust constraints.

topics.title: Satellite attitude control
topics.problem: Satellite attitude control with a physics-informed learned model inside MPC, including a reaction-wheel failure
topics.hook: Losing a reaction wheel should not end a mission. A physics-informed model inside MPC against a learned policy, under actuator failure.
topics.start: [Cena et al. 2026, hybrid MPC with a physics-informed network](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.15954); [El Hariry et al. 2025, underactuated attitude control](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00165); [Basilisk](https://hanspeterschaub.info/basilisk/)
topics.baseline: Quaternion PD or LQR
topics.angle: residual system identification (PINN or SINDy) + NMPC vs PPO under actuator failure

control.state: Orientation, angular rate and reaction-wheel momentum, with sensor noise and actuator availability.
control.action: Command reaction-wheel torque or magnetic actuation at each attitude-control step.
control.dynamics: Rigid-body motion and momentum accumulation determine future pointing error and actuator saturation.
control.objective: Track attitude targets with low effort while respecting momentum, torque and pointing constraints.

topics.title: Earth-observation satellite tasking
topics.problem: Earth-observing satellite tasking under power and storage constraints
topics.hook: Earth-observing satellites watch forests, ice and crops. Choosing what to image with limited battery and storage is a planning problem.
topics.start: [BSK-RL, Stephenson and Schaub 2024](https://hanspeterschaub.info/Papers/Stephenson2024c.pdf); [bsk-rl](https://avslab.github.io/bsk_rl/)
topics.baseline: Greedy scheduler
topics.angle: receding-horizon DP or tree search with a learned resource model, then an amortized policy
topics.venture: Earth-observation satellite operators, which pay to deliver more useful images per satellite under power and downlink limits.

control.state: Orbit position, current attitude, battery charge, data-storage occupancy and previous image coverage.
control.action: Select the next imaging or downlink task as opportunities become available.
control.dynamics: Slews consume time and energy; images fill storage and remove or change the value of future targets.
control.objective: Maximize science or coverage value within visibility, slew, energy, storage and communication constraints.

topics.title: Contrail-aware flight paths
topics.problem: Contrail-aware 4D flight trajectory optimization under forecast uncertainty
topics.hook: Contrails may warm the planet about as much as aviation's CO2, and a small change of altitude avoids many of them. The open toolchain already runs collocation with real winds.
topics.start: [Sun and Olive 2025, feasibility of climate-optimal routing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13907); [OpenAP.top, Sun 2022, Aerospace](https://www.mdpi.com/2226-4310/9/7/383); [openap-top](https://github.com/junzis/openap-top) (CasADi collocation, ERA5 winds)
topics.baseline: Deterministic fuel-optimal collocation
topics.angle: scenario or robust MPC with re-planning as forecasts update, or a policy amortized from many optimized trajectories
topics.venture: Airlines, which pay to cut the warming effect of their contrails at a small fuel cost.

control.state: Aircraft position, speed and fuel, with atmospheric and contrail-risk forecasts.
control.action: Choose altitude, heading and thrust for successive flight segments.
control.dynamics: Trajectory decisions change fuel reserves, future atmospheric exposure and the airspace reachable before arrival.
control.objective: Balance fuel and modeled climate impact while meeting arrival, aircraft-envelope and airspace constraints.

topics.title: Air traffic conflict resolution
topics.problem: En-route conflict resolution and arrival merging in BlueSky
topics.hook: Aircraft must stay 5 nautical miles apart, and more direct routes save fuel. Bring a model-based angle, not just another RL agent.
topics.start: [BlueSky-Gym, Groot et al. 2024](https://research.tudelft.nl/en/publications/bluesky-gym-reinforcement-learning-environments-for-air-traffic-a/); [bluesky-gym](https://github.com/TUDelft-CNS-ATM/bluesky-gym)
topics.baseline: Geometric and rule-based resolution
topics.angle: MPC with a learned intruder-intent predictor vs SAC or PPO; scaling with traffic density; the model-based angle is required here

control.state: Aircraft positions and velocities, intended routes and uncertainty about future motion.
control.action: Issue feasible heading, speed or altitude changes when conflicts are predicted.
control.dynamics: Commands alter future trajectories and may create later conflicts with other aircraft.
control.objective: Maintain separation with minimal delay and route disruption within aircraft maneuver and airspace limits.

topics.title: Delivery-drone energy
topics.problem: Energy-aware delivery-drone speed and altitude in wind, from real flight data
topics.hook: 196 real delivery flights with power, wind and payload. Fit how much energy each speed costs, then plan the speed profile.
topics.start: [Rodrigues et al. 2021, DJI Matrice 100 delivery dataset](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.13313); [Muli et al. 2022, drone energy models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.01609); [CMU dataset](https://kilthub.cmu.edu/articles/dataset/Data_Collected_with_Package_Delivery_Quadcopter_Drone/12683453)
topics.baseline: Constant cruise speed
topics.angle: fit power as a function of speed, payload and wind, then DP or MPC over the speed profile with scenario wind; validate on held-out flights

control.state: Drone position, speed, remaining battery energy and estimated wind along the route.
control.action: Choose speed, altitude and the next route segment during delivery.
control.dynamics: Flight spends a finite energy reserve; route and speed choices change later wind exposure and arrival feasibility.
control.objective: Minimize energy while meeting delivery time, flight-envelope and landing-reserve constraints.

topics.title: Satellite collision avoidance
topics.problem: Choose whether to wait for another tracking update or execute an avoidance burn before a conjunction, balancing collision risk, fuel use and loss of maneuvering time.
topics.hook: Each new conjunction message can change the assessed risk. Waiting may resolve uncertainty, but it also reduces the time left for an effective avoidance maneuver.
topics.start: [Bourriez et al. 2023, autonomous collision avoidance with RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.18966); [Uriot et al. 2020, ESA collision avoidance challenge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.03069); [Kelvins CDM dataset](https://kelvins.esa.int/collision-avoidance-challenge/data/)
topics.baseline: Threshold rule on collision probability
topics.angle: learn an observation or uncertainty-update model from CDM sequences, combine it with an orbital maneuver model, and solve the wait-or-burn problem by DP or belief-space planning. Compare risk and fuel on simulated conjunction episodes
topics.venture: Satellite operators and space-safety services, which pay to avoid both collisions and needless fuel-burning maneuvers.
topics.scope: The ESA challenge records describe conjunction-risk evolution, not supported counterfactual burn outcomes. Specify the orbital action model and observation assumptions; do not treat historical CDM sequences as an offline-RL action-transition dataset.

control.state: Beliefs about relative orbit and covariance, remaining fuel and time to closest approach.
control.action: Wait for another tracking update or select the timing and size of a feasible avoidance burn.
control.dynamics: Tracking updates change uncertainty; a burn changes the relative orbit and consumes fuel needed for later maneuvers.
control.objective: Reduce collision-risk and maneuver costs within fuel, orbital and response-time constraints.

topics.title: Wafer-fab dispatching
topics.problem: Lot dispatching in a wafer fab (SMT2020 in PySCFabSim)
topics.hook: Chip fabs route lots through hundreds of tools with setups and queue-time limits. Dispatching rules still dominate, so there is room to do better.
topics.start: [Tassel et al. 2023, fab scheduling with self-supervised and RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.07162); [Stöckermann et al. 2025, scalability of RL dispatching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11135); [PySCFabSim](https://github.com/prosysscience/PySCFabSim-release)
topics.baseline: FIFO, critical ratio, earliest due date
topics.angle: fluid or queueing model + rolling-horizon dispatch vs policy gradient; restrict to one bottleneck area (lithography)
topics.venture: Semiconductor fabs, where small throughput gains are worth millions.

control.state: Lot queues, processing stages, tool availability and setup or completion timers.
control.action: Assign waiting lots to compatible tools whenever capacity becomes available.
control.dynamics: Processing occupies tools and sends lots to later reentrant stages, changing future bottlenecks.
control.objective: Improve throughput and cycle time while respecting tool compatibility, setup and due-date constraints.

topics.title: Warehouse robot dispatch
topics.problem: Robot-to-task dispatch in a warehouse as a queueing control problem
topics.hook: A fleet of warehouse robots is a queueing network. Add realistic orders and congestion, or it stays a toy.
topics.start: [Krnjaic et al. 2024, scalable MARL for warehouse logistics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.11498); [RWARE](https://github.com/semitable/robotic-warehouse)
topics.baseline: Nearest-idle-robot and FIFO
topics.angle: aggregate fluid model of aisle queues + MPC-based assignment vs hierarchical MARL; add realistic order statistics and congestion, or it stays a toy
topics.venture: Warehouse operators and robot makers, who pay for more orders per hour from the same fleet.

control.state: Robot locations and battery states, open tasks and aisle or station congestion.
control.action: Assign tasks and reposition idle robots as orders arrive or tasks finish.
control.dynamics: Trips occupy robots and shared routes; current assignments alter later vehicle availability and congestion.
control.objective: Reduce order completion time and empty travel within battery, collision-avoidance and station-capacity limits.

topics.title: Metal 3D printing melt pool
topics.problem: Layer-to-layer melt-pool control in laser powder bed fusion
topics.hook: Metal 3D printing fails when the melt pool runs too hot or too cold. Learning control across layers is iterative learning control in action.
topics.start: [Liao-McPherson et al. 2024, layer-to-layer melt pool control](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.10218); [Ogoke and Barati Farimani 2021, thermal control with deep RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.03355); [AdditiveFOAM](https://github.com/ORNL/AdditiveFOAM) for validation
topics.baseline: Constant power or PI on the melt pool
topics.angle: learn a layer-to-layer linear or Koopman model from a few simulated layers, then iterative-learning control or MPC
topics.venture: Makers and users of metal 3D printers, who pay for fewer defective parts and less post-build inspection.

control.state: Estimated thermal field, melt-pool geometry and previous-layer temperature from sparse observations.
control.action: Adjust laser power along successive scan segments or layers.
control.dynamics: Heat diffuses and accumulates across tracks and layers, changing later melt-pool response.
control.objective: Track melt-pool targets and reduce defects while respecting laser-power and overheating limits.

topics.title: Mineral grinding circuit
topics.problem: Grinding-mill circuit control (run-of-mine ore)
topics.hook: Grinding ore takes a large share of a mine's energy. Ore hardness changes all the time, and the published model gives you every parameter.
topics.start: [Le Roux et al. 2013, grinding mill circuit model, Minerals Engineering](https://repository.up.ac.za/handle/2263/39683); [Van Niekerk et al. 2025, RL-tuned PID for grinding circuits, Control Engineering Practice](https://repository.up.ac.za/items/9ac56fb7-85b2-4949-9427-f172fa652e45)
topics.baseline: Decentralized PID
topics.angle: NMPC on the true model vs MPC on an identified model (SINDy or NN), RL-tuned PID; robustness to ore-hardness changes; the published ODE model is implemented by you
topics.venture: Mining companies, for which grinding is the largest energy use at a mine.

control.state: Mill and sump hold-ups, particle-size distribution and estimated ore hardness.
control.action: Set the published model's ore-feed, water and pump inputs at each interval.
control.dynamics: Grinding, recirculation and inventory accumulation delay size and throughput responses to input changes.
control.objective: Increase useful throughput with low energy while meeting product-size, hold-up and equipment constraints.

topics.title: Kraft pulp digester
topics.problem: Kappa-number control of a continuous kraft digester
topics.hook: Pulp mills cook wood chips for hours in a tall column. Long transport delays and grade changes make it a slow, hard MPC problem.
topics.start: [Rantanen et al. 2005, blow-line kappa number, IFAC](https://folk.ntnu.no/skoge/prost/proceedings/ifac2005/Fullpapers/03850.pdf); [kraft digester model code, University of Pretoria](https://researchdata.up.ac.za/articles/code/Kraft_digester_modelling_and_optimization_code/22302685)
topics.baseline: H-factor and PI temperature control
topics.angle: Koopman or NN surrogate of the distributed model + MPC with long transport delays and grade transitions

control.state: Chip residence and delignification profiles, liquor concentration and temperature estimates.
control.action: Adjust cooking temperature, alkali addition and controllable liquor flows.
control.dynamics: Chips travel and react over long residence times, so early cooking choices affect later pulp quality.
control.objective: Meet Kappa-number and throughput targets with low chemical and energy use within process limits.

topics.title: RL for multi-step nanocrystal synthesis
topics.problem: Choose, injection by injection over an episode of up to 20 injections, which reagent to add and at what volume and reaction time in a self-driving fluidic lab, under uncertainty about which partial sequences are even viable, to maximize the optical quality of the resulting core-shell quantum dots within a fixed experiment budget.
topics.hook: In the paper's own comparison, Bayesian optimization over the full sequence failed to find any viable 20-injection route in 100 experiments, while the sequential agent found one and reached 450% higher photoluminescence intensity than the literature protocol. The released digital twin lets you rerun that comparison without a lab.
topics.start: [Volk et al. 2023, AlphaFlow: autonomous discovery and optimization of multi-step chemistry using a self-driven fluidic lab guided by reinforcement learning, Nature Communications 14:1403](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10420940); [code, campaign exports and digital twin](https://github.com/AbolhasaniLab/AlphaFlow)
topics.baseline: the literature colloidal-ALD injection sequence, plus the paper's ensemble-NN Bayesian optimization over whole sequences
topics.angle: treat the injection sequence as a finite-horizon MDP and plan with the learned viability classifier and reward model; compare rollout depth, and try offline RL on the released campaign data instead of the paper's 4-step rollout

control.state: Partial synthesis history, estimated particle-growth state and measurements available between stages.
control.action: Choose the next reagent addition, volume and waiting time in a multi-step synthesis.
control.dynamics: Reactions irreversibly change particles; earlier additions constrain attainable structures and later useful actions.
control.objective: Reach target optical or material properties with low reagent and experiment cost within feasible synthesis protocols.

topics.title: Transient flow ramps for kinetics
topics.problem: Design the time profile of flow rate, temperature and feed concentration in a plug-flow reactor over a single 100-minute run, subject to pump, HPLC-sampling and monotonicity constraints, to minimize the posterior uncertainty of Arrhenius kinetic parameters that are only partially known beforehand.
topics.hook: One designed 2-hour ramp gave parameter precision comparable to a steady-state campaign of eight experiments at about eight hours each. The reactor model is a short ODE, so the whole loop is rebuildable, and the paper reports one designed experiment whose confidence region did not overlap the others, which is a real modelling-mismatch question to dig into.
topics.start: [Waldron et al. 2019, Model-based design of transient flow experiments for the identification of kinetic parameters, Reaction Chemistry & Engineering](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10086273/1/c9re00342h.pdf) (benzoic acid esterification, transient PFR as a train of batch reactors, D-optimal Fisher-information objective, all parameter ranges and initial guesses given); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: the paper's intuitively designed ramps, and its earlier campaign of 8 factorial plus 8 steady-state D-optimal experiments
topics.angle: cast information-maximizing experiment design as trajectory optimization on the reactor ODE, then make it closed-loop: re-plan the remaining ramp after each HPLC measurement as the parameter estimate moves

control.state: Reactor concentration and residence states, parameter beliefs and remaining experiment time.
control.action: Choose successive flow, temperature and concentration ramps under available measurement schedules.
control.dynamics: Transport delays shape observations; new measurements update kinetic beliefs and change the value of later excitation.
control.objective: Reduce kinetic-parameter uncertainty within pump, measurement and experiment-duration constraints.

topics.title: Experiment paths in a flow reactor
topics.problem: Pick the next reaction condition in a flow reactor at each sampling instant over an episode, where moving an input is itself costly and some moves are forbidden (flow rate may only decrease, so residence time is non-decreasing), to find high-yield conditions while minimizing total campaign time rather than number of experiments.
topics.hook: This is the cleanest example of why a self-driving lab is not black-box optimization: the lab cannot teleport between conditions, and some transitions corrupt the measurement. Both the constraint structure and an open emulator built from real reaction data are available, so the planning-versus-greedy comparison is a week of work plus thinking.
topics.start: [Folch et al. 2024, Transition Constrained Bayesian Optimization via Markov Decision Processes, NeurIPS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08406) (Knorr pyrazole transient reactor, 10 episodes of 10 steps, ODE-informed kernel); [SnAKe code with its SnAr cost-aware benchmark](https://github.com/cog-imperial/SnAKe); [Summit, with SnAr and data-driven cross-coupling emulators](https://github.com/sustainable-processes/summit)
topics.baseline: greedy UCB with no planning, which the paper reports performs very poorly under these transition constraints
topics.angle: solve the acquisition problem in policy space with dynamic programming or policy gradient over the reactor's reachable transitions; compare against a path-planning heuristic (SnAKe) and a myopic acquisition on the same emulator

control.state: Current reaction conditions, reactor transition state, surrogate-model beliefs and remaining campaign time.
control.action: Choose the next condition to visit and measure.
control.dynamics: Moving between conditions consumes time and settling effort; measurements update beliefs for subsequent experiment choices.
control.objective: Find high-yield conditions within wall-clock and transition constraints, accounting for the information value of each experiment.

topics.title: Battery test campaign as an MDP
topics.problem: Decide which of 224 six-step ten-minute fast-charging protocols to put on the 48 available test channels each round, and when to stop a running test early on the basis of its first cycles, to identify the longest-lifetime protocol under a fixed wall-clock budget and uncertain, noisy lifetime predictions.
topics.hook: The paper found good protocols in 16 days where exhaustive testing without early prediction would have taken over 500 days, and the repository ships the stochastic lifetime simulator the authors used for tuning, so the allocation and stopping policy can be studied against the real campaign. This is the lab-loop and test-allocation side of fast charging, not the battery physics.
topics.start: [Attia et al. 2020, Closed-loop optimization of fast-charging protocols for batteries with machine learning, Nature 578:397](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/117547r6); [closed-loop code, protocol space and stochastic lifetime simulator](https://github.com/chueh-ermon/battery-fast-charging-optimization); [early-prediction paper repo and the 124-cell dataset pointer](https://github.com/rdbraatz/data-driven-prediction-of-battery-cycle-life-before-capacity-degradation)
topics.baseline: the paper's closed-loop Bayesian optimization with a fixed early-prediction cutoff, and exhaustive testing
topics.angle: treat channel allocation plus early stopping as an optimal-stopping and budgeted-allocation MDP, where the stopping time is decided per cell from its own partial trace rather than fixed in advance
topics.venture: Battery developers, who pay to find good cell designs and charging protocols with fewer months of testing.

control.state: Partial cycling traces, protocol-value beliefs, occupied test channels and remaining campaign time.
control.action: Assign charging protocols to channels, continue tests or stop unpromising tests early.
control.dynamics: Tests occupy channels for many cycles; partial results update beliefs while stopping releases scarce future capacity.
control.objective: Identify a long-life protocol before the campaign deadline within channel and testing-budget limits.

topics.title: Optogenetic control of gene expression
topics.problem: Choose red or green light every five minutes for each of thousands of individual bacterial cells, over a horizon of a few hours, to hold or track a target fluorescence level despite cell-to-cell variability, division noise and an unstable intermediate range of a self-activating circuit.
topics.hook: The experimental paper controls up to 10,000 cells individually with a 5-minute light decision and a 2-hour horizon, searching about 1,000 candidate light sequences per cell per step; the companion paper gives a Gillespie simulator of the same circuit in JAX with PI, bang-bang and deep MPC baselines already implemented. You get a real actuator, a real sampling rate, and a controller comparison that someone cares about.
topics.start: [Lugagne/Dunlop et al., Deep model predictive control of gene expression in thousands of single cells, Nature Communications 15 (2024), preprint](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2022.10.28.514305.full.pdf); [control, training and analysis code](https://gitlab.com/dunloplab/deepcellcontrol); [Control of a bi-stable genetic system via parallelized reinforcement learning, CDC 2025 preprint](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.09.14.676149.full.pdf); [JAX/gymnax Gillespie simulator and PQN code](https://gitlab.com/lugagnelab/pqn-control-cdc2025)
topics.baseline: constant light, bang-bang and PI control, and the deep MPC with an LSTM encoder plus particle-swarm search over light sequences
topics.angle: learn a policy on the stochastic simulator and compare it against deep MPC on the same objective, with the real question being sample cost in simulated lab hours and transfer to the noise the microscope actually sees

control.state: Beliefs about gene-expression states from fluorescence measurements, with growth and division information.
control.action: Choose red and green light inputs at successive stimulation intervals.
control.dynamics: Expression and protein turnover respond with delays; stochastic division changes later observed fluorescence.
control.objective: Track an expression target with low light exposure while respecting illumination and biological operating limits.

topics.title: Turbidostat control for lab evolution
topics.problem: Set dilution events and temperature in each vial of a continuous-culture array, every 30 seconds over runs of hundreds of hours, to hold a population at a prescribed density or growth rate (or to track a designed selection pressure) despite drift in growth rate as the population evolves.
topics.hook: The paper evolves 78 yeast populations for 500 hours in different density windows, and the density window is exactly the experimental variable the controller sets, so controller design changes what the experiment measures. The hardware is open and the control scripts are plain Python, which makes the model-versus-threshold comparison concrete even if you only ever run it in simulation.
topics.start: [Wong et al. 2018, Precise, automated control of conditions for high-throughput growth of yeast and bacteria with eVOLVER, Nature Biotechnology 36:614](https://www.bu.edu/khalillab/_papers/wong-nbt2018.pdf); [eVOLVER control software, where feedback routines are written](https://github.com/FYNCH-BIO/dpu); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: the platform's threshold turbidostat (dilute above an upper OD, stop at a lower OD) with PID temperature control
topics.angle: replace the threshold rule with receding-horizon control on a Monod chemostat model identified online, so growth rate rather than density is the controlled variable and the selection pressure stays constant as fitness changes

control.state: Cell density, estimated growth rate and temperature, inferred from recent culture measurements.
control.action: Adjust dilution and permitted temperature settings during the evolution experiment.
control.dynamics: Dilution changes biomass; growth and population adaptation alter future density and selection pressure.
control.objective: Maintain the intended growth or selection regime within density, temperature and dilution-rate limits.

topics.title: Scheduling a self-driving lab
topics.problem: Assign each synthesis task of a batch of samples to an instrument and a start time on a robotic materials platform, with task durations from minutes to over twelve hours, lockstep capacity constraints (the centrifuge runs all its samples together), heater cooldown rules and limits on how long a prepared sample may wait, to minimize campaign makespan while new jobs keep arriving.
topics.hook: The authors report about 28 seconds to schedule a 16-job batch and 1.4 seconds to reschedule after 8 jobs are added, so there is a solved optimum to measure a learned dispatcher against. It is also the one topic where throughput, not sample efficiency, is what limits a real self-driving lab.
topics.start: [McDannald, Tisaranni and Joress, Optimal Resource Utilization for Autonomous Laboratory Orchestrators (NIST), preprint](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.01188); [autoMOF orchestrator and OR-Tools job-shop scheduler](https://github.com/usnistgov/autoMOF)
topics.baseline: the paper's constraint-programming job-shop solve, plus naive sequential and round-robin execution
topics.angle: learn a dispatching policy that re-decides as jobs arrive and durations turn out wrong, and feed the scheduling cost back into which experiments the campaign proposes, which the authors list as an open problem

control.state: Task dependencies, running experiments, instrument modes and heating, cooling or cleaning timers.
control.action: Assign the next ready tasks to instruments and choose their start times.
control.dynamics: Starting tasks occupies shared equipment and unlocks later stages only after processing and transition delays.
control.objective: Minimize campaign makespan or lateness while respecting dependencies, instrument capacity and sample hold times.

topics.title: Steering evolution with drug sequences
topics.problem: Choose which antibiotic to apply at each step of a one-to-three-step sequence before the final treatment, given a measured fitness landscape over 16 genotypes and uncertainty about the starting population, to minimize the probability that the population ends at the most resistant genotype.
topics.hook: The transition matrices come from measured growth rates of isogenic E. coli mutants under 15 antibiotics, and the paper finds that none of the 15 drug pairs commute, so order genuinely matters and exhaustive search over sequences stops being possible past three steps. It pairs naturally with a turbidostat as the apparatus that would run the policy.
topics.start: [Nichol et al. 2015, Steering Evolution with Sequential Therapy to Prevent the Emergence of Bacterial Antibiotic Resistance, PLoS Computational Biology 11(9)](https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid:39c50aee-1ae7-4241-a792-8cd36d6bca03/files/m96103ecee9c20e439ed9aea07333299f); [Markov chain model code](https://github.com/Daniel-Nichol/EvolutionarySteering); landscapes from Mira et al. (15 beta-lactams, blaTEM-50 mutants), model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: no steering, and the paper's exhaustive search over sequences of length one to three
topics.angle: solve the absorbing-Markov-chain model as a finite-horizon MDP, then as a POMDP where the genotype distribution is only observed through growth-rate measurements, which is what a continuous-culture experiment would actually give you

control.state: Genotype distribution or a belief over it, observed phenotypes and previous drug exposure.
control.action: Select the next drug at each treatment-sequence step in the evolutionary model.
control.dynamics: Drug-dependent selection changes the genotype distribution and susceptibility to later drugs.
control.objective: Minimize terminal resistance or pathogen fitness within the modeled sequence length and intervention constraints.

topics.title: LIGO hard-pitch angular loop shaping
topics.problem: Choose the feedback controller for LIGO Livingston's common-hard-pitch angular loop, running continuously while the detector is locked, under time-varying optical-spring dynamics and sensor noise, to minimize control noise injected into the 10-30 Hz band while keeping the loop stable and the mirror angle suppressed.
topics.hook: The current angular control loop adds noise that limits low-frequency sensitivity, and Deep Loop Shaping cut that control noise by over 30x in the 10-30 Hz band on the real detector. The identified plant and recorded data are public, so the problem can be studied without detector access.
topics.start: [Buchli et al. 2025, Improving cosmological reach of a gravitational wave observatory using Deep Loop Shaping, Science](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.14016); [identified CHARD plant model and selected ASC data from LIGO Livingston (Zenodo, CC BY 4.0)](https://zenodo.org/records/18892402); closed-loop model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: LIGO's hand-designed linear SISO controller
topics.angle: actor-critic RL with frequency-domain rewards on the identified plant, compared with convex or H-infinity loop shaping; test robustness to optical-spring drift

control.state: Angular motion, optical-spring response and controller-filter states under modeled disturbances.
control.action: Choose controller parameters, then apply the resulting feedback torque at every simulation sample.
control.dynamics: Closed-loop angular and filter dynamics determine future motion and the stability of the entire response.
control.objective: Reduce relevant-band angular noise while maintaining stability, alignment suppression and actuator limits.

topics.title: Rubin LSST survey scheduling
topics.problem: Choose the next pointing and filter for the Rubin Observatory visit by visit through each night of a multi-year survey, under uncertain clouds, seeing and sky brightness and with slew and filter-change time costs, to maximize survey metrics (depth, sky coverage, revisit cadence) subject to visibility and Moon-avoidance constraints.
topics.hook: The scheduler that will run Rubin picks each visit greedily from a hand-weighted reward, and the same code ships with a survey simulator (a full 10-year run takes about 6 hours, and shorter runs are an option). A better policy can be scored on the metrics the project itself uses.
topics.start: [Naghib et al. 2019, A Framework for Telescope Schedulers: With Applications to the Large Synoptic Survey Telescope, AJ](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.04815); [rubin_scheduler, the Feature Based Scheduler with survey simulation](https://github.com/lsst/rubin_scheduler); [docs](https://rubin-scheduler.lsst.io/); for an offline-RL variant on a small telescope, [Terranova et al. 2023, Self-Driving Telescopes, NeurIPS ML4PS workshop](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.18094) with [data, checkpoints and code](https://zenodo.org/records/8388483)
topics.baseline: the Feature Based Scheduler, which greedily picks the feasible survey with the highest weighted sum of basis-function rewards
topics.angle: learn the basis-function weights by policy search on the simulator's science metrics, or add receding-horizon lookahead over the night (MPC) on top of the greedy rule

control.state: Telescope pointing and filter, elapsed night time, visit history and current sky and weather conditions.
control.action: Select the next field, filter and exposure when the telescope becomes available.
control.dynamics: Slews and exposures consume time; visit history changes later cadence and coverage value.
control.objective: Maximize survey science value while meeting visibility, slew, exposure and revisit requirements.

topics.title: GW counterpart follow-up scheduling
topics.problem: Over the first nights after a gravitational-wave alert, choose which sky tiles a wide-field telescope observes, in what order and for how long, under skymap localization uncertainty, an unknown fading transient, visibility windows and weather, to maximize the probability that the counterpart is detected in two images over two nights within the available telescope time.
topics.hook: Coughlin et al. found that detection efficiency changes by a factor of 2 or more depending on the tiling, time-allocation and scheduling choice, so the decision rule matters. The scheduler is open source and installs from PyPI, so the whole loop can be closed in simulation.
topics.start: [Coughlin et al. 2018, Optimizing searches for electromagnetic counterparts of gravitational wave triggers, MNRAS](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.02255); [Almualla et al. 2020, Dynamic Scheduling: Target of Opportunity Observations of Gravitational Wave Events, MNRAS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.09718); [gwemopt code](https://github.com/mcoughlin/gwemopt)
topics.baseline: gwemopt's greedy or SEAR tile scheduling with a fixed time-allocation rule
topics.angle: closed-loop replanning (MPC) that updates the counterpart posterior after each non-detection; amortize the planner into a policy trained on many simulated skymaps

control.state: Sky-localization beliefs, previous detections or nondetections, telescope position and remaining observing time.
control.action: Choose the next tile, exposure and observing sequence after each update.
control.dynamics: Observations update location beliefs while the transient fades; slews consume opportunities for later detections.
control.objective: Maximize counterpart-detection probability within night length, visibility and telescope timing constraints.

topics.title: Cryo-EM data collection path planning
topics.problem: During a cryo-EM session of a few hours, choose which grid, square, patch and hole to image next, when hole quality is known only through a noisy classifier on low-magnification images and each move costs 2 to 10 minutes of stage time, to maximize the number of good (low-CTF) micrographs within the time budget.
topics.hook: Cryo-EM data collection is costly and needs expert operators, and in one of the paper's datasets only 33.4% of holes give usable images. CryoRL already beat average human operators; a planner that uses the patch/square/grid cost hierarchy explicitly is the natural next step.
topics.start: [Fan et al. 2024, CryoRL: Reinforcement Learning Enables Efficient Cryo-EM Data Collection, WACV](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/WACV2024/html/Fan_CryoRL_Reinforcement_Learning_Enables_Efficient_Cryo-EM_Data_Collection_WACV_2024_paper.html) ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.07543)); [code](https://github.com/IBM/CryoRL-pytorch); [hole-level image data](https://github.com/yilaili/cryoRL-pytorch-data)
topics.baseline: greedy ranking of squares and patches by predicted low-CTF count (the paper also compares with human operators)
topics.angle: treat it as stochastic orienteering over the grid hierarchy: lookahead/MPC or DP that uses the travel-cost structure, against the published DQN

control.state: Stage position, observed grid quality, beliefs about unvisited squares and holes and remaining session time.
control.action: Choose the next grid location to inspect or image.
control.dynamics: Stage transitions consume time; acquired images reveal quality and influence subsequent collection choices.
control.objective: Maximize usable micrographs within session time, transition costs and acquisition constraints.

topics.title: Neutron triple-axis measurement planning
topics.problem: During a beam-time allocation, choose the sequence of (Q, E) points a three-axis neutron spectrometer measures, when the intensity map is unknown and each point costs counting time plus axis travel time, to minimize the reconstruction error of the intensity at each cost milestone.
topics.hook: Beam time at neutron sources is scarce, and grid scans spend much of it on background. BASE already prices every move with the instrument's axis speeds and provides test cases and a scoring procedure, so a travel-aware planner can be compared fairly with grids and myopic active learning.
topics.start: [Teixeira Parente et al. 2022, Benchmarking Autonomous Scattering Experiments Illustrated on TAS, Front. Mater.](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/materials/articles/10.3389/fmats.2021.772014/full); [Teixeira Parente et al. 2023, Active learning-assisted neutron spectroscopy with log-Gaussian processes, Nat. Commun.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.00980); [BASE benchmark code (GPL-3.0)](https://jugit.fz-juelich.de/ainx/base)
topics.baseline: predefined grid scans, and the myopic log-Gaussian-process active learner
topics.angle: non-myopic, route-aware planning that trades information gain against motor travel (lookahead/MPC), or an amortized policy trained across the BASE test cases

control.state: Instrument-axis positions, beliefs about scattering intensity and remaining beam time.
control.action: Choose the next momentum-energy point and counting duration.
control.dynamics: Axis motion and counting consume time; counts reduce uncertainty and change later informative measurement choices.
control.objective: Minimize reconstruction error within beam-time, axis-motion and measurement feasibility limits.

topics.title: LC-MS/MS precursor selection (DDA)
topics.problem: At every MS1 survey scan of a liquid-chromatography run, choose which precursor ions to fragment next and which to exclude, under unknown elution profiles and a fixed scan-time budget, to maximize the number of distinct compounds that receive a usable fragmentation spectrum.
topics.hook: Every scan spent re-fragmenting an abundant ion is a compound left unidentified. ViMMS simulates acquisition scan by scan from real LC-MS data, and heuristics that Davies et al. tuned in it beat TopN on a real instrument, so gains in the simulator have carried over to hardware before.
topics.start: [Davies et al. 2021, Rapid Development of Improved Data-dependent Acquisition Strategies, Anal. Chem.](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.09.11.293092v1); [Wandy et al. 2022, ViMMS 2.0, JOSS](https://joss.theoj.org/papers/10.21105/joss.03990); [ViMMS simulator (MIT)](https://github.com/glasgowcompbio/vimms); [Wandy et al. 2023, Simulated-to-real benchmarking of acquisition methods in untargeted metabolomics, Front. Mol. Biosci.](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/molecular-biosciences/articles/10.3389/fmolb.2023.1130781/full)
topics.baseline: TopN with dynamic exclusion, and the grid-search-tuned SmartROI and WeightedDEW heuristics
topics.angle: policy gradient on per-scan fragmentation decisions in the simulator; offline RL or model-based lookahead from replayed real runs

control.state: Current MS1 peaks, previously fragmented compounds, exclusion timers and chromatographic time.
control.action: Select the next precursor for fragmentation and update the allowed exclusion decision.
control.dynamics: Compounds elute and disappear; fragmentation consumes scan time and changes later eligibility and information.
control.objective: Identify many distinct compounds within instrument scan-cycle and fragmentation constraints.

topics.title: STM single-atom manipulation
topics.problem: For each manipulation attempt in an episode of up to five moves, choose the bias voltage, tunneling conductance and tip start and end positions that drag an adatom toward a target site, under an unobserved tip condition that changes the response, to maximize the rate of placements within a/√3 (about 0.58 lattice spacings) of the target.
topics.hook: The fixed-parameter routine succeeded 100%, 92% and 68% of the time under three tip conditions, while the RL agent adapted and then built a 42-atom kagome lattice in 66 manipulations. The logged manipulations are public, so model-based and offline variants can be tested without an STM.
topics.start: [Chen et al. 2022, Precise atom manipulation through deep reinforcement learning, Nat. Commun.](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-35149-w); [code, logged training data and trained networks](https://github.com/SINGROUP/Atom_manipulation_with_RL)
topics.baseline: hand-tuned fixed parameters (10 mV, 6 µA/V, tip moved 0.1 nm past the target)
topics.angle: fit a stochastic dynamics model to the logged manipulations and plan with it (model-based RL, MPC), or offline RL compared with the published SAC agent

control.state: Beliefs about atom position and tip condition from images and previous manipulation outcomes.
control.action: Choose the next tip trajectory, bias and conductance settings.
control.dynamics: Manipulation can move the atom and alter the hidden tip response, changing the next move's success probability.
control.objective: Place the atom at its target within a small move budget and feasible manipulation settings.

topics.title: Adaptive sampling for protein folding MD
topics.problem: At each epoch of a molecular-dynamics campaign, choose which conformational states to restart a batch of trajectories from, given a Markov state model fit to the data so far and a fixed GPU budget, to reach the folded state and converge the kinetics with the fewest simulated nanoseconds.
topics.hook: Folding and binding happen on timescales far longer than a single trajectory, so where simulations are restarted decides whether a GPU budget ever sees these events. HTMD ships both the count-based and bandit strategies as baselines, plus a villin folding setup.
topics.start: [Pérez et al. 2020, AdaptiveBandit: A multi-armed bandit framework for adaptive sampling in molecular simulations, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.12582); [HTMD AdaptiveBandit tutorial on villin folding](https://software.acellera.com/htmd/tutorials/adaptive-bandit.html); [HTMD code (Community Edition, free for not-for-profit use)](https://github.com/Acellera/htmd)
topics.baseline: count-based MSM respawning (HTMD AdaptiveMD) and the UCB AdaptiveBandit
topics.angle: plan respawns over several epochs with the current MSM as a learned model (lookahead, MPC) instead of one-step bandit scores

control.state: Observed conformations, transition-model beliefs, running trajectories and remaining simulation budget.
control.action: Choose conformations from which to launch the next molecular-dynamics trajectories.
control.dynamics: Each trajectory consumes compute and reveals transitions that affect the value of future starting states.
control.objective: Reach rare states or improve kinetic estimates within fixed GPU-time and parallel-trajectory limits.

topics.title: Tokamak ramp-up
topics.problem: Tokamak ramp-up control in Gym-TORAX (ITER hybrid scenario)
topics.hook: A fusion plasma must be shaped carefully as its current ramps up. TORAX is differentiable, so you can optimize trajectories through the simulator itself.
topics.start: [Gym-TORAX, Mouchamps et al. 2025](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11283v1); [TORAX, Citrin et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.06718); [gymtorax](https://github.com/antoine-mouchamps/gymtorax)
topics.baseline: Open-loop reference and PI
topics.angle: gradient-based trajectory optimization through the differentiable JAX simulator, MPC with a reduced model, then amortize

control.state: Estimated plasma current, pressure and temperature profiles and actuator state.
control.action: Schedule the modeled heating and current-control inputs through the ramp-up.
control.dynamics: Current diffusion and thermal dynamics carry the effects of early heating into later confinement conditions.
control.objective: Reach the desired operating scenario while respecting plasma-state and actuator constraints throughout the ramp.

topics.title: Tokamak ramp-down
topics.problem: Robust tokamak ramp-down trajectory design with a learned plasma model
topics.hook: Disruptions during ramp-down can damage a reactor. Learn a plasma model, then design ramp-downs that stay safe under uncertainty.
topics.start: [Wang et al. 2024, ramp-downs with neural differential equations and RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09387); [Wang et al. 2025, predict-first experiments at TCV](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.12327); [DisruptionPy](https://github.com/MIT-PSFC/disruption-py) for open MAST data
topics.baseline: Hand-designed feed-forward ramp
topics.angle: neural state-space fit, constrained trajectory optimization under sampled parameters (robust MPC) vs constraint-conditioned RL

control.state: Plasma energy and current profiles, evolving stability indicators and available actuator headroom.
control.action: Choose heating and current-ramp commands during shutdown.
control.dynamics: Cooling and current decay alter later stability margins and the trajectories still reachable safely.
control.objective: Complete shutdown efficiently while limiting modeled disruption risk and respecting actuator and plasma-state limits.

topics.title: Particle accelerator tuning
topics.problem: Transverse beam tuning in a linac section with a differentiable accelerator simulator
topics.hook: Physicists spend hours tuning magnets by hand. A differentiable accelerator simulator makes model-based tuning possible.
topics.start: [Kaiser et al. 2022, ICML](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/kaiser22a.html); [Kaiser et al. 2023, RL vs Bayesian optimisation for online tuning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.03739); [Cheetah](https://github.com/desy-ml/cheetah), [rl-vs-bo](https://github.com/desy-ml/rl-vs-bo)
topics.baseline: Nelder-Mead and Bayesian optimisation
topics.angle: compare an RL-trained tuning policy with model-based belief-space planning over a fixed measurement budget. Infer hidden misalignments from beam images and previous adjustments; score final beam error and measurements used against Bayesian optimization
topics.scope: The sequential state includes unknown machine parameters, magnet settings and remaining measurements. A differentiable static beam map enables prediction but does not itself provide time-domain dynamics; lookahead must account for information gained by future measurements.

control.state: Current magnet settings, beam images, beliefs about hidden misalignments and remaining measurement budget.
control.action: Choose successive magnet adjustments and decide when to stop tuning.
control.dynamics: Adjustments consume measurements and travel; beam observations update hidden-parameter beliefs used for later settings.
control.objective: Reach the target beam with few measurements within magnet bounds, accounting for partial observability.

topics.title: Fermilab Booster regulation
topics.problem: Gradient-magnet power-supply regulation at the Fermilab Booster from logged data
topics.hook: One day of real control data from a Fermilab accelerator, and no simulator. Honest offline evaluation is the whole project.
topics.start: [St. John et al. 2021, real-time AI for accelerator control](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.07371); [BOOSTR dataset, Kafkes and St. John 2021](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.08359), [data on Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/record/4088982)
topics.baseline: The existing regulator visible in the logs
topics.angle: learned dynamics + MPC, or offline RL with off-policy evaluation; purely offline, so evaluation honesty is the project

control.state: Recent current-tracking errors, previous supply commands and observed cycle disturbances.
control.action: Set the power-supply compensation for the next accelerator cycle.
control.dynamics: Supply response and recurring disturbances carry information and control effects across cycles.
control.objective: Reduce cumulative current-tracking error within feasible compensation magnitudes and changes between cycles.

topics.title: Adaptive optics for exoplanets
topics.problem: Predictive adaptive-optics control for exoplanet imaging
topics.hook: Imaging planets around other stars needs mirrors that reshape about a thousand times a second to cancel the atmosphere. Predicting beats reacting.
topics.start: [Nousiainen et al. 2022, towards on-sky AO control with RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.07554); [Nousiainen et al. 2023, laboratory experiments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.00242); [OOPAO](https://github.com/cheritier/OOPAO)
topics.baseline: Integrator with a static reconstructor
topics.angle: learned temporal dynamics of the modes, predictive MPC or LQG; test under wind-speed changes

control.state: Estimated wavefront modes, previous mirror commands and beliefs about atmospheric temporal evolution.
control.action: Command deformable-mirror actuators at each feedback frame.
control.dynamics: Atmospheric turbulence evolves during sensing and actuation delays; commands affect later residual wavefronts.
control.objective: Minimize residual phase or image degradation while respecting mirror stroke and command-rate constraints.

topics.title: Cryogenic helium plant
topics.problem: Helium cryogenic refrigerator under pulsed heat loads
topics.hook: Superconducting magnets need helium at 4.5 K or colder. Pulsed heat loads from the machine test the refrigerator's controller.
topics.start: [Alamir et al. 2017, hierarchical MPC for a cryogenic refrigerator](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.08813); [Noga and de Prada 2008, LHC superfluid helium circuit model](https://www.msc-les.org/proceedings/emss/2008/EMSS2008_806.pdf)
topics.baseline: PID loops
topics.angle: learned residual model + hierarchical MPC with forecasting of pulsed loads; no open simulator, so modelling is most of the work

control.state: Helium temperatures, pressures and fluid inventories, with observed refrigeration load.
control.action: Set valves and compressor or other available plant references over successive intervals.
control.dynamics: Thermal inertia and fluid transport delay the effects of valve and compressor changes.
control.objective: Maintain cryogenic service with low energy use while respecting pressure, temperature and actuator limits.

topics.title: Depth of anesthesia
topics.problem: Depth-of-anesthesia control: propofol and remifentanil infusion rates to hold BIS in 40 to 60 and blood pressure in range, under surgical stimulation and patient variability
topics.hook: Anesthesiologists titrate drugs while watching a brain-activity index. Closed-loop control on a pharmacological model, tested on many virtual patients.
topics.start: [Schamberg et al. 2020, titrating propofol with deep RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.12333); [Python Anesthesia Simulator](https://github.com/AnesthesiaSimulation/Python_Anesthesia_Simulator) ([JOSS 2023](https://joss.theoj.org/papers/10.21105/joss.05480))
topics.baseline: PID or target-controlled infusion
topics.angle: nonlinear MPC on the PK/PD model with online patient-parameter estimation, then amortize into a policy; evaluate across sampled virtual patients

control.state: Estimated pharmacokinetic and effect-site states from BIS, blood-pressure and dosing history.
control.action: Choose infusion rates at successive virtual-patient control intervals.
control.dynamics: Drug accumulation and delayed effect-site response make each dose influence later sedation and hemodynamics.
control.objective: Maintain target anesthesia in simulation while limiting hypotension, excessive dosing and infusion-rate changes.

topics.title: Mechanical ventilation
topics.problem: Pressure-controlled mechanical ventilation: valve opening every 30 ms to track a pressure waveform across lungs with unknown resistance and compliance
topics.hook: A ventilator must deliver the right pressure to lungs it has never seen. Learn the lung from recorded breaths, then control through that model.
topics.start: [Suo et al. 2021, machine learning for mechanical ventilation control](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.06779); lung simulator in [deluca](https://github.com/google/deluca); [Kaggle ventilator dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/ventilator-pressure-prediction)
topics.baseline: PID per lung
topics.angle: identify a lung model from recorded breaths, then MPC or iLQR through it; test on unseen lungs

control.state: Airway pressure and flow, estimated lung mechanics and current breath phase.
control.action: Choose valve opening at each short control step in the ventilation model.
control.dynamics: Airway and lung dynamics retain pressure and volume, coupling commands within and across breaths.
control.objective: Track the prescribed pressure waveform while respecting pressure, flow and actuator limits.

topics.title: Sepsis treatment from ICU logs
topics.problem: Sepsis fluids and vasopressors from ICU logs (offline RL)
topics.hook: Sepsis is a leading cause of death in hospitals. Learning a treatment policy from logs alone is offline RL at its purest, and its riskiest.
topics.start: [Komorowski et al. 2018, The AI Clinician, Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-018-0213-5); [Tang and Wiens 2021, model selection for offline RL in healthcare](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.11003); [MIMIC-IV](https://physionet.org/content/mimiciv/) (credentialing takes 1 to 3 weeks); small [sepsis simulator](https://github.com/clinicalml/gumbel-max-scm) for sanity checks
topics.baseline: Clinician policy and a fixed protocol
topics.angle: fitted Q iteration or conservative offline RL with off-policy evaluation validated on the simulator first

control.state: Observed physiology and treatment history, with uncertainty about latent severity and confounding.
control.action: Select discretized fluid and vasopressor actions at each modeled treatment interval.
control.dynamics: Patient-state transitions and cumulative treatment effects change later outcomes; factual logs do not reveal alternative-action outcomes.
control.objective: Compare long-horizon outcome and treatment-burden objectives within supported action ranges, with explicit causal and evaluation assumptions.

topics.title: Adaptive radiotherapy
topics.problem: Adaptive radiotherapy fractionation: today's dose given observed tumour and organ positions and repopulation
topics.hook: Radiation is delivered over many sessions while the tumour moves. Exact DP gives the ground truth to measure a learned policy against.
topics.start: [Ramakrishnan et al. 2011, a DP approach to adaptive fractionation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.4524); [Bortfeld et al. 2015, fractionation with tumour repopulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.1332)
topics.baseline: Uniform fractionation
topics.angle: exact DP as ground truth, then a learned policy with model parameters estimated online

control.state: Estimated tumor and organ states, remaining dose budget and observed anatomical changes.
control.action: Choose the next fraction's dose using information available before that fraction.
control.dynamics: Dose accumulates in tissue; tumor response and organ injury alter the value and feasibility of later fractions.
control.objective: Improve modeled tumor control while respecting cumulative organ-dose and fractionation constraints.
