topics.title: HIV treatment interruption
topics.problem: Benchmark treatment on-off scheduling in the published HIV infection ODE, using simulated patient trajectories and batch-RL or model-based control.
topics.hook: The published infection model is a compact benchmark for learning from logged treatment trajectories: earlier treatment changes viral and immune states, altering the value of later decisions.
topics.start: [Ernst et al. 2006, clinical-data-based STI strategies, CDC](https://orbi.uliege.be/handle/2268/13367); ODE in [rlpy HIVTreatment](https://github.com/rlpy/rlpy/blob/master/rlpy/Domains/HIVTreatment.py)
topics.baseline: Fixed schedules
topics.angle: generate batch trajectories from declared behavior policies, then compare fitted Q iteration with a learned ODE and MPC on held-out simulated patient parameters. Report full-trajectory infection, immune-state and treatment-burden outcomes
topics.scope: The linked RLPy resource is a simulated infection model, not a released clinical treatment dataset. Conclusions concern that model and its parameter sensitivity.

control.state: Viral and immune-cell states, treatment status and observation history in the published infection model.
control.action: Choose whether treatment is active at successive modeled review times.
control.dynamics: Viral and immune dynamics carry treatment effects forward; stopping changes later rebound and recovery.
control.objective: Suppress modeled infection and preserve immune function with low treatment burden within the benchmark action schedule.

topics.title: Warfarin dosing
topics.problem: Warfarin dose titration to an INR target
topics.hook: Warfarin is a common blood thinner with a narrow safe range. Dosing with delayed lab results is a partially observed control problem.
topics.start: [Anzabi Zadeh et al. 2022, warfarin dosing with deep RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.03486v2); [hemosim](https://pypi.org/project/hemosim/) environments
topics.baseline: Clinical nomograms
topics.angle: PK/PD model with Bayesian parameter estimation and MPC, including the delayed-measurement variant

control.state: Beliefs about patient drug-response states from INR measurements and dose history.
control.action: Choose the next dose after each scheduled INR observation in a patient model.
control.dynamics: Drug accumulation and delayed coagulation response make today's dose influence INR at later visits.
control.objective: Keep modeled INR in range while limiting dose variability and excessive anticoagulation risk.

topics.title: Deep brain stimulation
topics.problem: Closed-loop deep brain stimulation: desynchronize a neural population with minimal stimulation energy
topics.hook: Closed-loop stimulation could treat Parkinson's symptoms with less energy and fewer side effects. A model neural population is the testbed.
topics.start: [Krylov et al. 2020, RL framework for DBS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10948); [RL-DBS environment](https://github.com/cviaai/RL-DBS)
topics.baseline: Open-loop high-frequency stimulation and delayed feedback
topics.angle: reduced phase or Koopman model + MPC

control.state: Estimated neural phase and synchronization from observed neural signals and previous stimulation.
control.action: Choose stimulation amplitude and timing at successive feedback opportunities.
control.dynamics: Neuronal dynamics and entrainment propagate the effects of stimulation into later network synchronization.
control.objective: Suppress pathological synchronization in simulation with low stimulation energy within amplitude and timing limits.

topics.title: Ambulance redeployment with ADP
topics.problem: Each time an ambulance becomes free, decide which base to send it to (and optionally move other idle units), under random call arrival times, locations and service durations, to maximize the fraction of calls reached within the response-time target with a fixed fleet and set of bases.
topics.hook: The move-up decision recurs after every call and directly sets how many calls are reached in time. JEMSS ships a Manhattan model you can calibrate with NYC's public dispatch file, which logs call creation, assignment, on-scene and hospital arrival times per incident by dispatch area.
topics.start: [Maxwell, Restrepo, Henderson & Topaloglu 2010, ADP for ambulance redeployment, INFORMS J. Computing](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/fpi/10.1287/ijoc.1090.0345); [JEMSS.jl EMS simulator with Auckland, Edmonton, Manhattan and Utrecht models](https://github.com/uoa-ems-research/JEMSS.jl); [NYC EMS incident dispatch data](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Public-Safety/EMS-Incident-Dispatch-Data/76xm-jjuj); [Guigues et al. 2024, EMS management tools with Rio de Janeiro SAMU call history](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.09154) and [their dispatch/relocation heuristics code](https://github.com/vguigues/Heuristics_Dynamic_Ambulance_Management)
topics.baseline: static policy that returns each ambulance to its home base (the paper's static benchmarks)
topics.angle: value-function ADP over the ambulance configuration with basis functions tuned by simulation; compare to PPO or a short-horizon MPC lookahead in the simulator

control.state: Ambulance locations, busy and return times and beliefs about spatial call arrivals.
control.action: Reposition available ambulances to bases as calls and service completions occur.
control.dynamics: Travel and emergency assignments remove units from coverage and determine availability for later calls.
control.objective: Reduce response times and missed coverage over the shift within fleet and relocation constraints.

topics.title: Hospital platelet ordering
topics.problem: Each day, decide how many platelet units to order given stock by remaining shelf life and orders in transit, under uncertain daily demand, to minimize expected outdating, shortage and holding cost with delivery lead times and a shelf life of a few days.
topics.hook: Platelets keep only three to seven days, so hospitals both discard units and run short. At RWTH Aachen University Hospital historical outdating was about 10.1% and shortage about 6.5%, and forecast-driven ordering roughly halved both in retrospective simulation; viso_jax lets you check any learned policy against the exact optimum.
topics.start: [Farrington, Li, Wong & Utley 2023, GPU value iteration for perishable inventory (arXiv)](https://www.arxiv.org/abs/2303.10672); [viso_jax code, Scenario C = hospital platelets after Mirjalili 2022](https://github.com/joefarrington/viso_jax); [Schilling et al. 2022, forecast-driven platelet ordering at RWTH Aachen, JMIR Med. Inform.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8848235)
topics.baseline: order-up-to policy fitted by simulation optimization, with exact value iteration as the reference optimum
topics.angle: decision-focused training of the demand forecaster on ordering cost instead of MAPE; amortize the value-iteration policy or train PPO and measure the gap to the exact optimum

control.state: Platelet inventory by age, outstanding orders and forecasts of transfusion demand.
control.action: Choose daily order quantities under the specified delivery schedule.
control.dynamics: Deliveries arrive after lead times; unused units age and expire, changing later stock availability.
control.objective: Balance shortage, expiry and holding costs within storage, shelf-life and order constraints.

topics.title: Dynamic kidney exchange: match or wait
topics.problem: At each match run, choose which cycles and chains of incompatible patient-donor pairs and altruistic donors to execute now versus keep in the pool, under random arrivals, departures and failed matches, to maximize (quality-weighted) transplants over the horizon subject to cycle and chain length caps.
topics.hook: Executing every cycle available today can consume pairs that would have formed better cycles after the next arrivals, while waiting risks patients leaving the pool. kep_solver includes a dynamic simulator and a published UK NHS 2022 generator, so the trade-off can be tested end to end with an exact IP inside the loop.
topics.start: [Dickerson & Sandholm 2015, FutureMatch: learning to match in dynamic kidney exchange, AAAI](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/9239); [Barkel et al. 2025, survey and empirical evaluation of kidney exchange models with open instances](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.04091); [kep_solver API: DynamicGenerator, DynamicSimulation, uk_nhs_generator2022](https://kep-solver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/source/kep_solver.html); [kep_solver on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/kep-solver/)
topics.baseline: myopic maximum-transplant matching at every run
topics.angle: learn vertex/pair potentials (a value function) that reweight the matching IP, tuned by policy gradient in the dynamic simulator; optionally learn when to run a match

control.state: Current compatibility graph, pair waiting times and beliefs about arrivals and dropout.
control.action: Execute feasible exchange cycles or chains now, or wait for future arrivals.
control.dynamics: Matching removes pairs; waiting may create better matches but also loses pairs through dropout.
control.objective: Maximize transplants over the horizon while respecting compatibility, chain-length and waiting-risk constraints.

topics.title: Inpatient overflow to off-service wards
topics.problem: Throughout the day, decide which waiting inpatients to place in a nonprimary (overflow) ward instead of waiting for a bed in their primary ward, under time-varying random admissions and discharges, to minimize long-run average waiting cost plus overflow penalties with fixed ward capacities.
topics.hook: Bed managers make this call every hour. In the paper's baseline scenario the ADP policy matched complete bed sharing on congestion with 20% less overflow, and the PPO follow-up scaled to 20 wards with about 25% lower cost than night-time-only practice.
topics.start: [Dai & Shi 2019, Inpatient overflow: an ADP approach, MSOM](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/suppl/10.1287/msom.2018.0730); [Sun, Shi & Dai 2024, Inpatient overflow management with PPO (arXiv)](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.13767v4); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: night-time-only overflow (current practice), complete overflow, and the Dai and Shi ADP policy
topics.angle: basis-function ADP from a fluid/single-pool approximation versus PPO on the multiclass multipool queue

control.state: Ward occupancy, patient queues by specialty and estimated remaining lengths of stay.
control.action: Place a patient in the preferred ward, use an off-service bed or continue waiting.
control.dynamics: Admissions occupy beds for uncertain durations and change the capacity available for later patients.
control.objective: Reduce waiting and off-service penalties while meeting bed-capacity and placement constraints.

topics.title: Tuning deceased-donor allocation rules
topics.problem: Choose the parameters of the deceased-donor kidney allocation rule (point weights on HLA match, waiting time, vPRA, donor-candidate age matching) that rank candidates for each donor, under random donor and candidate arrivals, offer acceptance and waitlist removal, to improve transplant outcomes and equity across groups and countries within Eurotransplant's balance rules.
topics.hook: Eurotransplant allocates organs across eight countries, and these simulators were built with its physicians and advisory committees to evaluate rule changes; ETKidney reproduces the current kidney rules, was validated on 2021 to 2024 outcomes, and exposes point weights in YAML. The shipped synthetic data is for trying the code only; research-grade conclusions need a study proposal to Eurotransplant.
topics.start: [de Ferrante et al. 2025, ETKidney discrete event simulator for Eurotransplant (arXiv)](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.15001v1); [ETKidney code with synthetic data](https://github.com/hansdeferrante/Eurotransplant_ETKidney_simulator); [de Ferrante et al., ELAS liver allocation simulator (arXiv)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10840); [ELAS code with synthetic data](http://github.com/hansdeferrante/Eurotransplant_ELAS_simulator)
topics.baseline: Eurotransplant's current ETKAS/ESP point system
topics.angle: black-box policy optimization (policy gradient or evolution strategies) over point weights, with a learned surrogate of simulator outcomes to cut simulation cost

control.state: Waiting-list composition, waiting times and historical allocation or fairness counters in the allocation simulator.
control.action: Choose allocation-rule weights whose rankings determine each successive donor assignment.
control.dynamics: Transplants remove recipients; arrivals, deterioration and deaths change later rankings and long-horizon equity outcomes.
control.objective: Improve simulated health benefit subject to allocation and equity requirements across the full donor stream.

topics.title: Week-by-week nurse rostering
topics.problem: Each week, assign shifts and skills to nurses knowing only that week's coverage requirements and requests while later weeks are unknown, to minimize the weighted soft-constraint penalty over a 4- or 8-week horizon subject to hard single-assignment, minimum-coverage, shift-succession and skill constraints.
topics.hook: A weekly solver has to decide how much of each nurse's total-shift and weekend quota to spend before seeing next week's demand, which is a value-function question. INRC-II gives 14 datasets (30 to 120 nurses, 4 or 8 weeks) with a stage-by-stage simulator and a validator.
topics.start: [Ceschia, Dang, De Causmaecker, Haspeslagh & Schaerf 2015, INRC-II problem description (arXiv)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.04177); [INRC-II datasets](https://mobiz.vives.be/inrc2/?page_id=20); [INRC-II simulator, validator and benchmark tools](https://mobiz.vives.be/inrc2/?page_id=245); [Kim & Mehrotra 2015, two-stage stochastic nurse staffing on Northwestern Memorial data, Operations Research](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/fpi/10.1287/opre.2015.1421)
topics.baseline: myopic weekly optimization that ignores future weeks
topics.angle: learn a value function of the end-of-week history (work and weekend counters, last shifts) and add it as a terminal cost to the weekly MIP or local search

control.state: Previous shifts, cumulative assignments and used weekends for each nurse, with current-week requirements.
control.action: Choose each week's nurse-shift assignments using available demand information.
control.dynamics: Assignments update counters and rest obligations, restricting feasible rosters in later weeks.
control.objective: Cover the full horizon with low preference and fairness penalties while satisfying hard staffing and rest rules.

topics.title: Hurricane relief pre-positioning
topics.problem: Every 12 hours before landfall, decide how much relief to produce at each distribution center, how much to ship to each shelter and whether to activate contingency capacity, under a Markov-chain forecast of hurricane track and intensity, to minimize logistics cost plus unmet-demand penalties within capacity limits.
topics.hook: Supplies must be produced and moved while landfall is still a moving forecast. The appendix lists the full South Carolina case: seven distribution centers, seven county shelters, 12-hour stages to landfall at period 11, and the cost parameters.
topics.start: [Castro, Bodur & Song, Markov chain-based policies for multistage stochastic integer programs with disaster relief, MSOM](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/fpi/10.1287/msom.2023.0658); [arXiv version](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.14779); [online appendix with the synthetic generator and the Hurricane Florence / South Carolina instance](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/suppl/10.1287/msom.2023.0658/suppl_file/msom.2023.0658.sm1.pdf); [NHC forecast verification and error database](https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/verification/); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: static two-stage plan or rolling two-stage re-solve, with the paper's linear decision rule as the strong baseline
topics.angle: MPC with a hurricane-state model fitted to NHC forecast errors; amortize the multistage solve into a neural policy and compare to the linear decision rule

control.state: Stocks, shipments in transit, facility readiness and updated storm and demand forecasts.
control.action: Produce, move and pre-position relief supplies at successive forecast updates.
control.dynamics: Transport lead times and facility commitments carry forward; landfall changes access and revealed needs.
control.objective: Reduce logistics and unmet-need costs within budgets, vehicle capacity and time-to-landfall constraints.

topics.title: Elective surgery booking with ward beds
topics.problem: Each day, decide how many waiting elective patients of each specialty to book into future OR days of a master surgical schedule, under random referrals, surgery durations and post-operative lengths of stay, to minimize waits beyond target, OR overtime and ward overcapacity.
topics.hook: Booking a surgery commits OR time on one day and a ward bed for the days after, so wait time, overtime and ward congestion trade off. The Zenodo file gives fitted duration distributions from 2,035,126 surgeries at 212 German hospitals to drive the simulator.
topics.start: [Astaraky & Patrick 2015, simulation-based ADP for multi-class, multi-resource surgical scheduling, EJOR](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/ejores/v245y2015i1p309-319.html); [Astaraky thesis, uOttawa](https://ruor.uottawa.ca/items/449f9534-f933-4c5a-a698-6459c0265f0c); [German surgical case mix and duration distributions (Zenodo, CC BY 4.0)](https://zenodo.org/record/7147921); [Leeftink & Hans OR scheduling benchmark and instance generator](https://www.utwente.nl/en/choir/research/benchmark-orscheduling/); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: first-come first-served booking into the earliest day with free OR time
topics.angle: least-squares approximate policy iteration as in the paper versus PPO, with a sampled-scenario MPC lookahead as a strong baseline
topics.venture: Hospitals, which pay for fuller operating rooms and fewer cancellations caused by missing beds.

control.state: Waiting lists, operating-room commitments, ward occupancy and length-of-stay forecasts.
control.action: Book numbers or groups of elective surgeries for successive future operating days.
control.dynamics: Surgery consumes room time and creates ward-bed demand that persists across later days.
control.objective: Reduce waiting and overtime while respecting operating-room capacity and downstream bed availability.

topics.title: Polling-place resources to cut wait times
topics.problem: Before and during election day, decide how a fixed pool of check-in stations, voting booths and floating poll workers is split across a county's polling places (and moved hour by hour), under uncertain turnout, arrival peaks and service times, to minimize the worst-place (or 99th-percentile) wait subject to the 30-minute standard and fixed equipment and staff.
topics.hook: In 2024, 11% of Election Day voters and 15% of early voters waited more than 30 minutes (SPAE). In central Florida in 2012, reallocating the same booths was estimated to cut the average wait from 49.2 to 39.0 minutes.
topics.start: [Allen, Yang, Huang, Hernandez 2020, Determining resource requirements for elections using indifference-zone generalized binary search, Computers & Industrial Engineering](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10134950); [Li, Allen, Akah 2013, Could simulation optimization have prevented 2012 Central Florida election lines?, Winter Simulation Conference](https://informs-sim.org/wsc13papers/includes/files/183.pdf); [Stewart 2015, Managing Polling Place Resources, Caltech/MIT Voting Technology Project](https://vote.caltech.edu/documents/152/Managing_Polling_Place_Resources.pdf); [BPC/Stewart hourly line-count program](https://bipartisanpolicy.org/votinglines); [SPAE 2024 survey data, CC0](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/GWBAP5); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: booths allocated in proportion to eligible voters, with no moves during the day
topics.angle: simulation-based optimization or an amortized policy mapping turnout forecasts to a minimax-wait allocation; MPC that moves floating poll workers using hourly line counts

control.state: Polling-place queues, staff positions and available booths, with turnout-arrival estimates.
control.action: Reassign movable workers and choose permitted resource deployment as election day unfolds.
control.dynamics: Queues accumulate; reassignment takes travel time and temporarily reduces service at the origin.
control.objective: Reduce long and unequal voter waits under fixed staffing, booth and relocation constraints.

topics.title: Adaptive sampling for risk-limiting audits
topics.problem: After an election, decide one draw at a time which stratum or batch of paper ballots to sample next and how much to bet on each observation, under uncertainty about the true vote shares and tabulation errors, to stop as early as possible while keeping the chance of confirming a wrong outcome below the risk limit, falling back to a full hand count otherwise.
topics.hook: Spertus and Stark found that a better stratum-allocation rule cut expected workload from 752 to 271 cards in one setting, and they leave optimal allocation as open future work. That makes this a clean sequential-design problem with real open-source audit code.
topics.start: [Stark 2020, SHANGRLA: sets of half-average nulls generate risk-limiting audits, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.10035); [Stark 2022, ALPHA: audit that learns from previously hand-audited ballots, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.02707); [Spertus & Stark 2022, Sweeter than SUITE: supermartingale stratified union-intersection tests of elections, E-Vote-ID](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.03379); [Spertus, Sridhar, Stark, Sequential stratified inference for the mean, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.06680); [Waudby-Smith, Stark, Ramdas 2021, RiLACS, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.11323); [SHANGRLA code](https://github.com/pbstark/SHANGRLA); [RiLACS code](https://github.com/WannabeSmith/RiLACS); [Arlo audit software](https://github.com/votingworks/arlo)
topics.baseline: ALPHA or BRAVO with a fixed betting rule and proportional or round-robin stratum sampling
topics.angle: treat the bet size and next-stratum choice as a predictable policy trained by DP or RL on simulated elections; anytime validity holds by construction, so only expected sample size is optimized

control.state: Audit sufficient statistics, current evidence, sampled ballots and remaining stratum sizes.
control.action: Choose the next sampling allocation and predictable test settings, or stop with a valid outcome.
control.dynamics: New ballots update evidence and future sampling value; stopping is irreversible and must preserve statistical validity.
control.objective: Minimize expected audit workload while maintaining the specified risk limit under adaptive sampling and stopping.

topics.title: Audit budgets against municipal corruption
topics.problem: Each year, decide which of several thousand municipalities (or federally funded programs) a national audit agency inspects with a fixed audit budget, under uncertainty about each one's irregularity rate and how audits deter future misuse, to maximize misused funds detected and prevented while keeping an unbiased national estimate of irregularity.
topics.hook: In a CGU randomized evaluation, raising annual audit risk from about 5% to 25% cut the share of procurement processes with evidence of corruption by about 15 percentage points, and a past audit lowers future corruption by about 8%. CGU has since moved from lottery to risk-matrix and machine-learning selection, which makes the detect, deter and estimate trade-off a live policy question.
topics.start: [Litschig & Zamboni 2018, Audit risk and rent extraction: evidence from a randomized evaluation in Brazil, BSE Working Paper 554](https://bse.eu/sites/default/files/working_paper_pdfs/554_0.pdf); [Avis, Ferraz, Finan 2018, Do government audits reduce corruption?, Journal of Political Economy (NBER w22443)](https://www.nber.org/papers/w22443); [Henderson et al. 2023, Integrating reward maximization and population estimation: sequential decision-making for IRS audit selection, AAAI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.11910); [CGU note on its audit-selection cycles](https://www.gov.br/cgu/pt-br/acesso-a-informacao/dados-abertos/arquivos/fiscalizacao-em-entes-federativos); [OpenTender procurement data (OCDS), optional contract-level covariates](https://data.open-contracting.org/en/publication/87); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: uniform public lottery at about 5% audit probability per year (CGU's original program), or greedy ranking by predicted risk
topics.angle: restless bandit or POMDP where audits both reveal and deter; learn a randomized index policy whose inclusion probabilities keep the inverse-propensity estimate of national irregularity unbiased

control.state: Municipal risk beliefs, past audit findings, selection probabilities and remaining audit capacity.
control.action: Choose randomized audit allocations in successive rounds.
control.dynamics: Findings update risk estimates; spending reduces later capacity and modeled deterrence changes subsequent behavior.
control.objective: Improve detection and prevention under budget and coverage limits while retaining valid population-level estimates.

topics.title: Dynamic refugee placement under capacity
topics.problem: As refugee cases arrive in weekly batches over a fiscal year, assign each family to a local affiliate or locality, under uncertainty about the future arrival mix and employment outcomes, to maximize expected employment subject to annual capacities, indivisible families, even allocation over time and group-fairness constraints.
topics.hook: Ahani et al. report over 98% of hindsight-optimal employment against under 90% for greedy-like approaches, and their algorithm runs inside the Annie MOORE software at a US resettlement agency. Bansak and Paulson report 40 to 50% gains over the status quo on US and Swiss data.
topics.start: [Bansak & Paulson, Outcome-driven dynamic refugee assignment with allocation balancing, Operations Research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.03069); [Ahani, Gölz, Procaccia, Teytelboym, Trapp 2021, Dynamic placement in refugee resettlement, ACM EC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.14388); [Freund, Lykouris, Paulson, Sturt, Weng, Group fairness in dynamic refugee assignment, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.10642); [Trapp et al., Placement optimization in refugee resettlement (Annie MOORE), Lund WP](https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid:ac6d7b8d-203e-4fd8-9bb7-cf9f8735bb87/files/s9593tv441); [US refugee arrivals by state, nationality and month](https://www.rpc.state.gov/admissions-and-arrivals/); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: greedy, status-quo-like placement, compared with the papers' minimum-discord and two-stage stochastic programming policies
topics.angle: online assignment as an MDP; learn or amortize bid prices from sampled future arrivals and compare with re-solving MPC, with fairness and balance constraints

control.state: Remaining locality capacities, household features, previous placements and beliefs about future arrivals.
control.action: Assign each arriving household to an eligible locality.
control.dynamics: Placements consume capacity irreversibly, changing the employment and fairness opportunities available to later households.
control.objective: Improve expected employment across the arrival horizon while respecting capacity, eligibility and fairness constraints.

topics.title: Landmine survey and clearance prioritization
topics.problem: Each quarter, decide which municipalities or suspected hazardous areas receive a limited number of survey and clearance teams, under uncertainty about where contamination remains (revealed only by survey, clearance or accidents), to minimize expected civilian accidents and maximize land released within a team-time budget.
topics.hook: Colombia's open registry lists 39,171 mine-related events in 774 municipalities from 1990 to 2023, including 7,299 accidents. RELand cut the mean number of empty cells visited before a region is cleared from about 227 to 132 compared with the previous risk model.
topics.start: [Dulce Rubio et al. 2023, RELand: risk estimation of landmines via interpretable invariant risk minimization, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.03115); [CMU ML blog on RELand, prioritization as a budgeted knapsack](https://blog.ml.cmu.edu/2024/11/07/identification-of-hazardous-areas-for-priority-landmine-clearance-ai-for-humanitarian-mine-action); [Kischelewski, Guedj, Wahl 2025, RestoreAI: pattern-based risk estimation of remaining explosives (virtual demining environment), arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.19873); [Colombia landmine events 1990 to 2023 by municipality, datos.gov.co, CC BY-SA 4.0](https://www.datos.gov.co/d/sgp4-3e6k); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: rank areas by historical event density or a static risk score and clear greedily within budget
topics.angle: Bayesian POMDP or bandit over municipal contamination with team-allocation actions; extension to tile-level adaptive search in a rebuilt virtual minefield

control.state: Contamination beliefs by area, previous survey results, available teams and remaining funds.
control.action: Assign survey or clearance teams to the next areas.
control.dynamics: Surveys reveal contamination; clearance removes modeled hazards and changes the future value of nearby work.
control.objective: Release useful land and reduce modeled risk within clearance budgets, team capacity and access constraints.

topics.title: Scheduling fact-checks on crowd flags
topics.problem: In continuous time over hours to days, decide which crowd-flagged stories to send to a limited pool of independent fact checkers and when, under uncertain spread (reshare point processes) and noisy flags, to minimize users exposed to stories later found false subject to a fact-checking rate budget.
topics.hook: Platforms send crowd-flagged stories to a small pool of third-party fact checkers, so the order of checks matters. Curb's public code and cascades let a student test a learned scheduler against a published optimal-control policy within the first week.
topics.start: [Kim, Tabibian, Oh, Schölkopf, Gomez-Rodriguez 2018, Leveraging the crowd to detect and reduce the spread of fake news and misinformation, WSDM](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.09918); [Curb code and Twitter/Weibo reshare data](https://github.com/Networks-Learning/curb); [Lykouris & Weng, Learning to defer in congested systems: the AI-human interplay (review-queue variant), arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.12237)
topics.baseline: Curb's optimal-control policy and the repo's flag-ratio and exposure heuristics
topics.angle: stochastic optimal control of SDEs with jumps as in Curb against a learned scheduler trained by policy gradient on simulated cascades; add a reviewer-capacity queue with deadlines

control.state: Story-exposure estimates, crowd flags, credibility beliefs and occupied reviewer capacity.
control.action: Choose which stories to review and when to submit them to available reviewers.
control.dynamics: Unreviewed cascades keep spreading; verification consumes reviewer time and changes later exposure.
control.objective: Reduce cumulative exposure to false stories within review-rate, staffing and latency constraints.

topics.title: Adaptive nonresponse follow-up in surveys
topics.problem: Each day of a survey field period, decide which nonresponding sample units get another interviewer visit or call, at what time and in which mode, or are retired, under uncertain contact and cooperation propensities, to maximize response representativeness (R-indicator) or minimize nonresponse bias subject to an interviewer-hours budget.
topics.hook: In the 2022 California Health Interview Survey, stopping low-propensity cases after three calls cut calls per sampled unit by about 14% while the completion rate fell about 0.3 points. Statistical agencies face this budgeted follow-up choice in every field period.
topics.start: [Calinescu & Schouten 2016, Adaptive survey designs for nonresponse and measurement error in multi-purpose surveys, Survey Research Methods](https://ojs.ub.uni-konstanz.de/srm/article/view/6157/6061); [Schouten, Calinescu, Luiten 2013, Optimizing quality of response through adaptive survey designs, Survey Methodology](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/12-001-x/2013001/article/11824-eng.htm); [Jackson, Hughes, Fu 2024, dynamic adaptive design for CATI nonresponse follow-up, JSSAM](https://academic.oup.com/jssam/article/12/3/712/7619574); [ESS contact-form call records, free after login, CC BY 4.0](https://data.norge.no/en/datasets/acd46276-1c00-3192-a97f-6ad4debe4f3b); [ESS contact form layout (per-attempt date, time, mode, outcome)](https://www.europeansocialsurvey.org/sites/default/files/2023-06/ESS9_source_contact_forms.pdf); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: fixed protocol with the same maximum number of visits for everyone, or a static design optimized by grid search
topics.angle: offline RL and off-policy evaluation of contact policies from call-record paradata; per-case optimal stopping under a cost budget

control.state: Contact histories, response-propensity beliefs, respondent composition and remaining follow-up budget.
control.action: Choose each next contact mode and timing, or stop contacting a sampled household.
control.dynamics: Attempts spend staff time and reveal response information, affecting later choices and final sample composition.
control.objective: Improve response and representativeness at low cost within staffing, contact and survey-deadline limits.

topics.title: Judicial time allocation to cut backlogs
topics.problem: Each week, decide how judges' hearing time is split between early-stage (admission) and later-stage cases and how hearings are booked in advance, under uncertain filings, adjournments and hearing lengths, to minimize mean time to disposition and pending caseload with a fixed number of judges and no case-level risk scoring.
topics.hook: Bakshi, Kim and Randhawa estimate that rebalancing judicial time between case stages at the Supreme Court of India could cut expected delay by up to 65% without adding judges. The open eCourts data covers over 80 million lower-court cases, with mean filing-to-decision times from 149 days to 5 years across districts.
topics.start: [Bakshi, Kim, Randhawa, Service operations for justice-on-time: a data-driven queueing approach, MSOM](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/fpi/10.1287/msom.2023.0530); [INFORMS summary with headline numbers](https://www.informs.org/News-Room/INFORMS-Releases/News-Releases/Court-Backlogs-Are-Clogging-the-System-New-Research-Finds-a-Surprising-Fix); [Development Data Lab India eCourts data 2010 to 2018 (filing, hearing, decision dates), CC BY-NC-SA](http://www.devdatalab.org/judicial-bias-data); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: current scheduling guidelines that favor fresh matters, with hearings fixed in advance
topics.angle: fluid or MDP model of a two-stage case queue with shared judges; MPC or a learned policy evaluated in a simulator calibrated to eCourts dates

control.state: Case queues by procedural stage and age, outstanding hearings and available judge time.
control.action: Allocate hearing capacity across stages and choose feasible bookings each review period.
control.dynamics: Completed hearings feed later procedural stages; adjournments and new cases alter future backlogs.
control.objective: Reduce cumulative waiting and case age while respecting judge capacity and procedural dependencies.

topics.title: Walleye fishery harvest rules
topics.problem: Harvest control rules for an age-structured, partially observed walleye fishery
topics.hook: Harvest rules decide whether a fishery survives. The population is age-structured and seen only through noisy surveys.
topics.start: [Montealegre-Mora et al. 2024, ML for harvest control rule design](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.12400); [rl4fisheries](https://github.com/boettiger-lab/rl4fisheries)
topics.baseline: Constant escapement and precautionary rules
topics.angle: belief-state MPC, or a parametric rule tuned on closed-loop performance, vs RL

control.state: Beliefs about age-structured abundance and recruitment from imperfect survey observations.
control.action: Choose annual harvest quotas or effort levels under the fishery model.
control.dynamics: Harvest removes fish that would survive and reproduce; uncertain recruitment changes future stock.
control.objective: Balance sustainable yield and rebuilding risk while respecting harvest and conservation constraints.

topics.title: Fishery near a tipping point
topics.problem: Fishery near an ecological tipping point: approximate model vs approximate solution
topics.hook: Is it better to solve a wrong model exactly, or the right model approximately? A clean experiment on this course's central question.
topics.start: [Montealegre-Mora et al. 2023, pretty darn good control](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.13654); [gym_fishing](https://github.com/boettiger-lab/gym_fishing)
topics.baseline: DP on a simplified model vs a learned policy on the full one vs learned dynamics + MPC
topics.angle: learn uncertain recruitment or a biomass belief model, then compare risk-aware DP or MPC with threshold harvest rules. Evaluate long-run yield, collapse frequency and recovery on unseen biological parameters and observation noise

control.state: Beliefs about biomass, recruitment parameters and ecological regime from catch and survey observations.
control.action: Set harvest effort at successive management periods.
control.dynamics: Nonlinear recruitment and harvesting can move the stock across a collapse threshold with slow recovery.
control.objective: Maximize long-run harvest value while limiting depletion risk under biological uncertainty and effort bounds.

topics.title: Wildfire firebreak placement and renewal
topics.problem: Choose annual firebreak placement and renewal under uncertain weather and ignitions, carrying landscape fuel and treatment condition across seasons to reduce long-run burned value under a fixed yearly budget.
topics.hook: A firebreak changes a landscape that will face more than one fire season. Spending this year on new protection leaves less for maintaining existing breaks, and fires change which areas need protection next.
topics.start: [Murray et al. 2024, DRL for firebreak placement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.08523); [Cell2Fire](https://github.com/cell2fire/Cell2Fire)
topics.baseline: Annual greedy or OR-based placement using the same treatment budget and current landscape
topics.angle: use Cell2Fire for within-season spread, add documented fuel-regrowth and treatment-deterioration transitions, and compare a learned planning surrogate or amortized multiseason policy with annual placement. Report cumulative burned value, cost and sensitivity to the added dynamics
topics.scope: The linked paper studies firebreak layout using a sequential construction agent. Multiseason regrowth, maintenance and landscape feedback are a proposed extension, not an existing feature to assume in the supplied simulator.

control.state: Landscape fuel and firebreak condition, past burns and remaining seasonal treatment budget.
control.action: Place or renew firebreaks at each annual planning update.
control.dynamics: Treatments persist and deteriorate; assumed fuel regrowth and simulated burns alter the landscape faced in later seasons.
control.objective: Reduce cumulative burned-value and treatment costs across seasons within annual treatment-area and access limits.

topics.title: Invasive species in a river network
topics.problem: Invasive species control in a river network (tamarisk)
topics.hook: Tamarisk spreads downstream along rivers. Small networks admit exact DP, so you can see exactly where approximation starts to hurt.
topics.start: [Alkaee Taleghan et al. 2015, PAC optimal MDP planning, JMLR](https://jmlr.org/papers/v16/taleghan15a.html); model in [Hall et al. 2012](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~crowley/papers/compsust2012.pdf)
topics.baseline: Exact value iteration on small networks, greedy heuristics
topics.angle: factored MDP with combinatorial actions and simulator-based planning beyond DP

control.state: Beliefs about infestation by reach, survey history and available management resources.
control.action: Allocate removal, survey or restoration effort each season.
control.dynamics: Local growth and downstream dispersal propagate infestation; removal changes later spread and survey value.
control.objective: Reduce long-run infestation and treatment cost within seasonal budgets and feasible reach access.

topics.title: Vaccine allocation
topics.problem: Age-structured vaccine allocation under limited supply
topics.hook: Who gets scarce doses first, and how should the plan change as case counts come in? Closed-loop allocation against open-loop plans.
topics.start: [Tonkens et al. 2021, vaccine allocation as optimal control](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.11908); [Covasim](https://github.com/institutefordiseasemodeling/covasim) ([Kerr et al. 2021](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009149))
topics.baseline: Oldest-first and the open-loop plan
topics.angle: MPC re-solved weekly from noisy case counts, robustness to model mismatch

control.state: Estimated epidemic compartments by group, vaccine stocks and delivery and administration capacity.
control.action: Allocate available doses among eligible groups each decision period.
control.dynamics: Vaccination reduces susceptible populations and uses stock; infections and deliveries change later priorities.
control.objective: Reduce modeled infections or deaths over the epidemic within stock, administration and eligibility constraints.

topics.title: Mosquito releases against dengue
topics.problem: Wolbachia mosquito release schedules for dengue suppression
topics.hook: Mosquitoes carrying Wolbachia stop dengue from spreading. The release schedules come from optimal control; feedback is the missing piece.
topics.start: [Almeida et al. 2019](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.02727); [Corum et al. 2026](https://www.arxiv.org/abs/2601.10967); seasonality from [OpenDengue](https://opendengue.org/)
topics.baseline: Open-loop optimal control from the papers
topics.angle: closed-loop MPC under stochastic releases and parameter uncertainty

control.state: Beliefs about wild and Wolbachia mosquito populations, observed prevalence and local conditions.
control.action: Choose release quantities, timing and locations across successive breeding cycles.
control.dynamics: Breeding and inheritance change future population composition and whether establishment thresholds are reached.
control.objective: Achieve persistent modeled establishment or disease reduction with low release cost within capacity constraints.

topics.title: Reservoir operation from US records
topics.problem: Multi-objective reservoir operation from historical records (hydropower, irrigation, flood)
topics.hook: Daily storage, inflow and release records for 679 US dams. Learn what operators do, then try to do better.
topics.start: [Wang et al. 2020, reservoir management with deep RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.03822); [Xu et al. 2021, ASCE](https://ore.exeter.ac.uk/repository/handle/10871/124834); [ResOpsUS](https://zenodo.org/records/5893641) records for 679 US dams; [pywr](https://github.com/pywr/pywr)
topics.baseline: Stochastic DP on a discretized inflow model and the historical operator policy
topics.angle: learned inflow model, scenario-tree MPC, operator imitation then offline improvement

control.state: Reservoir storage, season and beliefs about inflows and downstream demand.
control.action: Choose release at each management interval using current observations and forecasts.
control.dynamics: Water balance carries storage forward; releases trade present benefit against future scarcity and flood space.
control.objective: Balance hydropower, supply and flood objectives within storage, environmental-flow and release limits.

topics.title: Optimal order execution
topics.problem: Optimal order execution in a limit order book
topics.hook: Sell a large position without moving the price against you. Almgren-Chriss is an LQ problem from this course.
topics.start: [Nevmyvaka et al. 2006, ICML](https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~mkearns/papers/rlexec); [mbt_gym](https://github.com/JJJerome/mbt_gym) ([Jerome et al. 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.07823)); [ABIDES](https://github.com/jpmorganchase/abides-jpmc-public)
topics.baseline: Almgren-Chriss (an LQ problem) and TWAP/VWAP
topics.angle: learned impact dynamics + MPC, or train in mbt_gym and test on ABIDES

control.state: Remaining order inventory, time to deadline, order-book observations and estimated market-impact state.
control.action: Choose the size and timing of successive trade orders.
control.dynamics: Trades consume inventory and can change future prices or liquidity; waiting reduces remaining execution time.
control.objective: Complete the order with low slippage and inventory risk within deadline and participation constraints.

topics.title: Market making
topics.problem: Market making with inventory risk
topics.hook: Quote both sides, earn the spread, and don't get stuck holding inventory. The HJB solution gives you the baseline.
topics.start: [Ganesh et al. 2019, market making in a multi-agent dealer market](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.05892); mbt_gym and ABIDES
topics.baseline: Avellaneda-Stoikov quotes from the HJB equation
topics.angle: learned fill-probability dynamics, risk-sensitive objectives, misspecification

control.state: Inventory, market prices, order-book state and beliefs about order arrivals.
control.action: Set bid and ask quotes and permitted sizes at each quoting interval.
control.dynamics: Fills change inventory and future risk; market evolution changes which later quotes are profitable.
control.objective: Earn spread revenue while limiting inventory risk, position size and feasible quoting actions.

topics.title: Monetary policy as control
topics.problem: Monetary policy as control: setting the policy rate under uncertainty
topics.hook: Interest-rate changes affect inflation and activity with delays. This project compares feedback policies in an explicitly identified macroeconomic model under uncertain shocks and rate limits.
topics.start: [Wang 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17929); [Chen et al. 2021, Bank of England](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.09368); [FRED data](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/)
topics.baseline: Taylor rule and LQG on the same identified structural response model
topics.angle: estimate a stated structural response model from macroeconomic data, then compare constrained MPC with Taylor and LQG rules under common simulated shocks. Report cumulative inflation and activity loss and sensitivity to parameter drift
topics.scope: A forecasting VAR does not by itself identify the causal effect of changing the policy rate. Declare the identification assumptions and evaluate policy interventions only within the resulting model.

control.state: Estimated macroeconomic state, lagged policy rates and beliefs about structural shocks.
control.action: Choose the policy-rate path at successive modeled policy meetings.
control.dynamics: Structural response lags transmit current rates into later inflation and activity; predictive correlations alone do not identify this response.
control.objective: Minimize a stated inflation and activity loss while respecting rate and rate-change constraints in the chosen model.

topics.title: Airline revenue management
topics.problem: Airline seat inventory control and overbooking
topics.hook: Every seat is perishable inventory with a deadline. Exact DP on one flight, approximate DP on a network.
topics.start: [Shihab et al. 2019, autonomous airline revenue management](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.06824); [OR-Gym](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.06319)
topics.baseline: EMSR-b and exact single-leg DP
topics.angle: network revenue management with large action spaces via ADP or an amortized policy

control.state: Remaining seats, accepted bookings, time to departure and cancellation and demand beliefs.
control.action: Accept or reject fare-class requests and choose permitted booking limits.
control.dynamics: Accepted requests consume future capacity; cancellations and arrivals change later seat value.
control.objective: Maximize flight revenue net of denied-boarding cost within capacity and overbooking-risk constraints.

topics.title: Ride-hailing fleet rebalancing
topics.problem: Ride-hailing fleet rebalancing on NYC taxi demand
topics.hook: Empty cars cruising for riders cost money and emissions. Real NYC demand and a fluid model make it concrete.
topics.start: [Gammelli et al. 2021, GNN RL for mobility on demand](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.11434); [Feng et al. 2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.14679); [NYC TLC trip records](https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page); [AMoD simulator](https://github.com/DanieleGammelli/gnn-rl-for-amod) (CPLEX academic licence)
topics.baseline: MPC with a perfect forecast as upper bound, myopic matching
topics.angle: learned demand model + MPC, or a policy that sets the parameters of a downstream LP

control.state: Vehicle counts and trip-completion times by zone, with current requests and demand forecasts.
control.action: Assign requests and reposition idle vehicles each dispatch interval.
control.dynamics: Trips and repositioning occupy cars for travel time, changing later service capacity across zones.
control.objective: Increase served-demand value while reducing waiting and empty travel within fleet and routing constraints.

topics.title: Solar and battery market bidding
topics.problem: Solar plus battery bidding in energy and reserve markets
topics.hook: Batteries next to solar farms earn from energy and reserve markets at once. Real Australian market data, real price spikes.
topics.start: [Li et al. 2024, storage bidding in energy and reserve markets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.19110); [Li et al. 2024, solar-storage in real-time markets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.15853); [AEMO NEM data](https://aemo.com.au/energy-systems/electricity/national-electricity-market-nem/data-nem/aggregated-data)
topics.baseline: Rolling-horizon MILP with a price forecast, SDP
topics.angle: joint energy and reserve co-optimization with learned price dynamics
topics.venture: Owners of solar and battery plants, whose revenue depends on how they bid into energy and reserve markets.

control.state: Battery charge, solar forecasts, outstanding market commitments and price uncertainty.
control.action: Submit energy or reserve bids and set battery charging or discharge on a rolling horizon.
control.dynamics: Market awards create future obligations; storage use changes energy available to honor later commitments.
control.objective: Maximize risk-adjusted market revenue while satisfying charge, power and reserve-delivery constraints.

topics.title: Data-centre cooling
topics.problem: Data-centre cooling and carbon-aware workload shifting
topics.hook: Google showed that a learned linear model plus MPC can cool a real data centre. Add carbon-aware workload shifting.
topics.start: [Lazic et al. 2018, data center cooling using MPC, NeurIPS](https://research.google/pubs/data-center-cooling-using-model-predictive-control/); [SustainDC benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.07841) and [dc-rl](https://github.com/HewlettPackard/dc-rl)
topics.baseline: Fixed setpoints, then linear MPC with a learned model as in Lazic
topics.angle: learn a thermal and workload-response model for MPC or optimize a feedback policy on the same simulator. Retain temperature and task queues between decisions, and compare energy or carbon, deadline misses and temperature violations on unseen workloads
topics.venture: Data-centre operators, which pay for lower cooling energy and lower carbon per workload.

control.state: Server and cooling-system temperatures, queued workload and available cooling capacity.
control.action: Choose cooling setpoints and permitted workload shifts at each operating interval.
control.dynamics: Heat accumulates and tasks progress or wait, so current cooling and scheduling affect later temperatures and latency.
control.objective: Reduce energy or carbon cost while satisfying temperature, task-deadline and cooling-capacity constraints.

topics.title: LLM inference scheduling
topics.problem: LLM inference scheduling and batching under latency SLOs
topics.hook: Every chatbot answer goes through a scheduler that batches requests under latency targets. Queueing control at the heart of AI's energy bill.
topics.start: [Sarathi-Serve, Agrawal et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02310); [Fu et al. 2024, scheduling by learning to rank](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.15792); [Vidur simulator](https://github.com/microsoft/vidur); [Azure LLM traces](https://github.com/Azure/AzurePublicDataset), [BurstGPT](https://github.com/hpmll/burstgpt)
topics.baseline: FCFS and fixed chunking
topics.angle: queueing MDP with a learned output-length model, tail latency as a chance constraint
topics.venture: Companies serving language models, who pay for more requests per GPU within their latency targets.

control.state: Request queues, prefill and decode progress, KV-cache occupancy and output-length beliefs.
control.action: Choose batching, chunking and request priority at successive GPU scheduling opportunities.
control.dynamics: GPU service advances some requests and holds memory until completion, affecting later queueing and admission.
control.objective: Increase useful throughput per energy while meeting latency targets and GPU-memory constraints.

topics.title: GPU power control
topics.problem: GPU frequency and power-cap control for energy-efficient serving or training
topics.hook: Lowering a GPU's clock or power cap often costs little speed and saves a lot of energy. Find the sweet spot as the load changes.
topics.start: [DynamoLLM, Stojkovic et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.00741); [Zeus, You et al. 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.06102); [Perseus, Chung et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.06902); [Zeus library](https://github.com/ml-energy/zeus)
topics.baseline: Max frequency and a static per-job optimum
topics.angle: identify power, service-rate and thermal responses, then compare load-forecast MPC or a recurrent policy with static caps and a myopic bandit. Carry temperature and unfinished work between steps; measure workload energy, throughput and latency on unseen arrival traces
topics.venture: Companies running GPU clusters, who pay for lower energy per token or per training step at the same speed.
topics.scope: Needs a GPU with controllable power limits, or an explicitly calibrated simulator. Frequency-to-power curves alone are static; include workload progress or queue dynamics and thermal response in the final policy comparison.

control.state: GPU temperature, active-job progress and queued work, with current utilization observations.
control.action: Set power caps or supported clock settings at each control interval.
control.dynamics: Heat and unfinished work persist; aggressive throttling now creates later backlog and thermal changes.
control.objective: Reduce energy per completed workload while maintaining throughput, latency and thermal limits over time.

topics.title: Internet congestion control
topics.problem: Internet congestion control
topics.hook: Every TCP connection runs a controller on its sending rate. A learned controller must cope with links it has never seen.
topics.start: [Aurora, Jay et al. 2019, ICML](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.03259); [PCC-RL](https://github.com/PCCproject/PCC-RL); [ns3-gym](https://github.com/tkn-tub/ns3-gym)
topics.baseline: CUBIC, BBR, PCC-Vivace
topics.angle: learned link model + MPC on the sending rate; generalization to unseen links

control.state: ACK, RTT and loss history, with beliefs about bottleneck queues and available capacity.
control.action: Choose packet sending rate or congestion-window updates at each feedback step.
control.dynamics: Sent packets join queues and influence later delay and loss observed after network feedback latency.
control.objective: Maximize useful throughput while limiting delay, loss and unfair bandwidth use under changing capacity.

topics.title: Database tuning
topics.problem: Choose database configuration changes over a drifting workload, accounting for reconfiguration downtime, cache warmup and queued queries to improve cumulative performance subject to latency constraints.
topics.hook: Databases have hundreds of knobs and workloads that drift. Treat tuning as control over time, not a one-shot search.
topics.start: [QTune, Li et al. 2019, PVLDB](https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol12/p2118-li.pdf); [Bao, Marcus et al. 2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.03814); [Park](https://github.com/park-project/park) environments
topics.baseline: Defaults and static Bayesian optimization; a myopic query-steering bandit is an additional baseline
topics.angle: learn a model of workload, queue and configuration-transition effects, then plan configuration changes or train a feedback policy across workload episodes. Compare cumulative throughput, tail latency and tuning overhead, including cold-cache and workload-shift cases
topics.scope: Choose knobs whose changes can be applied and timed in the selected database. Instrument warmup and reconfiguration, or declare a calibrated transition simulator; independent query-plan choices without persistent effects are a contextual-bandit baseline.

control.state: Current configuration, workload beliefs, cache-warmup state, queues and recent latency measurements.
control.action: Choose supported configuration changes and their timing across workload intervals.
control.dynamics: Reconfiguration consumes time; caches warm and queues persist, so settings affect later performance as well as immediate throughput.
control.objective: Improve cumulative workload throughput within latency and resource limits, accounting for reconfiguration and warmup costs.

topics.title: Cluster job scheduling
topics.problem: DAG job scheduling on a Spark-like cluster
topics.hook: Decima learned to schedule Spark jobs with a graph policy. Real Google cluster traces let you test it under realistic load.
topics.start: [Decima, Mao et al. 2019, SIGCOMM](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.01963); [decima-sim](https://github.com/hongzimao/decima-sim); [Google 2019 cluster trace](https://github.com/google/cluster-data/blob/master/ClusterData2019.md)
topics.baseline: FIFO, fair, shortest-job-first, critical path
topics.angle: planning with a learned stage-duration model over structured actions

control.state: Ready and running DAG tasks, executor availability, dependency progress and resource occupancy.
control.action: Assign tasks and executors whenever scheduling resources become available.
control.dynamics: Tasks occupy resources; completion unlocks successors and changes capacity for later jobs.
control.objective: Reduce job completion time or stated fairness cost within dependency, CPU and memory constraints.

topics.title: Autoscaling inference servers
topics.problem: Kubernetes autoscaling for inference pods with cold starts
topics.hook: A new GPU server takes time to start, so the autoscaler must act before the burst arrives. Delayed actions on real traces.
topics.start: [KIS-S, Zhang et al. 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.07932); [Azure Functions traces](https://github.com/Azure/AzurePublicDataset)
topics.baseline: Threshold autoscaler and M/M/c sizing
topics.angle: learned arrival and latency dynamics, MPC with a forecast; cold start makes it a delayed-action problem
topics.venture: Companies serving models in the cloud, who pay for fewer idle GPUs without missing latency targets.

control.state: Request backlog, active and warming replicas and forecasts of incoming demand.
control.action: Start or stop replicas at successive autoscaling decisions.
control.dynamics: Cold starts delay usable capacity; stopping replicas reduces future service and can force later expensive restarts.
control.objective: Minimize serving cost while meeting tail-latency and capacity targets under start-up and minimum-run constraints.

topics.title: Compressed-air compressor sequencing
topics.problem: Every few seconds, choose which fixed-speed compressors to load and the output of a variable-speed compressor, using receiver pressure, machine modes and a demand forecast, to minimize electricity and switching costs while maintaining delivery pressure and minimum on/off times.
topics.hook: A receiver tank stores enough air to shift compressor operation through short demand bursts. The controller must trade electricity against pressure dips and excessive starts.
topics.start: [Bezold et al. 2025, RL control of industrial compressed-air systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.18317), including the receiver mass balance, machine modes and industrial-controller comparison. Equipment parameters are confidential: build a reduced benchmark with documented compressor curves and label its parameters separately from the paper's plant.
topics.baseline: Pressure-band lead-lag sequencing, then mixed-integer MPC on the same reduced model
topics.angle: learn short-horizon demand and compressor power-to-flow maps, then amortize MPC decisions. Report kWh per delivered air volume, pressure violations and starts per hour on held-out demand profiles; do not treat the paper's reported savings as reproduced on a different plant
topics.venture: Factories and compressor service firms could buy a retrofit supervisory sequencer. The value is lower metered kWh per delivered air volume at the same pressure service; commissioning must establish savings against the site's existing sequencer.

control.state: Receiver pressure, compressor modes, switching timers and estimated compressed-air demand.
control.action: Choose compressor load, unload or speed settings as demand changes.
control.dynamics: Receiver mass balance carries pressure forward; compressor commitments restrict future switching and capacity.
control.objective: Meet pressure requirements with minimum electricity and switching wear within compressor and timing limits.

topics.title: Water-network pressure and leakage control
topics.problem: Adjust pressure-reducing-valve setpoints through the day from pressure and flow measurements, inferred demand and tank levels, to reduce pressure-dependent leakage while meeting minimum service pressures, storage requirements and limits on valve movement.
topics.hook: A valve can reduce leakage by lowering excess pressure, but the highest or most distant customer still needs enough water. Demand uncertainty makes a fixed nighttime pressure setting a useful baseline.
topics.start: [Smart pressure management extension for EPANET, Journal of Hydroinformatics 2022](https://doi.org/10.2166/hydro.2022.172), with [public code and examples](https://zenodo.org/records/6243078); [Negm et al. 2023, pressure optimization with Q-learning](https://eprints.lancs.ac.uk/id/eprint/212501/4/Negm_Ahmed_IEEE_CAI_Submission_word.pdf). The extension uses an EPANET 3 development version, so reproduce its example before changing engines.
topics.baseline: Fixed-outlet and time-modulated valve control from the pressure-management paper
topics.angle: learn a demand model and plan valve setpoints over several hours. Keep tank storage or actuator limits in the formulation so decisions have consequences beyond a single hydraulic solve; test unseen demand peaks and misspecified leak coefficients
topics.venture: Water utilities and valve suppliers could buy supervisory pressure control for an existing metered district. Measure cubic metres of leakage avoided and service-pressure violations; use the hydraulic model for the project and inlet-flow measurements for a future field trial.

control.state: Network pressures, tank levels, previous valve positions and uncertain demand.
control.action: Adjust pressure-reducing valves at successive control intervals.
control.dynamics: Tank storage and limited valve motion couple pressure choices across time; static hydraulics alone omit that coupling.
control.objective: Reduce leakage and operating effort while maintaining service pressure and feasible tank and valve conditions.

topics.title: Aquaculture aeration under oxygen limits
topics.problem: Choose an aerator operating schedule from dissolved oxygen, fish biomass, feeding and expected renewable generation, to minimize electricity cost while keeping oxygen above a species-specific limit despite uncertain oxygen consumption.
topics.section: Food security and the future of food
topics.hook: Aerators can shift electricity use, but dissolved oxygen limits how long they can stay off. Feeding changes oxygen demand, so a forecast error has a direct biological cost.
topics.start: [Nakadomari et al. 2026, renewable-integrated aquaculture under dissolved-oxygen constraints](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.seta.2026.105029), with an experimentally calibrated oxygen model and economic MPC; [dos Santos et al. 2022, water-quality control in a recirculating aquaculture system](https://folk.ntnu.no/skoge/prost/proceedings/dycops-2022/files/0080.pdf). Rebuild the reduced oxygen model; these references are not a packaged simulator or a promised release of farm logs.
topics.baseline: Continuous aeration and an oxygen-threshold rule, then the paper's economic MPC on the reconstructed model
topics.angle: learn oxygen-consumption residuals after feeding and train forecasts for aeration decisions. Start with one tank and aeration alone; compare energy cost, minimum oxygen and duration below the limit across temperature and biomass changes
topics.venture: Land-based fish farms and aquaculture equipment integrators could buy an aeration supervisor. The value is lower electricity per production cycle while meeting oxygen limits; an initial product could recommend schedules through the farm's existing control system.

control.state: Dissolved oxygen, estimated biomass and oxygen demand, with water and feeding conditions.
control.action: Schedule aeration power across successive feeding and electricity-price periods.
control.dynamics: Respiration depletes oxygen while aeration replenishes it; stored oxygen provides limited flexibility for later intervals.
control.objective: Minimize aeration electricity while keeping dissolved oxygen above the stated welfare threshold within equipment limits.

topics.title: Wafer polishing under pad wear
topics.problem: After each measured wafer lot, adjust polishing pressure and rotation settings for the next lot, using removal rate, nonuniformity and process history, to keep oxide removal on target as the pad wears and metrology arrives with delay, within recipe bounds.
topics.hook: The same polishing recipe removes a different amount of material as its pad ages. Measurements arrive after processing, so the next recipe must compensate for a tool that has already changed.
topics.start: [Boning et al. 1996, Run by Run Control of Chemical-Mechanical Polishing, open paper](https://www.telf.com/~roland/Publications/1996-cpmt.pdf), with response-surface models and tool experiments; [DRL-tuned double-EWMA control, 2023](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cherd.2023.07.049). Rebuild the published response model and introduce explicitly specified wear and delay scenarios; this does not require access to a fab's private logs.
topics.baseline: Fixed recipe and the exponentially weighted moving-average run-to-run controller from Boning et al.
topics.angle: estimate drifting process coefficients online and use constrained MPC, or learn how to tune the existing controller. Compare tracking, within-wafer nonuniformity and recovery after pad replacement on wear trajectories excluded from fitting
topics.venture: Polishing-tool suppliers and fabs could buy recipe-adaptation software. Measure out-of-spec wafers, monitor-wafer consumption and recovery lots after a pad change; shadow recommendations provide a possible first integration, while production qualification remains substantial work.

control.state: Measured removal and uniformity, estimated pad wear and past polishing recipes.
control.action: Choose the pressure, rotation and other modeled recipe settings for each next wafer.
control.dynamics: Pad wear drifts across runs; delayed wafer metrology updates the response model for subsequent recipes.
control.objective: Maintain removal and uniformity targets with low recipe variability within process-setting bounds.

topics.title: Rapid thermal wafer processing
topics.problem: Set lamp-zone powers during a wafer's temperature ramp and hold, using a reduced thermal state estimated from sparse temperature measurements, to track the recipe while limiting spatial nonuniformity, peak temperature and actuator power under uncertain emissivity.
topics.hook: A wafer must heat quickly and evenly even as its radiative properties change. A controller that tracks the average temperature can still leave the wafer edge outside the recipe tolerance.
topics.start: [Schaper et al. 1992, Dynamics and Control of a Rapid Thermal Multiprocessor, model and open paper](https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/thermal_multiprocessor.html); [Model-Based Control of Rapid Thermal Processing for Semiconductor Wafers, ACC 2004](https://skoge.folk.ntnu.no/prost/proceedings/acc04/Papers/0704_FrA01.2.pdf). Rebuild a small thermal model from the papers; commercial controller software and production traces are not supplied.
topics.baseline: Nominal feedforward lamp recipe with feedback correction, following the published controller
topics.angle: identify emissivity or thermal-model residuals from simulated calibration runs, then use MPC and amortize it. Compare ramp error, maximum spatial temperature spread and solve time under held-out emissivity and sensor-bias conditions
topics.venture: Thermal-processing equipment suppliers could buy a controller or recipe-transfer module for their tools. Measure recipe qualification runs and time within temperature-uniformity tolerance; electrical savings alone do not establish wafer-yield improvement.

control.state: Estimated wafer temperature profile, sparse sensor readings and uncertain emissivity.
control.action: Set lamp-zone powers at each thermal-processing control interval.
control.dynamics: Radiative heating and conduction accumulate and redistribute heat, constraining later ramps and uniformity.
control.objective: Track the required temperature trajectory while limiting nonuniformity, peak temperature and lamp power.

topics.title: Adaptive video streaming with delivery costs
topics.problem: Select the next video chunk's bitrate from buffer occupancy, recent download rates, chunk sizes and the previous quality level, to trade picture quality against stalls, quality changes and delivered bytes under uncertain bandwidth.
topics.hook: Higher bitrate spends both bandwidth and the player's buffer. Real network traces let you test whether a learned forecast improves the viewing experience enough to justify its delivery cost.
topics.start: [Mao, Netravali and Alizadeh 2017, Pensieve, paper and project](https://web.mit.edu/pensieve/); [authors' simulator, network traces and MPC baselines](https://github.com/hongzimao/pensieve). The original training stack uses TensorFlow 1: port the small trace-driven simulator and baselines before attempting to reproduce training.
topics.baseline: Buffer-based adaptation and robust MPC; offline DP with future bandwidth revealed is a benchmark, not an online controller
topics.angle: learn bandwidth forecasts for MPC or optimize a policy directly. Sweep the delivered-byte penalty as an added project objective and compare stall time, quality switches and bytes on network families excluded from training
topics.venture: Video platforms and streaming infrastructure vendors could buy a player-side adaptation module. Demonstrate fewer bytes at matched quality and stall targets; customer-retention gains would need a separate user experiment.

control.state: Playback-buffer level, previous video quality and throughput beliefs from recent downloads.
control.action: Choose the bitrate of the next video chunk.
control.dynamics: Downloading takes uncertain time; playback drains the buffer and chosen quality affects later switching cost.
control.objective: Maximize cumulative viewing quality while limiting stalls, quality changes and data use over the video.

topics.title: Battery-free sensor duty cycling
topics.problem: Choose each sensor node's sleep interval from capacitor voltage, recent light and sensing history, to collect useful measurements without exhausting stored energy through nights and weekends under uncertain indoor energy harvesting.
topics.hook: A sensor can use today's light to take more measurements, or save that energy for a dark weekend. The published ACES deployment makes the tradeoff measurable without buying hardware for the project.
topics.start: [Fraternali et al., ACES, preprint 2019 and TOSN 2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.01968); [authors' simulator, sample light traces and Q-learning controller](https://github.com/francescofraternali/ACES). Adapt the legacy research scripts and verify their capacitor-energy accounting before extending the controller.
topics.baseline: Fixed sleep intervals and the ACES tabular Q-learning controller
topics.angle: learn light-arrival dynamics and compare finite-horizon DP or MPC against Q-learning under a common energy budget. Hold out rooms or lighting schedules and report dead time, sampling intervals and event capture separately
topics.venture: Building-automation and sensor-platform vendors could buy energy-management firmware for harvesting nodes. Measure sensing coverage at a fixed storage capacity and time spent offline; avoided battery-service visits are a potential customer benefit to validate.

control.state: Capacitor voltage or stored energy, recent harvested power and sensing history.
control.action: Choose the next sleep duration and sensing or transmission opportunity.
control.dynamics: Sleeping harvests energy; sensing and transmission spend it, changing future availability and measurement freshness.
control.objective: Collect useful fresh samples while avoiding energy depletion within storage and device timing constraints.

topics.title: Cellular base-station sleep control
topics.problem: Choose active, sleep and wake-up decisions from the traffic queue, recent arrivals and the current radio mode, to minimize energy while limiting request delay and switching frequency, accounting for the time and energy required to wake the base station.
topics.hook: A quiet cell can sleep, but the next burst waits while the radio wakes up. Prediction is useful only if the energy saved survives that delay and wake-up cost.
topics.start: [Liu et al. 2018, DeepNap, IEEE Internet of Things Journal](https://doi.org/10.1109/JIOT.2018.2846694); [authors' implementation and experimental resources](https://github.com/zaxliu/deepnap). Rebuild the queueing and sleep model in a current environment: the original code targets an old CUDA/Python stack and downloads data externally, so check data access before committing to a trace-reproduction study.
topics.baseline: Always on and a queue-threshold sleep rule; exact DP on a small discretized queue provides a model-based comparison
topics.angle: fit an arrival model and plan sleep decisions with DP or MPC. Start with one cell; test forecast errors, unexpected bursts and wake-up delays, reporting energy together with delay percentiles and dropped requests
topics.venture: Mobile operators and radio-access-network vendors could buy a cell-level energy supervisor. Measure kWh per carried traffic volume at matched delay and loss targets; integration with existing radio management and fallback rules would be part of a commercial pilot.

control.state: Traffic queues, active or sleeping hardware modes and wake-transition timers.
control.action: Choose sleep depth and wake-up timing as traffic estimates change.
control.dynamics: Backlogs grow while service is unavailable; wake delays and mode transitions affect later energy and latency.
control.objective: Minimize base-station energy while meeting modeled delay and loss requirements within hardware-transition constraints.

topics.title: Adaptive tutoring with a hidden learner state
topics.problem: After each response, choose an example, a quiz or a question with feedback, using a belief over the learner's current understanding, to minimize expected time to mastery when learning and response errors are stochastic and each activity has a different duration.
topics.hook: A quiz can reveal a misconception that changes which example the tutor should show next. The controller must decide when information about the learner is worth the time spent obtaining it.
topics.start: [Rafferty, Brunskill, Griffiths and Shafto 2016, Faster Teaching via POMDP Planning, Cognitive Science](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/cogs.12290). Rebuild one of the published concept-learning tasks using its learner models, activity costs and supplementary parameters; the paper includes simulations and human experiments.
topics.baseline: The paper's random activity policy, quiz-example policy and one-step maximum-information policy
topics.angle: learn response-error or learner-transition parameters in simulation, then compare belief-state lookahead with a policy amortized from the planner. Measure time to mastery across learner models and model mismatch; improvements on simulated learners require separate evidence before claiming classroom benefits

control.state: A belief about learner knowledge and misconceptions from response history and response times.
control.action: Choose the next example, question or feedback action within a teaching session.
control.dynamics: Instruction changes latent knowledge while responses update beliefs, affecting which later intervention is useful.
control.objective: Reach specified mastery with few interactions while respecting session time and appropriate task difficulty.

topics.title: Accessible paratransit pickup-window assignment
topics.problem: As next-day paratransit bookings arrive, confirm a narrow pickup window within each rider's requested interval, using the current bookings and feasible fleet routes, to reduce vehicle hours while honoring pickup commitments, capacity and ride-time constraints under uncertain later demand.
topics.hook: A convenient pickup window promised now can make later bookings expensive to serve. This is door-to-door public transport for riders who face barriers to using standard transit, with actual agency requests and a published booking simulator.
topics.start: [Sivagnanam et al. 2022, Offline Vehicle Routing Problem with Online Bookings, IJCAI](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2022/546); [authors' simulator, baselines and 180 days of Chattanooga agency requests](https://github.com/smarttransit-ai/ijcai22). Start with a few days: the legacy environment needs adaptation and full travel-matrix preprocessing is expensive.
topics.baseline: Deterministic greedy booking and simulated-annealing routing from the repository, with a common routing-time budget
