topics.angle: learn the future cost of committing to a pickup window from historical booking days, or amortize lookahead decisions. Split by day and compare vehicle hours, passenger ride times and pickup feasibility on unseen days

control.state: Accepted trips, promised pickup windows, route schedules and remaining vehicle capacity.
control.action: Assign a feasible pickup window to each new booking and update permitted route commitments.
control.dynamics: Promised windows restrict future route insertions; trips consume vehicle time and capacity before later requests arrive.
control.objective: Serve requests with low vehicle-hours while honoring pickup, ride-time and capacity requirements.

topics.title: EEG speller optimal stopping
topics.problem: After each completed stimulus group in a P300 EEG speller, either collect more observations or select a character, using the posterior over intended characters, to minimize spelling time and the cost of selection errors under noisy, user-dependent EEG responses.
topics.hook: A communication aid can wait for clearer brain signals or commit to a letter sooner. The decision trades time against errors, and can be studied by stopping early within recorded stimulus sequences.
topics.start: [Mainsah et al. 2015, dynamic stopping in a P300 speller, including an ALS study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4631027/); [Akimpech public EEG recordings and readers](https://itzamna.izt.uam.mx/p300db/). Akimpech contains healthy participants; evaluate that population explicitly when using those recordings.
topics.baseline: A fixed number of stimulus groups and the published posterior-confidence stopping rule
topics.angle: learn calibrated target/non-target observation models and solve an optimal-stopping problem with an explicit error-correction cost. Hold out complete characters or users, preserve the recorded stimulus order, and report selection accuracy and corrected characters per minute

control.state: Posterior character probabilities from EEG evidence, stimulus history and elapsed selection time.
control.action: Collect the next stimulus group in the recorded order, or stop and output a character.
control.dynamics: Each stimulus updates beliefs and costs time; stopping ends the current character-selection episode.
control.objective: Minimize selection time and character-error cost while preserving the stated confidence or accuracy requirement.

topics.title: Shelter and permanent-housing capacity planning
topics.problem: At each budget review, choose additions to shelter and permanent housing, and conversions between them, using current occupancy, waiting populations and committed construction, to reduce cumulative unsheltered person-days over several years under funding and construction lead-time constraints.
topics.hook: Shelter places remain occupied while residents wait for permanent housing, so adding beds alone may leave the bottleneck in place. A county-calibrated queueing simulation makes the timing of investment a sequential decision.
topics.start: [Singham, Lucky and Reinauer 2023, Discrete-event simulation modeling for housing of homeless populations, PLOS ONE](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0284336), calibrated to Alameda County with public simulation resources linked in the paper. Add explicit budget and construction-delay dynamics to the aggregate model; individual eligibility decisions are outside this project.
topics.baseline: The paper's fixed multi-year shelter and housing investment plan under the same total budget
topics.angle: learn arrival and return-rate models from simulated observations, then adapt capacity investment with MPC or approximate DP. Compare cumulative unsheltered person-days, waiting times and cost under unseen arrival surges and funding delays; state which conclusions depend on the simulation's housing pathways

control.state: Shelter and housing occupancy, waiting queues, funded projects and construction lead times.
control.action: Choose investments, conversions and feasible capacity allocations at successive planning reviews.
control.dynamics: Construction adds capacity after delays; placements and exits change later queues and available beds.
control.objective: Reduce cumulative unsheltered days and spending within capital, operating-budget and construction constraints.

topics.title: Lead service-line inspection and replacement
topics.problem: Each planning period, allocate a limited budget between inspecting uncertain service lines and replacing identified hazardous lines, updating beliefs from excavation results, to remove hazardous connections efficiently while maintaining a specified level of inspection coverage across neighborhoods.
topics.hook: The pipe material is buried underground, so an inspection buys information as well as locating a possible hazard. A high-risk-first policy can miss the value of inspecting an uncertain part of the network.
topics.start: [Abernethy et al. 2018, ActiveRemediation: The Search for Lead Pipes in Flint, Michigan](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.10692), including inspection/replacement rules, cost models and field and simulated evaluations. Check access to parcel-level inspection labels before proposing a data-reproduction study; a documented reconstruction of the paper's simulation is a separate option.
topics.baseline: Uniform inspection and greedy inspection of the highest predicted hazard probabilities, as in ActiveRemediation
topics.angle: learn a spatial material model and plan several inspection batches ahead, or train predictions for remediation cost. Compare hazardous lines replaced per budget, unnecessary excavations and neighborhood inspection coverage; keep pipe-material detection separate from a model of residents' exposure

control.state: Beliefs about pipe materials, inspection results, completed replacements and remaining annual funds.
control.action: Select the next inspection and replacement batches.
control.dynamics: Inspections reveal labels that improve later targeting; replacements remove hazards and consume future work capacity.
control.objective: Replace hazardous lines efficiently while meeting budget, crew-capacity and neighborhood-coverage requirements.

topics.title: Worker heat-exposure management
topics.problem: Choose work intensity, rest periods and cooling actions over a shift, using an estimated thermal state and weather forecasts, to balance completed work with modeled heat strain under physiological and task-completion constraints, with uncertainty in clothing, metabolic heat and environmental conditions.
topics.hook: Body heat accumulated early in a shift changes which work and rest choices remain feasible later. An explicit thermoregulation model connects a schedule to predicted core and skin temperatures.
topics.start: [JOS-3 thermoregulation model, authors' Python code and paper](https://github.com/TanabeLab/JOS-3); [pythermalcomfort model documentation](https://pythermalcomfort.readthedocs.io/en/stable/documentation/models.html). Begin with one virtual worker and piecewise-constant work and rest conditions, using published model validation cases to check the simulator.
topics.baseline: Fixed work-rest cycles and a thermal-state threshold rule with the same modeled task and exposure limits
topics.angle: learn a reduced thermal model for MPC, then amortize its schedule decisions. Evaluate predicted heat exposure, completed work and constraint violations under held-out weather and physiological parameters; the project evaluates scheduling in a physiological simulator

control.state: Estimated body thermal state, recent work and rest, task progress and weather.
control.action: Choose work-rest intervals and available cooling interventions during the shift.
control.dynamics: Work adds body heat and advances tasks; rest and cooling reduce heat with delayed recovery.
control.objective: Complete useful work while limiting modeled heat strain under task, rest and cooling-resource constraints.

topics.title: Classroom ventilation and clean-air control
topics.problem: Set outdoor-air flow and filtration levels from estimated occupancy, indoor CO2 and particle measurements, to reduce modeled aerosol exposure and energy use while maintaining comfort under changing occupancy and outdoor pollution.
topics.hook: Opening the outdoor-air supply clears occupant-generated CO2 but can bring in outdoor particles. Ventilation and filtration provide different control inputs, and the best combination changes as rooms fill and empty.
topics.start: [Risbeck et al. 2023, Data-driven control of airborne infection risk and energy use in buildings, open paper](https://web.mit.edu/bazant/www/papers/pdf/Risbeck_2023_BuildingEnv_Data-driven_control_infection_risk_energy_use.pdf); [MIT indoor-air, occupancy and HVAC data](https://github.com/acoh64/MIT-JCI-IAQ-HVAC). The data include measured and imputed signals; use the documented raw/clean distinction when fitting the room model.
topics.baseline: Fixed ventilation and CO2-threshold demand-controlled ventilation, with a common comfort requirement
topics.angle: identify room mass-balance dynamics, learn occupancy forecasts and plan ventilation/filtration with MPC. Compare modeled exposure, energy and comfort on held-out days; add outdoor-pollution disturbances explicitly, and treat infection-risk reductions as model predictions

control.state: CO2 and particle concentrations, room temperature and occupancy estimates.
control.action: Set ventilation and filtration operation at successive occupied-room control intervals.
control.dynamics: Contaminants accumulate or are removed; ventilation also changes thermal load and later comfort.
control.objective: Reduce cumulative exposure and energy use within comfort, noise and equipment-capacity limits.

topics.title: Maternal-health outreach scheduling
topics.problem: Each week, allocate a limited number of live service calls among participants in a maternal-health messaging program, using observed listening histories and uncertain engagement transitions, to maintain engagement over the program while respecting call capacity and a chosen service-coverage constraint.
topics.hook: A participant's engagement can decline even in weeks when no one calls. Scarce staff time must be allocated over an evolving population, which makes this a restless-bandit problem with a shared intervention budget.
topics.start: [Mate et al. 2022, Field Study in Deploying Restless Multi-Armed Bandits: Assisting Non-profits in Improving Maternal and Child Health, AAAI](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/21460). Rebuild the scheduling formulation with documented transition matrices; access to the ARMMAN beneficiary records requires separate verification or an agreement.
topics.baseline: Round-robin service calls, greedy engagement-based calling and the paper's restless-bandit allocation method
topics.angle: learn engagement-transition models and compare finite-horizon allocation or a learned policy under a common call budget. Use exact DP for a small cohort and simulation for scale; report retained engagement and coverage under transition uncertainty, with health outcomes requiring separate evidence

control.state: Beliefs about participant engagement from listening and call history, with remaining weekly call capacity.
control.action: Choose which participants receive outreach calls each week.
control.dynamics: Engagement changes between contacts; calls may alter future participation and reveal who needs later support.
control.objective: Improve sustained engagement under a fixed call budget and stated service-coverage constraints.

topics.title: Urban stormwater and sewer-overflow control
topics.problem: Adjust detention-basin outlet openings every few minutes from water levels, recent inflows and a rainfall forecast, to limit downstream flooding and pollutant discharge while respecting storage, outlet and receiving-channel constraints during uncertain storms.
topics.hook: An upstream basin can hold back runoff until a downstream bottleneck clears. Coordinating existing outlets can change which neighborhoods or waterways receive the peak flow without building another storage tank.
topics.start: [Rimer et al. 2023, pystorms: A simulation sandbox for stormwater control algorithms](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.12289); [pystorms scenarios, simulator interface and examples](https://github.com/kLabUM/pystorms). Start with one supplied scenario and its stated flow or water-quality objective before extending the network.
topics.baseline: Uncontrolled outlets and a water-level rule using the same scenario-specific performance metric
topics.angle: learn an inflow or reduced storage model and run MPC, or optimize a feedback policy in the hydraulic simulator. Hold out complete storms and compare overflow volume, peak discharge and pollutant load where the selected scenario models water quality

control.state: Basin levels, pipe flows and estimated pollutant loads, with rainfall forecasts.
control.action: Set controllable outlet openings as a storm develops.
control.dynamics: Storage fills and drains with routing delays; present release consumes downstream capacity needed by later inflows.
control.objective: Reduce flooding and pollutant discharge while respecting basin levels, outlet and downstream-capacity constraints.

topics.title: Wildlife-conservation patrol planning
topics.problem: Plan each ranger patrol from the current location, terrain, remaining patrol time and observations of illegal activity, to improve coverage and expected threat detection while updating a spatial risk model under imperfect detection and observations biased by previous patrol effort.
topics.hook: A patrol history shows where rangers looked as well as where threats occurred. A planner that treats unvisited areas as safe can repeatedly miss the same places.
topics.start: [Xu et al. 2020, Stay Ahead of Poachers: Prediction and Patrol Planning Under Uncertainty with Field Test Evaluations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.06669); [PAWS public risk-modeling and patrol-planning code](https://github.com/lily-x/PAWS-public). The code expects park observations and geographic inputs: secure access or document a reconstructed landscape and observation process before committing to a reproduction.
topics.baseline: Uniform patrol coverage and greedy patrols using the same fitted risk map and travel budget
topics.angle: learn a detection-aware risk model and plan repeated patrols with lookahead or a decision-focused objective. Compare detection, spatial coverage and robustness to biased historical effort on a declared threat simulator; field detections and wildlife-population outcomes are different evaluation targets

control.state: Ranger positions, past search effort, detected signs and beliefs about spatial threat intensity.
control.action: Choose repeated patrol routes and next areas to visit.
control.dynamics: Travel spends patrol time; new detections update spatial risk beliefs and change the information available for later patrols.
control.objective: Improve modeled protection and detection within ranger, travel-time and coverage constraints, accounting for search bias.
